title: Opus: validate the header in Decoder::from_head (#425)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #425.

`Decoder::from_head` is public and takes an `OpusHead` whose fields are all public, but it trusted them. `Decoder::new` goes through `OpusHead::parse`, which checks the stream counts and the mapping table; a hand-built header skipped those checks. With zero streams, concealment indexed `streams[0]`; with a mapping shorter than `channels`, or a mapping or coupled-stream count out of range, `decode` indexed `mapping[c]` or `scratch[s]` out of bounds. A `Result`-returning API could panic.

`OpusHead::validate` now checks the invariants the decoder indexes by: at least one channel, `1 <= streams`, `coupled_streams <= streams`, `streams + coupled_streams <= 255`, `mapping.len() == channels`, and every mapping entry either 255 (silence) or below `streams + coupled_streams`. These are the same checks and `InvalidHeader` messages that `OpusHead::parse` / `from_dops` already apply, plus the mapping-length check that the parser gets for free from slicing. `from_head` calls it first, so `Decoder::new` and `Decoder::simple` are unchanged (their headers already pass).

Tests in `multistream.rs`:
- `from_head_rejects_inconsistent_headers`: zero streams, short mapping, out-of-range mapping index, more coupled streams than streams, and zero channels all return an error. It fails on main (zero streams is accepted).
- `from_head_accepts_valid_headers`: mono, stereo, a 3-channel multistream layout and a silent (255) mapping entry still build a decoder.

title: xtask: assets audit no longer panics on Unicode names and reads real paths from git (#424)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #424.

Both problems from the issue are in `xtask/src/assets.rs`.

**1. Wildcard matching panicked on multibyte names.** `glob()` checked `rest[..i].contains('/')` for every byte offset `i` before it checked `is_char_boundary(i)`. A `*` that crossed a character such as `ż` or `日` sliced in the middle of it and panicked. The wildcard now steps only over char boundaries (`char_indices()` plus the end of the string). The rules stay the same: `*` matches any run of characters except `/`.

**2. Git-quoted paths disappeared from the audit.** `git ls-files` without `-z` quotes paths that contain non-ASCII or special characters (with the default `core.quotePath`), for example `"assets/\305\274.png"`. Those strings never `exists()` on disk, so the file was dropped from the check and a missing attribution went unreported. The audit now runs `git ls-files ... -z` and splits the output on NUL. The names come back unquoted whatever `core.quotePath` is set to, and names with spaces or newlines stay whole.

Tests (in `xtask/src/assets.rs`):
- `glob_handles_multibyte_names`: wildcards through Polish and CJK names, `*` still stops at `/`, an attributed Unicode asset passes, and an unattributed one (`assets/é.png`) is reported. On `main` the first assertion panics with "byte index 1 is not a char boundary".
- `ls_files_output_is_nul_separated_and_unquoted`: NUL-separated output with a Unicode name and a name that contains a space and a newline parses to the exact file names.

title: CLI: render-transition refuses --t values that would share one file name (#423)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #423.

When `render-transition` is given several `--t` values, each frame is written to `<stem>-t<value>.png`, with the value rounded to three decimals. Two different values that round to the same name, such as `0.1001,0.1002`, or the same value given twice, wrote to the same file. Only the last frame was kept, but the command still printed one output line for each frame.

The output paths are now built before anything is rendered or written, by a small `frame_paths` helper. If two of them are the same, the command returns an error that names the file, and nothing is written. This is the "detect/reject collisions before any output writes" option from the issue. The file names stay the same, so scripts that read `-t0.250.png` etc. keep working. A single `--t` still writes to OUT unchanged.

Tests (`apps/deckcraft-cli/src/main.rs`):
- `single_frame_uses_out_as_is`: one value writes to OUT.
- `frames_get_distinct_names`: ordinary separated values get the existing `-tN.NNN.png` names.
- `values_rounding_to_one_name_are_rejected`: `0.1001,0.1002` and `0.5,0.5` give an error. Without the fix, there was no check, so both pairs went to one file.

title: Info: keep a property draft when another field or the side menu is clicked (#422)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #422.

The Info page lost a property edit unless it was finished with Enter. I checked the two paths the issue describes against `main`:

- **Clicking another field (e.g. edit Author, then click Title).** Title is drawn first and takes the focus when it is clicked. When Author was drawn next, its draft had already been reset to the saved value, because the field no longer had the focus. `lost_focus` then saw nothing to commit. Now the commit check runs after the `TextEdit` is drawn, and the reset to the saved value runs only when the field has no focus and has nothing to commit.
- **Clicking a side-menu entry (Save, Home, Save As, Close, ...).** The side menu is drawn before the page, so `Save` ran `app.save()` before the field could commit. The file was written without the new value and the presentation was left dirty. Each side-menu click now commits the Info page's drafts first (`commit_props`, which runs only while Info is shown), and then runs the action.

Esc is unchanged: it still leaves the File tab before the page is drawn, and the edit is dropped. Enter still commits as before.

Tests (kittest, real pointer input):
- `info_keeps_a_property_draft_when_another_field_is_clicked`: type an Author, click Title, and check that the author is set.
- `info_saves_a_property_draft_when_save_is_clicked`: on a presentation that has a file, type an Author and click Save. The author is set and the presentation is not dirty, so the value went into the saved file.

Both tests fail on `main`. The existing Enter test (`info_shows_and_edits_the_properties`) still covers the Enter path.

title: Engine: moving the selection to another text body settles the composition (#421)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #421.

`Session::select` changed the selection without touching an active IME composition. The composition only stores an offset and a length, so after selecting another text body, the next `compose_text`/`commit_text` replaced characters at that offset in the *new* body, while the old body kept its preedit.

`Session::select` now records the text owner (slide, target, shape, table cell, notes) before running the callback and, if a composition is active and the owner changed, settles it with `end_composition()`. This is the same thing `execute` (journalled commands), `key` and pointer presses already do, so the old body keeps its composed text as one "Type Text" undo step and the new body is left untouched. Moving the caret inside the same body leaves the composition alone, as before.

Tests (`tests_keys.rs`), both failing on `main`:
- `select_into_another_body_settles_the_composition`: compose in text box A, select text box B, commit: B gets only the committed text, A keeps its composed text.
- `select_into_another_table_cell_settles_the_composition`: the same between two cells of one table.

title: Honeycomb transition: cover the bottom of the slide with new-slide cells (#420)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #420.

`honeycomb` placed row centres every `rh * 0.866` but counted rows as if they were `rh * 1.5` apart. On a 16:9 slide that gave 11 rows, so the last new-slide cells stopped at about y = 0.75 and the bottom quarter stayed black until the frame at t = 1 snapped to the full new slide.

The row count now uses the same spacing as the placement: `(1 / (rh * 0.866)).ceil() + 2`. The hex vertical radius is `0.577 * rh`, so a row spacing of `0.866 * rh` (1.5 radii) is the correct pointy-top lattice, and the last row now sits below y = 1 for every aspect. Columns already cover the full width (`0..=cols` with half-column offset), so they are unchanged.

Test: `honeycomb_new_cells_reach_the_bottom_of_the_slide` checks that at t = 0.99 the new-slide cells reach y >= 1 for 16:9 and 4:3. It fails on main (bottom about 0.75) and passes with the fix.

title: Format scientific number formats (0.00E+00) in chart labels (#419)
author: MarekSpodBiedry

title: Media: drain stale video frames before sending a seek, not after (#416)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #416.

`VideoFeed::seek` sent `Cmd::Seek` to the decode worker and only then drained the frame channel. A worker that answered fast (for example one parked at the end of the stream, waiting for a command) could publish the first frame of the new position, or its EOF, while that drain was still running. Those messages were thrown away, so the feed skipped the frame it had seeked to, or waited for an EOF that never came while the worker waited for its next command.

The fix moves the drain in front of the send. Before the send, everything in the channel belongs to an older generation, so dropping it is safe. If the worker refills the channel with stale frames between the drain and the send, `pull` already skips them by generation. The drain still unblocks a worker waiting to hand over a stale frame. Only the native worker path changes: the wasm path decodes inline and has no channel.

Test: `feed::tests::seek_keeps_the_frames_and_end_sent_for_it` builds a `VideoFeed` around a fake worker. The frame channel holds a long backlog of stale frames, and the worker answers the seek with a frame and EOF of the new generation. With the old order, the drain is still busy when the worker answers, so it eats both and `frame_at` returns `None`. With the fix, the feed gets the frame and then reaches the end.

title: UI: notes, alt text and rename drafts no longer carry over to another document (#413)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #413.

Three text drafts were cached by slide index or shape id alone, so they could show up in, and be written to, the wrong place:

- **Notes Page** (`sorter.rs`): the box kept its text under `("notespage", slide_index)` and committed it on focus loss. The same index in another document, a slide reorder or an undo of the notes brought back the old text. The draft is now keyed by document uid and slide index, and it remembers the notes it started from. When the stored notes change underneath it (other document, reorder, undo), the stored notes are shown again instead of the stale draft.
- **Selection pane rename** (`selpane.rs`): `State` kept `renaming` under a bare shape id, so a pending rename could be committed to a shape with the same id in another document. `State` now records which document (uid) it belongs to. `show` calls `State::bind(uid)` first, and on a document switch the rename, folds, anchor and drag are reset.
- **Format Shape > Alt Text** (`panes.rs`): this field had the same problem. Its draft was keyed by shape id only and never cleared. It now uses the same document-uid key and the same resync as the Notes Page.

The resync logic is one small helper, `widgets::text_draft`, used by both text fields.

Tests:
- `selpane::tests::switching_document_drops_a_pending_rename`: the same document keeps the draft, another document drops it (and the folds).
- `widgets::tests::text_draft_keeps_typing_while_the_stored_text_is_unchanged` / `text_draft_drops_a_stale_draft_when_the_stored_text_changes`.

The Outline pane drafts were already safe because they are cleared as soon as the field loses focus, so I left them as they are.

title: Pptx: keep the math namespace equations inherit from the slide root or a wrapper (#412)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #412.

Equation import stored the OMML children of `a14:m` with `El::to_xml()`, which drops namespace declarations inherited from above. When a file declares `xmlns:m` on the slide root or on a wrapper (e.g. `mc:Choice`, whose declarations `resolve_mc` moves onto the `p:sp`), the stored fragment had an unbound `m:` prefix, and export wrote it out that way.

Changes:
- The math branch of `read::dml::paragraph` now serializes through `Part::keep_inner`, the namespace-preserving path already used for other raw fragments (`Part::keep`), extended with prefixes declared below the root.
- `Part` now also records `inner_ns`: prefixes declared on inner elements but not on the root. A prefix bound to two different namespaces in one part is skipped, so nothing gets a wrong binding. `Part::keep` and its other callers are unchanged.
- Equations that declare `xmlns:m` themselves (what DeckCraft and PowerPoint write) are unaffected: `keep_xml` never re-adds a declaration the element already has.

Tests: `crates/pptx/tests/math_ns.rs` exports an equation, moves its `xmlns:m` onto `<p:sld>` (first test) or `<mc:Choice>` (second test), imports again and checks that the stored OMML declares the namespace. Both tests fail on `main`. The existing `roundtrip.rs` math test covers the case where the equation declares the namespace itself.

title: PPTX: a paragraph's own default run properties (pPr/defRPr) reach its runs (#411)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #411.

`dml::paragraph` called `ppr` but threw away its third value, the paragraph's `a:pPr/a:defRPr`. Runs, breaks and fields were read from their own `a:rPr` only. So a paragraph that set size, bold, colour and so on in `defRPr`, with runs that did not repeat them, lost that formatting on import.

The fix keeps the `defRPr` result. After the paragraph is read, it merges those properties into every text run, break and field, and into the end-of-paragraph mark (`endParaRPr`), with `RunProps::inherit`. `inherit` only fills fields that are still `None`, so the order the issue asks for holds: direct `rPr` beats the paragraph default, and the paragraph default beats the list and master styles, which only fill what is still unset. Inline math runs are skipped, because they never carry run properties on import. `list_style` already used the same third value of `ppr` for `lvlNpPr/defRPr`.

Round trip: the model has no paragraph-level default field, so the merged values are written back as each run's own `rPr`. The text looks the same, and nothing is lost.

Test: `paragraph_default_run_props_reach_runs` (crates/pptx/src/read/dml.rs). It reads a paragraph with `defRPr sz="3000" b="1"`, one run with no `rPr`, one run that sets only `sz="1200"`, and a break. It checks that the plain run gets 30 pt bold, the partial run keeps 12 pt and still gets bold, the break gets 30 pt, and the end mark gets 30 pt. It fails on main, where those values are `None`.

title: MCP: do not resend a command whose reply was lost (#409)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #409.

`Remote::call` (`crates/mcp/src/backend.rs`) reconnected and resent the request after any I/O error, also when the request had already reached the app and only the reply was lost. An insert/delete/undo could then run twice while the client saw one successful call.

The request is now split into `send` and `receive`:

- **Send fails** (the app never got the line): reconnect and send once more, as before.
- **Send succeeds but the reply is lost**: no replay. The call returns an error saying the command may or may not have run. The connection is dropped, so the next call opens a fresh one.
- **The app restarted between calls**: before writing on a kept connection, a non-blocking `peek` checks whether the app has already closed it. If it has, a new connection is opened first. Without this check, the first call after a restart would write into the dead socket and report "outcome unknown" for a request that never arrived. Today's retry handles that case, so this keeps it working.

This follows the issue's second suggestion: report outcome-unknown, do not replay. It needs no change to the control protocol or the app. Idempotency keys would need the server to store replies, so I left them out. All methods use the same rule. A separate retry policy for read-only methods would need a list of which methods are safe to replay, and that is a maintainer decision.

Tests (fake server in `backend.rs`):
- `lost_reply_is_not_resent`: the server runs the first request and drops the connection without a reply. The call returns the outcome-unknown error, the request ran exactly once, and the next call works on a fresh connection. On `main` the request runs twice.
- `connection_closed_before_the_call_is_retried`: the server closes the first connection before any request, like an app restart. The call is sent on a new connection, succeeds, and runs once.

title: Engine: a command that fails after editing puts the presentation back (#405)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #405.

`Session::execute_unguarded` returned through `r?` when a command failed, so a command made of several edits could fail after some of them had already gone through. Those changes stayed in the document with no undo step and no journal entry.

The fix: when the outermost command returns an error and the presentation changed during it, the engine puts back the presentation and selection it started with and bumps the revision so views redraw. This does for an ordinary error what the panic guard in `guard.rs` already does for a panic. Nested commands are unchanged, so undo grouping still works the same way: only the outermost command restores, and only on error.

All three cases from the issue go through this one path:
- `picture.change` with a target that does not exist: the image it stored is removed again.
- `shape.connect` with a non-line `preset`: the shape it inserted is removed again.
- SmartArt that inserts its shapes and then fails in `arrange.group`: the inserted shapes are removed again.

Tests (in `guard.rs`, next to the panic-guard test). Both fail without the fix:
- `a_command_that_fails_after_editing_leaves_the_document_alone`: `shape.connect` with `preset: "rect"` fails, and afterwards the document is the same one as before and the undo stack has not grown.
- `a_failed_picture_change_adds_no_media`: `picture.change` with an unknown id fails, and the document is the same one as before.

title: Table: split and cell fill stay inside the table (#400)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #400.

The issue names two loops that use sizes they never check against the table:

- **`Table::split`** walked `row_span x grid_span` cells starting at the split cell and only checked inside the loop whether each cell existed. A cell with spans far past the table edge (from a file or a model edit) made it run through billions of missing cells. The loop now stops at the last real row and column. It uses `saturating_add`, so `r + span` cannot overflow on 32-bit targets either.
- **`table.cellFill`** with no `cells` param turned the whole selection rectangle into a `Vec` before checking any cell. `table.selectCells` accepts any endpoints, so a selection that reached far past the table could allocate without limit. The rectangle is now clamped to the table's last row and column before the list is built. A selection that lies fully outside the table gives an empty range.

Nothing changes for selections and spans that stay inside the table. `table.merge` already rejects rectangles outside the table, so I left it as it is. The pptx reader already clamps spans it reads to 1..=1000.

Tests:
- `model::table::tests::split_ignores_spans_past_the_table`: a 2x2 table whose top-left cell has `u32::MAX` spans splits at once and is reset to 1x1.
- `engine::tests::cell_fill_walks_only_the_cells_a_huge_selection_covers`: selects from (1,1) to (1e9, 1e9) on a 2x2 table and runs `table.cellFill`. Only cell (1,1) gets the fill.

Without the fix, both tests run out of time or memory and never finish.

title: Bitstream: reject bad NAL length widths, check NAL endpoints and signed Exp-Golomb limits (#397)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #397.

Both points of the audit are handled in `crates/bitstream`, the crate that the H.264 and HEVC decoders share:

**1. `length_prefixed_nals`**
- A `length_size` outside `1..=4` now returns a new `BitError::InvalidLengthSize` instead of looping forever on width 0. `1..=4` is the full range that the 2-bit `lengthSizeMinusOne` in avcC/hvcC can express, so every stream that decoded before still decodes, including one with a 3-byte prefix.
- The bounds checks are now `length_size > data.len() - i` and `len > data.len() - i`, so they can't overflow `usize` on 32-bit/WASM targets when a 4-byte length is huge. A bad length still returns `BitError::Eof`, as it did before.

**2. Signed Exp-Golomb**
- `read_se` works out the value in `i64` and returns `BitError::InvalidExpGolomb` if it doesn't fit in an `i32`. That value is +2^31, from the `ue` code `u32::MAX`, which used to wrap to `i32::MIN`. This is the same error `read_ue` returns for codes that are too long.
- `write_se` works in `i64`/`u64`, so `i32::MIN` no longer overflows. It writes the 33-bit code for 2^32, which `read_se` rejects. The doc comment says so.

`h264`, `hevc` and `vp9` convert `BitError` through `#[from]`, so the new variant needs no other changes.

**Tests** (`crates/bitstream`)
- `signed_exp_golomb_extremes`: `i32::MAX` and `i32::MIN + 1` round-trip; `i32::MIN` and the `ue` code `u32::MAX` both return `InvalidExpGolomb`. Without the fix, `write_se(i32::MIN)` panics in debug builds and `read_se` returns `i32::MIN`.
- `length_prefixed_rejects_bad_width_and_oversized_length`: widths 5 and 0 are rejected, a 3-byte prefix still splits, and an oversized 4-byte length returns `Eof`. Without the fix, width 5 returns `Eof` instead of `InvalidLengthSize`.

title: Matroska: stop following chapter and tag nesting past 32 levels (#396)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #396.

`parse_chapter` and `parse_simple_tag` in `crates/matroska/src/meta.rs` called themselves for every nested `ChapterAtom` / `SimpleTag` with no depth limit, so a small file with deeply nested metadata could overflow the stack.

Both now take a depth argument. Children at 32 levels or deeper are skipped, the same way unknown elements are skipped. The file still opens, and the shallower part of the tree is kept. The limit of 32 is the same as `MAX_TREE_DEPTH` for the PPTX shape tree in `crates/pptx/src/read/shapes.rs`. Because the parsed tree is never deeper than 32 levels, dropping it is also bounded, which covers the cleanup point in the issue.

Tests (in `meta.rs`): a chain of exactly 32 nested chapters and of 32 nested SimpleTags parses in full. A chain of 82 is cut to 32. Without the fix, the 82-level case keeps all 82 levels.

Changed only `crates/matroska/src/meta.rs`.

title: AV1: reject tile groups that repeat, skip or reorder tiles (#395)
author: MarekSpodBiedry

title: Slide: leading tabs in a new slide's body set the outline level (#370)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #370.

`add_slide` (MCP) runs `slide.new`, and its description says "body: one paragraph per line, leading tabs indent". But `slide.new` put the body in with a plain `TextBody::from_text`, so a leading tab stayed in the text as a literal character and the paragraph stayed at level 1.

`text.set` already turns leading tabs into the outline level (capped at 8) and strips them. This PR moves that code into a small helper, `apply_leading_tabs` in `cmd/text.rs`, and calls it from both `text.set` and `slide.new`, so the two commands now handle the body text the same way. `text.set` behaves exactly as before: tabs still win over the levels it keeps from the old paragraphs.

Test: `new_slide_body_leading_tabs_become_levels` creates a slide with the body `"Level one\n\tLevel two\n\t\tLevel three\nLevel one again"` and checks for levels 0, 1, 2, 0 with no tab left in the text. Without the fix it fails, because the second paragraph is `"\tLevel two"` at level 0.

title: Slide show: Honeycomb's hexagons cover the whole slide again (#420)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #420.

**What was wrong.** The Honeycomb row count came from `1/(1.5*rh)` — the row spacing alone — and ignored how far a settled hexagon reaches. On a 16:9 slide the eleven rows stopped at ~75% of the height: from t≈0.9, when every cell has settled, the bottom quarter was plain black until the t=1 endpoint snapped to the full new slide.

**The fix** (two lines in `crates/anim/src/transition_fx.rs`): the count now derives from the real geometry — rows sit `0.866*rh` apart and a settled hexagon's **flat bottom zone** reaches `0.289*rh` past its centre, so counting to the flat-zone reach covers the slide bottom for every aspect ratio. 16:9 gains four rows (15, was 11); 4:3 gains seven (20, was 13). Rendering cost stays inside the existing layer budget.

**Review caught the subtle half:** counting to the *vertex* reach (my first cut, `−2/3` in the formula) still left small V-notches of black above the bottom edge on about a third of aspect ratios (US Letter, square, …) — where the last row's flat zone ends above y=1 there is no next row to fill the taper between hexagons. The landed formula counts to the flat zone; the new test's aspect list includes the failing sizes (US Letter `11/8.5`, square).

**Tests:** at t=0.99 — every cell settled, seams ~0.012% open — a 0.02-step grid over the unit slide must sit inside settled incoming cells (padded 1% past the hairline seams) on five aspect ratios (16:9, 3:2, 4:3, US Letter, square). Fails on the old count at (0.2, 0.74); passes with the fix. Verified visually with `deckcraft-cli render-transition … --t 0.95`: the black band is gone and the lattice closes to the bottom edge. ROADMAP progress-log row added.

title: feat(ui): smooth fade and slide transitions when switching ribbon tabs (#461)
author: Osaym
body:
Closes #461

### Summary
When switching between ribbon tabs (e.g., Home, Insert, Draw, Design, Transitions, Animations, Slide Show, Review, View, etc.), the switch previously produced an abrupt cut. In Microsoft PowerPoint and modern office presentation suites, switching ribbon tabs features smooth and responsive transitions.

This pull request implements smooth fade and slide transitions when navigating between ribbon tabs, matching PowerPoint's motion and feel.

### Key Changes
1. **Active Tab Indicator Glide**:
   - The accent-colored indicator bar underneath the active tab button glides smoothly between tabs across the tab strip (interpolating position and width over 160ms) using egui's `animate_value_with_time`.
2. **Directional Content Slide & Fade**:
   - When switching tabs, the ribbon panel content smoothly fades in (opacity 0.2 -> 1.0) with a subtle directional slide (16 pt -> 0 pt) using a cubic ease-out curve.
   - Moving forward (e.g., Home -> Insert) slides in from the right; moving backward (e.g., Insert -> Home) slides in from the left.
3. **Accessibility & Test Support**:
   - Strictly respects `ui.style().animation_time`. When animations are turned off in settings or in headless test harnesses, switches complete instantaneously with 0 delay.
4. **Quality & Standards**:
   - 100% safe Rust (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` preserved).
   - Zero panics (`clippy::unwrap_used`, `clippy::expect_used`).
   - Added unit test `ribbon_tab_switch_animation` verifying directional transitions.
   - Verified with `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test`.

title: Copy and Cut buttons and menus put the text on the system clipboard (#431)
author: Zetenypapp
body:
Fixes #431, at least the part I could reproduce on Windows 11.

**Upfront:** this is my second contribution, and like the first (#349) it was written by Claude (Claude Code, Opus 5.5). I tested it myself in the app.

## The bug

Ctrl+C and Ctrl+X work. But the ribbon's **Copy** and **Cut** buttons, the slide's **right-click Copy/Cut**, the menus and the command palette never put anything on the system clipboard, so whatever you copy with them can't be pasted into another program. To reproduce:

1. In Notepad, copy `hello`.
2. In DeckCraft, select some slide text and click the ribbon's Copy button.
3. Paste in Notepad. You get `hello`, not the slide text.

## Why

Ctrl+C runs `edit.copy` and hands the returned text to `ctx.copy_text`. Everything else runs the same command through `SlideApp::run`, which dropped the text.

## The fix

`SlideApp::run` keeps the text of a successful `edit.copy` / `edit.cut` and hands it to the clipboard on the next frame, the same way `pending_urls` works. So every button, menu, the palette and the control channel behave like the keyboard. It's one small change in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`, plus a line in the `ROADMAP.md` progress log.

## Testing

- **New test:** `copy_and_cut_commands_reach_the_system_clipboard` runs Copy and Cut through `SlideApp::run` and checks the frame's `CopyText` output. It fails without the fix.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes locally on Windows 11 (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm).
- **Manually in the release build:** the clipboard went from `hello` to the slide text after the command path's Copy.
- It merges cleanly with #189 (pasting objects without text).

**Not covered:** the report also says Ctrl+C/V don't work at all for the reporter. On Windows 11 those work for me, so that part may be specific to their system (no OS or version was given).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Model: format scientific number codes (0.00E+00) instead of folding the exponent into fixed-point digits (fixes #419)
author: saadkhantareen
body:
Fixes #419.

## Summary

`numfmt::format` treated every digit placeholder in a format section as one fixed-point field, so for a scientific format such as `0.00E+00` the exponent placeholders were folded into the fractional digits and the `E`/`+` were dropped: the value 1234 formatted as `1234.0000` instead of `1.23E+03`. Chart axis and data labels using scientific codes silently lost their notation. Scientific codes are now parsed and formatted explicitly.

## Changes

- `crates/model/src/numfmt.rs` (+126/−0): detect scientific codes and format them with the mantissa normalised to [1, 10), honouring mantissa precision, minimum integer/fraction digits and the locale decimal mark; `E+` always shows the exponent sign, `E-` only for negative exponents; the exponent is zero-padded to its `0` placeholders; rounding that pushes the mantissa to 10 renormalises (9999 → `1.00E+04`). Unsupported shapes fall through to the existing fixed-point path.
- Same file: new unit test `scientific_codes` covering the reported example, zero, negative exponents, the `E-` rule, exponent-width padding, renormalisation and a locale decimal mark.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p deckcraft-model numfmt` — 4 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test -p deckcraft-model --lib` — 43 passed, 0 failed
- `rustfmt --check` on the changed file — clean

title: H.264: bound frame_num gap work and reject gaps the SPS forbids (#427)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Closes #427.

**What was wrong.** `Dpb::fill_frame_num_gap` (`crates/h264/src/dpb.rs`) inserted one "non-existing" frame per missing `frame_num`, and the decoder callback allocated and copied a full picture for each one. With `log2_max_frame_num = 16`, one small slice could set off ~65 535 full-frame allocations and copies. `gaps_in_frame_num_value_allowed_flag` was parsed but this path never checked it.

**Fix.**
- **Forbidden gaps are rejected.** If the active SPS has `gaps_in_frame_num_allowed = 0`, `start_picture` now returns an error for a picture with a `frame_num` gap, so it no longer fills the gap (7.4.2.1.1 / 8.2.5.2).
- **Allowed gaps cost bounded work.** The sliding window keeps at most `max_num_ref_frames` short-term references (≤ 16). When the gap is longer than that, inserting the whole gap would push out every earlier short-term reference and every non-existing frame except the last `max_num_ref_frames`. So the earlier short-term references are now marked unused up front, and only the tail of the gap is built as frames. The POC state (`update_gap_frame`) still walks every missing `frame_num` in order, so `FrameNumOffset` wraparound comes out the same. Long-term references are left alone, as before.

**Tests.**
- `dpb.rs` unit tests: a 65 533-frame gap builds only 4 frames, walks the POC state over every missing number, and leaves exactly the last 4 non-existing frames as references. Also covered: a gap that wraps around `MaxFrameNum`, a short gap that keeps earlier references, and a huge gap with a long-term reference.
- `synth_tests.rs`: tiny CAVLC streams with a `frame_num` gap. When the SPS forbids gaps, the error is reported and the gap is not filled. When it allows them, the gap is filled and both pictures are output.
- The existing `pcm_long_term_mmco_gaps_*` bit-exact tests still pass.

`cargo xtask ci` is green: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, tests, assets, layers, wasm.

title: Media: a failed or stalled audio output hands the clock back to wall time (#417)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
- `AudioOut` gains a defaulted `failure()` that the player polls each `tick`; the cpal output reports a `DeviceNotAvailable` stream error through it right away, not only when the stream stops.
- `Player::tick` also notices a stream that stops calling back: no callback for more than a second while a voice plays counts as stalled. An idle (paused) stream doesn't count.
- In either case the stream stops and the voices continue on the wall clock (silent) instead of freezing. The next `play` tries the device again, and after 3 failures the player gives up on the device and stays silent.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p deckcraft-media --lib player`: new tests for a failed output (wall-clock fallback, restart on play), a stalled output, an idle stream that is not a stall, and repeated failures giving up on the device
- [x] `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm)

Closes #417

title: Media: scope playback to its document and keep media identities stable (#415)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
- Playback (voices, videos, GIF clocks) now belongs to one document (`DocState::uid`). Switching to another deck or closing the last one stops all of it, slide-show voices included, so a shape with the same id in the new deck never inherits old media.
- `Player::play` gives a voice the new audio and restarts it from its start when the voice's media changes (a clip was replaced), instead of keeping the old audio. `MediaHost` also drops that shape's old video feed.
- Pointer-keyed caches keep their source bytes: the decoded-audio cache and the probed-duration cache hold the `Arc` they are keyed by, so the address can't be reused while the entry lives. A key that names other bytes is decoded again. The duration cache is bounded to 16 entries.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p deckcraft-ui-egui --lib media::tests`: two decks with the same shape id, same-document no-op, last-document close; the duration cache holds its bytes and stays bounded

title: Control server: bound connections, line length, queue and socket timeouts (#418)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
- At most 16 control connections at once; extra clients get a `busy` error line and are closed. The slot comes back when the client thread ends, however it ends.
- Request lines are read with a 16 MiB cap, so a huge line with no newline can't eat memory. A longer line gets an error and the connection is closed.
- The request queue is bounded (64); when it's full the request is answered `busy` straight away instead of piling up.
- Sockets get a read deadline (closed after 10 min idle) and a write deadline (30 s), so idle or stalled clients don't hold threads forever. The 60 s UI reply timeout stays the same.
- `docs/control-protocol.md` documents the limits. No unwrap/panic in non-test code.

## Test plan
- [x] New `control_server` tests with small limits: round trip, oversized line, idle timeout on an unterminated line, connection limit refuses and then frees the slot, blocked UI times out while the full queue answers busy
- [x] `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm)

Closes #418

title: Anim: group animations by sequence in one pass (#410)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
- `Timeline::with` groups a slide's animations by sequence in a single pass (a `HashMap` index into an ordered list). Sequence order stays first appearance, main first. Before, each trigger was found with `Vec::contains` and then all animations were rescanned for every sequence.
- The build stops at `MAX_EFFECTS` before starting the next sequence, so nothing past the cap is grouped or filtered again.
- Paragraph-group dedup (`ByParagraph` text builds) uses a `HashSet` instead of `Vec::contains` on the growing group list.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p deckcraft-anim --lib`: new tests for interleaved triggers keeping first-appearance order and step counts, and 110,000 distinct triggers (past the cap) building exactly 100,000 effects in order. The old code needed about 1.2e10 steps for that; the whole suite now runs in 0.11 s
- [x] `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm)

Closes #410

title: Table: inserting and deleting rows and columns keeps merges consistent (#408)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
- `insert_row`/`insert_col`/`delete_row`/`delete_col` now account for merged cells. They read the merged areas first, shift or resize each one, and rebuild every cell's spans and merge flags, so no cell is left covered with no anchor and no span overlaps or runs past the grid.
- A row or column inserted inside a merge widens it, and its new cells are covered. One inserted before a merge shifts the merge along.
- Deleting a row or column inside a merge narrows the merge, and a merge that shrinks to one cell is dropped.
- Deleting the anchor row or column moves the anchor's contents (text, fill, borders) to the next cell the merge covers, so the merged text is kept.
- No unwrap/panic in non-test code.

## Test plan
- [x] New model tests check, for a 2×2 merge, that every insert/delete position before, inside, at and after the merge leaves each cell owned by exactly one anchor
- [x] Tests for a merge growing when a row or column is inserted inside it, and for the text staying when the anchor row or column is deleted
- [x] `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm)

Closes #408

title: Web: a picked file lands where it was requested (#414)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Closes #414.

## Summary
- `Services::open_async` now takes a **ticket** with each request, and every `Inbox` entry is an `InboxFile { name, bytes, ticket }` (`ticket: None` for a dropped file).
- When a web pick starts, `SlideApp` stores what the ticket is for: the command (`file.openBytes`, `insert.picture`, `insert.audio`, `insert.video`) and, for inserts, the **document uid and slide id** that were current.
- When the file arrives, that command runs on **that** document and slide, even if the user has moved to another slide or presentation in the meantime. Afterwards the user is put back on the slide or presentation they were viewing.
- If the presentation has been closed or the slide deleted by then, nothing is inserted and the status bar says why. A ticket that is answered twice, or that was never issued, does nothing.
- The requested operation is kept. A `.txt` picked from Insert ▸ Picture is no longer turned into outline slides by guessing from the content.
- Dropped files work as before.

## Test plan
- [x] `crates/ui-egui/src/picker_tests.rs`:
  - The user changes slide while the file loads: the file lands on the slide the request came from, and the view stays where the user is.
  - The user switches to another presentation while the file loads: the file lands in the presentation it was requested from.
  - Two answers arriving in reverse order each reach their own slide.
  - The target slide was deleted, or the presentation was closed (and another opened): the insert is cancelled.
  - A mismatched file type, a repeated ticket and an unknown ticket do nothing.
- [x] `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, test, assets, layers, wasm all pass.
- [x] `cargo clippy -p deckcraft-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -- -D warnings`
- [ ] Manual check in the browser build (not run: no browser session for the web app here)

title: Edit: copies remap media, connector ends, animation targets and triggers (#406)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
- `reid` returns the old-to-new shape-id map. A connector end on a shape that was copied too follows its copy. An end on a shape outside the copied set is detached (the geometry stays), so a copy no longer stays glued to the original or to a same-id shape in another deck.
- New `remap_animations` for slide paste and `slide.duplicate`: animation targets and triggers point at the copies. An animation whose target wasn't copied is dropped, and a trigger that wasn't copied is cleared. Before, slide paste kept the old ids, and duplicate remapped targets by position but not triggers.
- `bring_media` returns the ids it had to change when a media id clashes with different bytes. Pasted shapes are rewritten to use those ids (pictures, media and posters, picture fills, opaque previews, a pasted slide's picture background). Copying a slide now also carries its picture-background media.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib copy_remap`, new tests:
  - [x] two decks with colliding media ids and different bytes: the pasted picture shows the copied bytes, and the destination's own picture is unchanged
  - [x] connected shapes duplicated together: the copy connects the copies; a connector copied alone detaches, and the original keeps its ends
  - [x] a triggered animation on duplicated and pasted slides resolves to the cloned target and trigger, still after a `.deckcraft` save/reload
- [x] `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm)

Closes #406

title: Render: budget shape path-gradient work on dense outlines (#404)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
- A `shape` path gradient tested every raster pixel (up to 384×384) against every flattened outline edge. An outline with tens of thousands of segments meant billions of tests and a long render stall.
- `pathgrad::fill` now caps pixels × edges at 64M. Before rasterising, the outline is simplified to fit: points closer together than one raster pixel are dropped first (detail the image can't show), then, if it's still too dense, every k-th point is kept.
- Each polygon stays closed and keeps at least 8 edges. Normal outlines (ellipses, triangles, presets) are under the budget and are used unchanged.
- No unwrap/panic in non-test code.

## Test plan
- [x] An 80k-edge square is simplified to ≤ 400 edges and still gives correct positions (0.5 half way to a side and to a corner)
- [x] A gradient fill of that square through `fill` finishes quickly (≈0.1 s in the test run)
- [x] Existing ellipse/triangle/focus-box gradient tests unchanged and passing
- [x] `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm)

Closes #404

title: Text: bidi levels for language runs in linear time (#403)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Closes #403.

## Summary
- `levels_lang` (`crates/text/src/bidi.rs`) no longer rescans the text for every character, so a long run of `$` in a Hebrew or Arabic-language run, or many short neutral spans, now takes linear time instead of quadratic.
- **W4/W5 (currency and percent signs next to numbers):** each ET character used to search forward through the rest of its ET run. The first non-ET index after each position is now computed once (`next_non_et`).
- **Neutrals in right-to-left runs:** each span used to search backwards and forwards for the nearest strong direction, which is also quadratic when spans repeat. The direction after a span is now computed once up front, and the one before it is carried along as the loop goes. This is exact: resolving a span only changes characters before the scan position.
- Behaviour is unchanged. The old implementation is kept in the tests as a reference and compared against the new one.

## Test plan
- [x] `matches_the_reference_on_random_mixed_text`: 4000 random paragraphs (Latin, Hebrew, Arabic, European/Arabic digits, ET/ES/CS signs, brackets, combining marks, mixed run languages, both paragraph directions) give the same levels as the pre-change code.
- [x] `long_currency_and_neutral_runs_are_linear`: 200 000 `$` after a Hebrew letter, and 200 000 alternating right-to-left and left-to-right neutrals, finish at once in a debug build.
- [x] `currency_signs_join_numbers_on_either_side_in_rtl_runs`: `$$5`, `5%%` and lone `$$` checked in a Hebrew-language run.
- [x] `next_non_et_points_past_each_et_run`
- [x] `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, test, assets, layers, wasm all pass.

title: Render: cap RGBA conversion and bound the failed-image cache (#402)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
- Raster picture decodes refuse anything whose straight-RGBA output would be over 512 MiB. The size is checked from the header before decoding and again before `to_rgba8`, which the image crate's 512 MiB decoder limit doesn't cover (a grey image converts to 4× its decoded size). Before, up to 400 million pixels (about 1.6 GB of RGBA) were allowed.
- The failed-decode ("bad") cache is bounded: at most 256 sources and 64 MiB of encoded bytes, oldest forgotten first, so evicted sources' `Arc`s are released. A failed input larger than the byte budget isn't kept at all. A hit must be the same `Arc`, not only the same address.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p deckcraft-render --lib images::tests`, new tests:
  - [x] with a small cap, a grey PNG whose RGBA exceeds it is refused, and one that fits exactly decodes
  - [x] marking more failed sources than the limits keeps 256 entries and stays within the byte budget, evicted sources go back to `strong_count == 1`, and oversized inputs aren't retained
  - [x] control: invalid bytes fail repeatedly, and a valid PNG decodes and comes back from the cache as the same pixmap
- [x] `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm)

Closes #402

title: Web: keep a picked file on the document and slide that asked for it
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary

The browser file picker queued only a file name and its bytes. When the read finished, DeckCraft guessed the command from the name and ran it on whichever document and slide were active. Switching slides or presentations while a file was being read, or having two picks finish out of order, could insert a picture, sound, video or outline into the wrong place.

A pick or a drop now records the document, the slide (or master/layout), the operation that was requested, and a cancellation id. The file is applied to that target when it arrives. If the presentation or slide is gone, or the picker was dismissed, the file is dropped instead of landing in whatever is open.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p deckcraft-ui-egui --lib inbox_tests` covers a picture and an audio clip finishing in reverse order after a slide and document change, an outline staying on the document that opened it, a video request that does not insert a PNG as a picture, a deleted slide, a closed presentation, a dismissed picker, and a drop
- [x] `cargo clippy -p deckcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo xtask assets`, `cargo xtask layers`
- [x] `cargo check -p deckcraft-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` and `cargo check -p deckcraft-ui-egui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`
- [ ] In the browser, Insert → Picture, change slide while the file is read, and confirm the picture is on the slide that asked for it

Closes #414

title: Pptx: budget chart points, chart XML size, inflate work and VML lookups (#401)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
- **Charts:** every category, value and bubble-size cache now takes from one chart-wide budget of 1M decoded slots (the 100k-per-cache cap stays), so sparse `ptCount`/`idx` declarations across up to 1000 series can't expand far beyond the XML they came from.
- **Chart XML size:** chart parts now go through the 96 MiB XML guard (new `Package::xml_bytes`) instead of reading the raw part.
- **Decompression work:** `Package::open` counts every byte it inflates, including parts it then throws away (too big, or failing part-way), against a 4 GiB budget (`MAX_INFLATE_WORK`), and stops reading entries once that's spent. The per-part, total and entry-count limits are unchanged.
- **VML previews:** each legacy VML drawing is parsed once per import into a shape id → picture part index (cached on `Imp`), instead of re-parsing the drawing and its rels for every OLE object that uses it.
- No unwrap/panic in non-test code.

## Test plan
- [x] Chart: five sparse series, each declaring 100k points, under a small budget stay within it, and the last series is cut short
- [x] OPC: discarded parts are charged, so a later part that would fit is not read once the budget is spent; `xml_bytes` returns small parts and nothing for missing ones
- [x] VML: 200 OLE frames sharing one drawing (including missing and unknown shape ids) each get the right preview or none
- [x] Existing OLE/VML and chart tests pass
- [x] `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm)

Closes #401

title: AV1: reject duplicate film-grain scaling points; a failed job still publishes (#394)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
- The film-grain header rejects Y, Cb and Cr scaling point values that don't strictly increase (AV1 spec 6.8.20) with `Error::Invalid`. Before, a duplicate value made the scaling lookup divide by zero.
- The scaling lookup (7.18.3.4) moves into `scaling_lut`, which skips a non-increasing pair and uses checked indexing, as defence in depth.
- `run_job` runs `decode_frame` inside `guarded` (`catch_unwind`), so a panic in a frame job turns into an error published to the picture slot and the reference slot. The output and dependent frames get an error instead of waiting forever on threaded decoding.

## Test plan
- [x] `header::grain_point_tests`: duplicate and descending point values are rejected; empty, single and increasing lists are accepted
- [x] `grain::tests`: the lookup still interpolates, and duplicate or descending points don't panic
- [x] `decoder::guard_tests`: a panicking job wakes both waiters (output and dependent reference) with an error, bounded by a 10 s `recv_timeout`, not an unbounded hang
- [x] `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm)

Closes #394

title: Recovery: unique uids, per-instance ownership, keep snapshots until replaced (#390)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
- **Unique document uids:** a random per-process base plus a counter, kept below 2^53 so they survive JSON numbers. Before, uids started at 1 in every process, so instances sharing the recovery folder overwrote and deleted each other's entries.
- **Instance ownership:** each instance holds an OS file lock (`File::try_lock`) on `owner-<id>.lock` in the folder while it runs, and the entry metadata records its `owner`. `file.recovery.open` skips the entries of a running owner and deletes lock files left by dead instances.
- **No early delete:** opening an entry doesn't delete it any more. The recovered presentation keeps the entry's uid and takes ownership of it, so the snapshot stays on disk until the next recovery save replaces it, or a save/close removes it. A second crash right after recovery still finds it. Entries already open in the session aren't opened twice.
- Entry files and metadata are both written via temp file + rename.
- No unwrap/panic in non-test code.

## Test plan
- [x] Recover, then "crash" again before any checkpoint: the presentation is recovered again. Saving it removes the entry.
- [x] Another live instance's entry (its lock held) survives this instance saving clean and dirty presentations and is skipped by recovery open. Once its lock is released, the entry is recovered and the stale lock file removed.
- [x] Uids are distinct and not the old small per-process numbers
- [x] `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm)

Closes #390

title: Media: keep playback with the document and the clip (#415)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
- Playback belongs to the open presentation. Switching decks, or closing the last one, stops the previous voices and GIF clocks, so a shape id shared by two decks cannot keep the old clip.
- Replacing a clip while it is playing swaps in the new audio, duration, and video feed. Resuming the same source still continues from where it paused.
- The decode cache and the duration cache keep the source bytes they are keyed by, and the duration cache stays within 16 entries, so a freed allocation cannot be reused as a stale hit.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p deckcraft-media --lib player::tests` (including replacement of a voice's source, retained cache bytes, and resume of the same source)

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask assets`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`

title: Video: check the whole picture store against a memory budget (#398)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Closes #398.

## Summary
- New `deckcraft_bitstream::budget` module: `PictureShape` gives a picture's allocated bytes (luma plus subsampled chroma, sample size) using checked `u64` arithmetic, and `fits(pictures, budget)` checks a whole picture store against a budget. `DECODE_MEMORY_BUDGET` is 4 GiB on 64-bit targets and 1 GiB on 32-bit ones (wasm32).
- Each video decoder checks its **whole picture store** before allocating for a picture: the current picture, every reference slot and the pictures still in flight on worker threads, padded the way that decoder pads them. A header over budget is a decode error, not an out-of-memory abort.
  - **AV1:** `NUM_REF_FRAMES + 1 + max_in_flight` frames on the 128-sample superblock grid plus 160 samples of slack, 16-bit samples, monochrome-aware. The 65536 × 65536 axis maximum (over 8 GiB of luma per frame) is now refused.
  - **VP9:** 8 reference slots + 1 + threads + 2 frames on the 64-sample grid, 16-bit samples.
  - **HEVC:** `sps_max_dec_pic_buffering + 1 + max_in_flight` pictures, 16-bit samples, chroma format from the SPS.
  - **H.264:** `MaxDpbFrames + 1 + max_in_flight` pictures, 8-bit samples, chroma format from the SPS.
- `set_memory_budget(bytes)` on each decoder lets hosts lower the budget, and lets tests use small budgets without allocating huge images.
- The existing per-axis caps stay as they were.

## Test plan
- [x] `bitstream::budget` tests: bytes for 4:2:0, 4:4:4, odd sizes and monochrome; the exact budget boundary (fits at N bytes, not at N − 1, not with one more picture); overflow is never within budget.
- [x] H.264 and HEVC synthetic streams decode exactly at the computed budget (DPB size from their SPS + current + in flight), fail one byte below it, and decode at the default budget.
- [x] AV1 and VP9: the axis maximum is over the default budget, 4K and 1080p are within it, and the exact boundary and reference count are checked on padded sizes.
- [x] `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, test, asse…

title: Text: draw a saved normAutofit shrink as saved while the text fits (#327)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary

- The importer already read these values and the writer already wrote them, so only the layout changes.
- The issue's other point, EMF pictures shown as a missing-picture box, is already fixed on `main` (`deckcraft-metafile` draws EMF/WMF; see `docs/gaps.md`), so this PR doesn't touch it.

## Test plan

- [x] Text that overflows at its saved 90% is fitted again below 90%
- [x] A 100% shrink still uses our own fit; `shrink_on_overflow` unchanged

title: UI: open presentations in the background with a progress window (#350)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Closes #350.

## Summary

title: Designer: layout ideas that rearrange the current slide (#314)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
- New commands `design.ideas` (query: `{slide?}` → `[{id, label}]`) and `design.applyIdea` (`{id, slide?}`) in `crates/engine/src/cmd/ideas.rs`. The UI, CLI and MCP all reach them the same way.

A text-only slide (title and text) gets: a title column, a centred title over the text, and the text above with the title at the foot.

- The Design Ideas pane shows the layout ideas first, then the themes under a "whole presentation" heading. Its thumbnails are cached until the deck revision, the slide or the pane width changes, instead of rendering every slide variant each frame (the ~24 ms/frame cost from the report).

title: Show: render the next slide in the background while the current one rests (#240)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
- Advancing in the slide show rendered the new slide synchronously on the UI thread, at full screen resolution, before anything appeared, so every advance paid the whole render cost.
- While a slide rests (no animation step or transition playing), the show now renders the next slide's first frame (next in `show_order`, at the current size, with hide-while-not-playing media hidden) on a background thread. Entering that slide uploads the finished image instead of rendering. If the render is still running, it waits for it rather than starting over.
- Any mismatch (different step, size, document, playing media, or a slide entered mid-animation) falls back to rendering as before. Slides with animated GIFs (their frame depends on when they're entered) and the web build (no threads) are not prefetched.
- The frame rendering is shared through one `render_frame` helper, so prefetched and on-demand frames come from the same code. No unwrap/panic in non-test code.

## Test plan
- [x] A prefetched frame has the key the show computes on entry and is pixel-identical to the frame rendered on demand
- [x] Existing transition-texture test passes
- [x] `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm)

title: Shapes: smooth a rectangle's corners into a squircle (#286)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Closes #286.

## Summary
- New `deckcraft_geom::squircle::path_d(w, h, radius, smoothing)`: a rectangle outline whose corners are **smoothed**, like the corner-smoothing control in design tools.
  - Each corner takes `(1 + s) · r` of the edge and keeps a circular arc of `90° · (1 − s)` about the diagonal.
  - Cubic curves join the arc to each edge, tangent to both.
  - When the corner would pass the middle of an edge, the smoothing is reduced first, then the radius.
  - Hostile input (NaN, infinity, negative) gives a plain rectangle.
  - The construction is derived here from those constraints; no code was copied.
- New command **`shape.smoothCorners {smoothing: 0–100, radius?, ids?}`** (Shape Format ▸ Insert Shapes ▸ Edit Shape):
  - A rectangle or rounded rectangle becomes custom geometry with smoothed corners. The radius is the rounded rectangle's own unless `radius` is given.
  - An outline already smoothed takes a new value when given a `radius`. Other shapes are refused.
  - One undo step. Available to MCP and the control channel like every command.
- **Edit Shape ▸ Smooth Corners** slider (0–100 %) under the Change Shape gallery. It remembers the radius per shape, so the slider keeps re-smoothing the same corners, and it applies one undo step per adjustment.
- PPTX: the result is saved as `a:custGeom`, so PowerPoint shows the same outline.
- Limit: a smoothed shape is a custom outline. Resizing it afterwards stretches the corners, as with any custom shape. Moving the slider again rebuilds them at the new size.

title: Slide show: a slide with many distinct animation triggers builds its timeline in linear time (#410)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #410.

**What was wrong.** `Timeline::with` was quadratic on slides with many distinct animation triggers, three ways: trigger-sequence discovery ran `Vec::contains` per triggered animation, every sequence rescanned the entire animation list, and each animation's shape was looked up by walking the whole shape tree (`slide.shape`) — with the base-colour pass adding a `tl.colors` scan and another tree walk per effect. A slide with a trigger on every shape stalled the show's startup for seconds; none of it was bounded by `MAX_EFFECTS`, which only limits the output.

**The fix** (`crates/anim/src/timeline.rs`): one pass groups animation indices by `Sequence` into a map plus a first-appearance order vec (main first — identical sequence and within-sequence order to the old scan); the shape tree is flattened once into an id→shape map (the walk includes group children and first-match-wins, matching `Slide::shape` exactly); the colour pass uses a seen-set and the same map; the `MAX_EFFECTS` cap is enforced per animation (exact old truncation mid-sequence at 100,000) with an O(1) per-sequence early-out, and triggers of sequences past the cap are dropped with it. The by-paragraph group dedup also swaps its linear `tl.groups.contains` for a set, so an oversized text body no longer goes quadratic on itself.

**Tests:** a slide with 100,050 animations carrying distinct triggers (fifty past the 100k effect cap) — the timeline caps at exactly 100,000 effects, effect *k* points at animation *k* (slide order), triggers exist for every processed sequence, and building finishes in ~0.4s; the unfixed code cannot finish in 100 seconds. All existing timeline behaviour tests pass unchanged.

**Out of scope, noted for follow-up:** per-frame query paths (`state_with` filters all effects per shape per frame; `animated_shapes` is quadratic) are the next superlinear wall the same indexing would fix. ROADMAP progress-log row added.

title: Media: bound audio decode memory and cancel stopped jobs
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
- Each playing voice keeps a bounded PCM window (two seconds of stereo by default). A longer file slides that window forward as the playhead moves.
- Finished clips that fit in the window are cached up to 8 MiB. At most two decodes run at once. Stopping a voice, stopping all voices, or dropping the player cancels a decode that is no longer needed.
- On the web, where there are no threads, each tick pulls one bounded chunk. Duration probes for files with no container length count frames into a reused buffer.

author: Dejan-Port

Adds an **opt-in, off-by-default** `self-hosted-update` feature to `apps/deckcraft-web`, for one case only: people who **host DeckCraft's web build on their own server**. It is not for desktop users. The desktop app, the CLI and the release packages are untouched, and a web build without the feature makes no update requests and shows nothing.

**Why.** We run self-hosted web deployments of GridCraft, WordCraft and DeckCraft. title: Engine: seeded editor soak tests; tiny charts no longer blank the slide
author: NikitkaRa
body:
There is no tracking issue for this. It is ROADMAP "Upcoming" item 1 ("No data loss, no startup crashes": editor soak tests), `docs/gaps.md` "No soak or long-session testing". I checked item 2 (EMF/WMF/SVG and the PPTX issues) first: every concrete issue there already has an open PR (#380, #437, #485, #452, #451, #374/#250, #271/#216).

## Summary
- New `crates/engine/src/soak_tests.rs` runs seeded, deterministic random command sequences over a deck of about 100 slides. Every non-file command is called with plausible parameters built from the live document, plus some hostile ones. After every step it checks that:
  - no command panics, including panics the guard catches (`EngineError::Internal` fails the test)
  - `Presentation::validate()` is empty and the selection slide is in range
  - the undo stack stays within its limit
  - undo followed by redo of a real edit gives back the **exact** document (both compared with `PartialEq`)
  - every 100 steps, the deck saves and reopens as both `.deckcraft` and `.pptx` with the same slide count and a valid document
- At least 10% of steps must change the document, so the soak can't pass by only hitting disabled commands. In practice about 23% do.
- CI runs 4 seeds × 400 steps in under a second. `soak_long` is `#[ignore]` and takes `DECKCRAFT_SOAK_STEPS` and `DECKCRAFT_SOAK_SEED`. A failure prints the seed and the last 20 commands so it can be replayed.
- `undo_stack_stays_bounded_and_drains` covers undo depth: it adds limit + 50 edits, checks the stack is exactly the limit, and undoes exactly that many.
- **Bug found by the soak and fixed:** a chart a few points wide panicked in `f64::clamp` because the label gutter's minimum (`base * 1.5`) was above its maximum (`width * 0.3`). The render guard then **blanked the whole slide**. `chart.rs` now uses `clamp_soft`, which cannot panic, for both gutters and the zero line. Render test: `tiny_chart_does_not_blank_the_slide`.

title: Pictures: compress pictures to a target resolution
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
- New `picture.compress {ppi?: 330|220|150|96 (default 220), deleteCropped?: bool (default true), all?: bool, ids?}` → `{pictures, before, after}`.
- **Downsampling:** each PNG/JPEG/BMP/TIFF/WebP picture goes down to the pixels its shown size needs at that ppi. With the crop kept, the visible part is what gets the full resolution.
- **Formats:** JPEG stays JPEG (quality 85); the others become PNG. SVG, EMF/WMF, GIF and linked pictures are left alone.
- **Delete cropped areas:** cuts the cropped-away pixels and resets the crop. Padding crops (negative values) are kept.
- **No growth:** a picture is replaced only when the result is smaller or a crop was removed. A picture shared by shapes at the same size and crop is compressed once.
- **Originals:** an original nothing else uses is dropped, so the `.deckcraft` and `.pptx` files really shrink. One still used by a picture that wasn't compressed stays. One undo step restores everything.
- **UI:** Picture Format › Adjust › **Compress Pictures** opens PowerPoint's options: Apply only to this picture, Delete cropped areas of pictures, and HD / Print / Web / E-mail resolution. A Compress button runs it, and the status bar reports the KB saved.
- **Docs:** parity checklist row M → D; removed from gaps.md "Smaller missing rows".

No issue tracks this; it's a docs/gaps.md item.

title: Review: compare with a revised copy and accept its slides
author: NikitkaRa
body:
There is no tracking issue. This is the `docs/gaps.md` "Smaller missing rows" item "compare presentations" and the `docs/parity-checklist.md` row Review › Compare presentations (now M → P). It is a coherent first slice: list the revisions, accept them, end the review.

## Summary
- `review.compare {path} | {name, data: base64}` (noundo) reads a revised copy (native or PPTX) and opens the **Revisions** pane. It returns slide-level changes against the open presentation:
  - **inserted** slides, placed after the open slide that matches the revised slide before them
  - **deleted** slides
  - **changed** slides, with readable details: `Title 1: text`, `Picture 3 inserted`, text formatting, moved, resized, rotated, formatting, picture, other properties, object order, layout, notes, transition, animations, background, hidden or shown
- Slides match by id, since a revised copy keeps them. When the decks share no slide id at all, they match **by position**, and that mode is fixed for the whole session so accepting slides can't switch the matching halfway. Shapes match by id, then by name.
- `review.accept {index} | {all: true}` (undoable, one step) applies revisions. A revised slide is adopted safely:
  - its media is copied into the open deck, and remapped if an id clashes with different bytes
  - its shape ids are kept unless another slide uses them; fresh ids are allocated otherwise, and animations and triggers follow
  - its layout is matched by id, then by name, then falls back to the first layout
  - a changed slide keeps the open slide's id, and the last remaining slide is never deleted
- `review.revisions` (query) and `review.endCompare` complete the set. Accept and End are disabled when no compare is running.
- Review tab gets a new group: **Compare** (file picker; the web build reports that it needs the desktop app for now, instead of opening the file as a new document), **Accept All** and **End Review**.
- The Revisions pane shows one card per change, colour-code…

title: Format: report damaged embedded media and open such files as a repaired copy
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
- `deckcraft_format::load_checked` lists each embedded media member it couldn't read: missing, too large, or failing its read/CRC check. `load` used to drop these failures silently. Linked media saved without its bytes doesn't count as damage.
- `file.open` and `file.openBytes` now return `damagedMedia`. When it isn't empty they show a message and open the deck as an untitled "… (Repaired)" copy. Save then asks for a new name, so the original file isn't overwritten with empty pictures.
- Undamaged files open as before: same path, same title.
- Overlap: the older open #42 also changes `read_entry` and the media loop to handle size limits and errors. A conflict in `crates/format/src/lib.rs` is possible. This PR covers the recovery and warning behaviour #392 asks for.

Closes #392

## Test plan
- [x] `missing_or_corrupt_media_is_reported` (format): a missing member and a bad CRC are each reported once, the media is left empty, and linked-only media isn't reported
- [x] `damaged_native_file_opens_as_repaired_copy` (engine): a good file keeps its path. A bad-CRC file gets no path, a "(Repaired)" title, a message and `damagedMedia` through both open routes, and the original file stays byte-identical
- [x] `cargo xtask ci`
- [ ] Manual check of the message in the desktop app (the box has no display, so the UI wasn't checked by screenshot)

title: Format: bound total embedded media when opening a .deckcraft
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
- Opening a `.deckcraft` now caps all embedded media together at 4 GiB inflated and the number of media items at 100,000. Before, only each member was capped (2 GiB).
- A member that declares more than the remaining budget is refused before it's inflated. A member that inflates past what it declared is stopped at the limit.
- A repeated media id keeps only its first item, so the member is inflated once. Before, duplicates inflated it again each time and the deck couldn't be saved afterwards (a zip can't hold two `media/<id>` entries).
- Overlap: this touches the same media loop as my #526 (#392) and the older #42, so a small conflict is possible. It's based on main and not stacked.

Closes #393

- [x] `repeated_media_ids_are_read_once`: 51 references to one 1000-byte member open within a 1000-byte budget and the deck saves again

title: PPTX: keep add-in tags on the presentation, slides and shapes
author: NikitkaRa
body:

title: PPTX: read Office 2016 charts (waterfall, funnel, treemap…) and keep them
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
- Waterfall, funnel, treemap, sunburst, histogram, Pareto and box & whisker charts are stored in a `chartEx` part behind an `mc:AlternateContent` choice that requires `cx1`. DeckCraft used to take the fallback, usually a text box saying "This chart isn't available in your version of PowerPoint", so these charts were lost on open and again on save.
- The `cx1` choice is now taken for `chartEx` frames, and the new `read/chartex.rs` reads the part into the chart model. Each layout maps to its existing `ChartType`, and the reader takes the categories (innermost level), values, number format, series name, title, legend and data labels.
- An unchanged chart is written back as its `chartEx` part in a `cx1` choice, with a plain chart of the same data as the fallback, the way PowerPoint writes it. The workbook link is dropped, as it already is for plain charts. An edited chart is saved as a plain chart only.
- Not covered: region maps aren't read and keep their fallback. Drawing still uses the bar renderer, so a waterfall has no floating bars yet. docs/gaps.md is updated.

## Test plan

An unchanged export has the chartEx part (no externalData), the content type, both rels, the cx1 choice and the plain-chart fallback, and it reimports as a waterfall. An edited chart writes no chartEx and no cx1.

title: File › Settings: custom keyboard shortcuts (#127), interface size, new-presentation defaults, backup and reset
author: Zetenypapp
body:
Hi again! This follows on from #349 (interface themes). Like that one, it's an experiment more than a finished proposal: take the whole thing, take only the parts you like, or close it. No hard feelings either way.

**Upfront about how this was made:** I'm not a programmer. The code, the tests and this description were written by Claude (Claude Code, Opus 5.5). I described what I wanted, made the design decisions and tried every tab myself on Windows 11.

**It builds on #349.** This branch contains #349's commits, so please look at #349 first. The 3 new commits on top are what this PR adds.

## What it does

The themes from #349 move from File › Account to a new **File › Settings** page, which the title bar's gear now opens. Account goes back to exactly how it is on `main`, plus a link to Settings. The Settings page has a search box above five tabs:

| Tab | What's in it |
|---|---|
| General | **Interface size:** 90–175% buttons and 5% steps, from 75% to 200%. **Reduce motion:** no animated menus, panes or scrolling; slide animations still play. **When DeckCraft starts:** the start screen, the last presentation or a blank one |
| Themes | The themes from #349 |
| New Presentations | The theme, slide size (16:9 or 4:3) and font every new presentation starts with, with a preview. Set as Default Shape is now kept between sessions (until now it was forgotten on quit) |
| Keyboard Shortcuts | **Custom shortcuts (#127):** give any command or slide-show action your own keys. Keys are recorded from a key press, and you're asked before a key moves from another action. Each action can be reset, or all of them at once. **Save cheat sheet…** writes a printable HTML page of every key, including your own; **Copy as text** copies the list |
| Backup and Reset | **Back up settings… / Restore from a backup…:** all settings to one JSON file and back (recent files are left out). **Reset all settings**, with a confirmation; presentations and recent files are kept |

Typing in the sear…

title: Draw: Ink to Shape converts pen strokes into shapes
author: NikitkaRa
body:

## Summary

- Strokes that aren't recognised, highlighter strokes and tiny marks stay ink. The ink shape is removed once it is empty. Nothing to convert is a no-op, not an error.
- The recogniser is pure geometry in `engine/src/inkshape.rs`: ends meeting, area covered within the bounding box, and spread from the fitted ellipse. It ignores non-finite points and caps the point count, and it never panics.
- The Draw tab's **Ink to Shape** button now works. It is enabled when the slide has ink.
- Ribbon big buttons now carry an accessibility label (`widget_info`, with newlines read as spaces), so screen readers and kittest can find them.

- [x] Command test: a rectangle stroke plus a zigzag gives one rect with the stroke's width and leaves the zigzag as ink. Undo restores the ink. A slide with no ink is a no-op.
- [x] kittest: the Black Pen draws a rectangle with mouse drags, Ink to Shape replaces it with a rect at the drawn bounds, and the result is selected. I checked the rendered screenshot.

title: Tables: Draw Table pencil and Table Eraser
author: NikitkaRa
body:

## Summary
- **Insert › Table › Draw Table** turns on a table pencil, which stays on until you pick another tool, as in PowerPoint.
  - Dragging a box on an empty part of the slide makes a **one-cell table**.
  - Drawing a line inside a table **splits the cells it crosses**, horizontally or vertically. A row or column is added only where needed; the cells it doesn't cross stay whole (they get a span). A line on an existing grid line splits the merged cells there.

- The grid work is pure in `engine/src/drawtable.rs`. It rebuilds the table from its anchor cells, so existing merges survive, and handles vertical lines by transposing. It rejects non-finite points, snaps to lines within 4 pt, caps the grid at 200 rows and columns, and never panics.
- The canvas preview shows a flat border line inside a table and an outline for a new table.
- Ribbon big buttons now carry an accessibility label (\`widget_info\`), the same one-line change as in #539.

title: Pictures: Remove Background with a classical matte
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
- Picture Format ▸ **Remove Background** was a disabled "coming soon" placeholder. It now opens a menu with Remove Background, Remove More (looser) and Remove Less (tighter).
- The new `picture.removeBackground` command `{tolerance?: 0..100, ids?}` uses a classical matte, with no ML model. A flood fill starts from every edge pixel and spreads through similar colours. Each step has to be close to the pixel before it, so gradients and soft shadows are followed, and close to the edge colour it started from, so the fill can't leak into the subject. That region turns transparent, with a one-pixel soft edge.
- The picture then points to a new `<name>-no-background.png`, and its crop and corrections are kept. Undo restores the original picture.
- Pictures whose edges are all subject are left alone, and the command reports that it found no background. Pictures over 16 megapixels are refused with a hint to compress them first. Shapes that aren't pictures are skipped.
- docs/gaps.md: "remove background" is removed from the smaller missing rows.
- Limits: there's no Keep/Remove marking tool like PowerPoint's yet, and a subject that matches its background's colour at the edge will lose that part.

No issue exists for this. It's a gaps.md depth item.

## Test plan

author: NikitkaRa

Until now, View › Guides painted two fixed centre lines that you couldn't move, add to or save.

## Summary
- **Guides belong to the presentation.** The model has a new `Presentation.guides: Vec<DrawGuide { vertical, pos }>`. They are read from and written to `p:slideViewPr/p:cSldViewPr/p:guideLst` in `viewProps.xml`, in eighths of a point as PowerPoint stores them, so guides survive a round trip with PowerPoint.

- The slide context menu has a **Grid and Guides** submenu with a Guides checkbox, Add Vertical Guide and Add Horizontal Guide.
- **Snapping:** while guides are shown, moving and resizing shapes snaps to them, alongside the existing smart guides.
- New commands: `guide.add {vertical, pos? | defaults}`, `guide.move {index, pos}` and `guide.delete {index}` are undoable; `guide.list` is a query. Positions are clamped to the slide, non-finite values are rejected, and there are at most 200 guides.
- **Overlap with #536:** #536 (Grid Options) is complementary. Its "Display drawing guides" checkbox sets `ui.guides` directly, so after both merge, that path won't add the centre guides until it goes through `view.guides`. That is a one-line follow-up.
