title: MCP: validate reply IDs and bounded response frames (#718)
author: MMexicann
body:
Fixes #718. Implemented with Codex on behalf of @MMexicann.

## Problem and root cause

A remote MCP mutation could be reported as successful using another request's reply. `Remote::receive` used an unbounded `read_line`, accepted EOF without a terminating newline, and `call` inspected `ok` without validating the request ID or envelope. The socket preflight could not see unsolicited bytes already held in `BufReader`.

## Changes

- Bound reply frames to 16 MiB including the terminating newline; accept CRLF and reject incomplete or oversized frames.
- Require the current numeric request ID, boolean `ok`, and exactly one of a success `result` or string `error`.
- Drop invalid connections and report that the command may or may not have run, without replaying it.
- Check buffered unsolicited bytes before sending and open a fresh connection when present.
- Add seven loopback tests alongside the existing lost-reply/reconnect tests; update protocol, roadmap, gaps and parity evidence. Scores remain unchanged.

## Reproduction

Run `cargo test -p deckcraft-mcp backend::tests`. The synthetic peer in `wrong_reply_id_is_not_command_success` receives `engine.execute` / `slide.new` and answers `{"id":999,"ok":true,"result":"unrelated"}\n`. Previously the call returned success; now it returns an unknown-outcome error and invalidates the connection.

The buffered-frame test sends a valid reply plus an unsolicited second success together. It explicitly loads the second frame into `BufReader`, with an ID matching the next request. The next mutation must reach a fresh connection and receive its actual application error.

## Verification

- Nine backend tests against unchanged upstream production code in an isolated harness: **4 passed, 5 failed** (the five reported defect cases).
- `cargo test -p deckcraft-mcp`: **19 unit + 5 integration tests passed**, including after rebasing onto b1ca123. The final test checks that an oversized reply invalidates its connection before cleanup.
- Foc…

title: media: check the ASF object walk's arithmetic so hostile sizes cannot panic
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`probe_asf` walks ASF header objects with unchecked arithmetic: the loop guard is `while pos + 24 <= header_end` and the advance is `pos += size`, where `size` is read as a raw 64-bit object size. A 64-byte file — the ASF header GUID followed by 48 × `0xFF` — reads back `usize::MAX` as the size, so the walk panics (`attempt to add with overflow` with overflow checks; a slice-index panic after the wrap without them) instead of rejecting the file, and the editor probes media on the UI thread, so inserting or playing it takes the app down.

The fix uses `pos.checked_add(24)` in the loop condition and `pos.checked_add(size).filter(|&p| p <= header_end)` for the advance: an object that overruns the header ends the walk, which is also the correct ASF semantics. A regression test (`hostile_asf_object_sizes_end_the_walk`) builds that exact header and asserts `probe_asf` returns `Ok(container == "asf")`; it fails on the old code with `attempt to add with overflow` at `probe.rs:233` and passes with the fix, and the whole `deckcraft-media` suite is green.

Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

Addresses #750

title: media: walk ID3 tag chains iteratively so crafted files cannot overflow the stack
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`Container::sniff` recurses once per ID3v2 tag: when the bytes start with `ID3` it slices off the tag and calls itself again, so a file made of N copies of a 10-byte empty ID3v2 header consumes N stack frames — ~1 MB of crafted input is ~100k frames, far past the main and worker stacks. This produces an uncatchable stack-overflow abort (SIGABRT) rather than an error, and `Session::execute`'s panic guard cannot catch it; the editor probes media on the UI thread on insert and playback.

The fix walks the tag chain iteratively — each pass consumes at least 10 bytes, so it always terminates — and sniffs the bytes after the last tag exactly as before (only `Adts` survives the match; everything else is `Mp3`). The regression test (`id3_tag_chains_do_not_recurse_the_stack`) feeds 200,000 empty tags followed by an MP3 frame sync; on the old code the test process dies with `fatal runtime error: stack overflow` (SIGABRT), and with the fix the test and the whole `deckcraft-media` suite pass.

Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

Addresses #750

title: Preferences: Cancel, Esc and the close button undo the dialog's changes (#752)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #752

## What was wrong

The Preferences dialog applies each control as it changes: Dark appearance, Interface size, the Editing checkboxes (smart guides, snap to grid, smart quotes, AutoCorrect) and the comment author name write straight into the live settings. Its button row returned `(ok, cancel)`, but the dialog only used `ok`, so clicking **Cancel** did nothing at all: the window stayed open and the changes stayed applied.

## The fix

- When Preferences opens, the dialog keeps a snapshot of what it can change (appearance, interface size, the engine `Prefs`).
- **Cancel** puts that snapshot back and closes the dialog.
- **Esc** and the window's close button do the same, as in other preference dialogs.
- **Done** keeps the changes, as before.

The controls still preview live (switching Dark appearance still restyles at once); only the way out changed. Opening *AutoCorrect Options…* from Preferences still switches to that dialog and keeps what was changed so far, as before.

User-visible change: Cancel/Esc/close in Preferences now discard the changes made in that session of the dialog (previously Cancel did nothing and Esc/close kept them).

## Tests

- New `preferences_cancel_restores_the_settings_done_keeps_them` (egui_kittest): toggles Dark appearance, Show smart guides and Snap objects to grid, then checks that Cancel and Esc each close the dialog and restore all three, and that Done closes it and keeps them. It fails on `main` (Cancel leaves the dialog open) and passes with the fix.
- Local `cargo xtask ci` steps all pass: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, assets, layers. The `wasm` step was not run: this machine's Rust (Gentoo) has no wasm32 std. The change touches no wasm-specific code.

title: control: a request that timed out while queued is abandoned, never run late (#719)
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A control request answered `timeout` after 60 s was still sitting in the UI's queue, so a window that resumed draining ran the mutation anyway — a client retry could execute twice, and the old command could land on a newly active document. `ControlRequest` now carries a pending/taken/abandoned state (the same pattern the sibling LightCraft control channel uses): when the reply wait expires the server abandons a request that is still queued, and `SlideApp::drain_control` skips anything whose sender gave up, so it never runs late. If the app had already claimed the request, the reply reports an unknown outcome instead of a definite failure. Regression tests cover deadline-before-dispatch and dispatch-before-deadline, plus a unit test for the state handshake.

Fixes #719

title: text: a bare normAutofit draws at 100% and an edit stores the fitted scale (#724)
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A file whose `<a:normAutofit/>` carries no `fontScale` was read as 100 % and then refitted on open, so DeckCraft drew overflowing text shrunk where PowerPoint draws it as it is. The saved scale is now an `Option`: `None` means the file had no `fontScale`, is drawn at 100 % and is not refitted on open, while a scale the file saved is still drawn as saved. After a text change the engine lays the body out as if the scale had been reset and stores the scale the layout computes, so the file is saved with the `fontScale`/`lnSpcReduction` DeckCraft draws instead of a bare `<a:normAutofit/>`; the writer also writes an explicit 100 % for a scale the model holds, keeping reopen consistent. Tests pin bare-vs-saved-100 % parsing, the no-refit draw, the edit path (with undo/redo and a saved `.pptx` carrying the scale) and a native-format round trip. One note for review: a `.deckcraft` whose body has no saved scale omits `fontScale`, so older builds will report a missing field for that body (the `.pptx` path is unaffected).

Fixes #724

title: Text: anchorCtr centres the drawn text block - right-aligned text stayed glued to the box edge (#736)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #736.

**What was wrong.** With `anchorCtr="1"`, the centring offset was computed for a block that starts at the box's left edge and then **added** to lines that alignment had already placed within the box. For a right-aligned line the two shifts stacked: the line began at the box's centre and ran past the right edge — on the fixture, the sentence was cut off at "…paragraph rig". The `.max(0.0)` clamp made wide content worse: all the overflow went right, never left. The issue's "zero-size shape" framing is incidental — placeholder inheritance resolves the real box (828×104 pt); the defect is the anchorCtr placement whenever alignment is not left.

**The fix** (`crates/text/src/lib.rs`, ~15 lines): with `anchorCtr` on (horizontal text, single column), the origin is set so the **drawn text block's own centre** — min/max of the laid-out line extents — lands on the box's centre. Every alignment stays inside the box when it fits; content wider than the box now overflows symmetrically past both edges, as PowerPoint draws it (the old clamp is gone). Empty lines carry no ink and stay out of the block, so a trailing empty paragraph can't skew the centring. Vertical text and multi-column bodies are untouched — centring was already unimplemented for them (comment states it plainly now).

**Tests** (`anchorctr_centres_the_text_block`, font-metric independent): the drawn block's centre equals the box centre for right-aligned, left-aligned, trailing-empty-paragraph, mixed-alignment, and symmetrically-overflowing configurations; plus a no-anchorCtr control pinning right-alignment at the box edge. Verified visually with `render` on the public fixture: before, the sentence was cut at "…rig"; after, the whole sentence is centred. ROADMAP progress-log row added.

title: Add Craft AI: the family's built-in local assistant (Gemma 4 catalogue, loopback runtimes, shared models folder)
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
## What this is

**Craft AI** — one assistant across the ArtCraft family, as a pane in DeckCraft. It talks to a local model runtime on this machine and never to a cloud service:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Local and private** | Every request is `http://127.0.0.1` — Ollama (11434), LM Studio (1234) or llama.cpp's server (8080), whichever answers. No account, no key, no telemetry, and no address a cloud service could be reached at exists in the code. |
| **Light by design** | No inference engine, no weights, no GPU code enters the app. The runtime the user already has (or installs) does the running — Craft AI is a loopback conversation. |
| **Optional** | Without a runtime or a model the pane says so and touches nothing beyond loopback. Downloading is a button, never a default. |
| **Specialised** | The system prompt tells the model it is inside DeckCraft and names this app's world — slides and layouts, masters and placeholders, speaker notes, charts on slides, pptx and pdf export — so answers are about this app, not generic advice. The ready-made tasks (tighten slide text, speaker notes, outline into slides, review the flow, title suggestions) are framed for it, with the honesty clause: never invent menu or slide names. |
| **One download serves every app** | The model file lands in a shared folder the whole family reads — `<data_home>/ArtCraft/Craft AI/models` — so a model downloaded here is already there in every other ArtCraft app, no second download. Ollama's own store works the same way machine-wide. |

## The three tabs

- **Assistant** — runtime and model pickers, the task, the question, the answer; the conversation is kept, copyable, and Arabic answers are drawn through the same visual-order pass as the rest of the Arabic interface. Worker thread, so the UI never blocks; a busy timer ticks while the model thinks.
- **Models** — the Gemma 4 catalogue, every figure from the model's own card: **E2B** (3.1 GB, 4 GB RAM) for the lightest machines, **E4B** (5.0 GB, 6 GB),…

title: Render: a cropped picture keeps its resolution (Intersect no longer blurs it)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #762

## Cause

`paint::picture` asked `images::decode_for` for a pixmap sized to the picture's **box** on screen. A cropped picture shows only part of the image, magnified to fill the box, so the image was decoded (and downscaled) to a fraction of the resolution it is drawn at, then stretched back up. Merge Shapes ▸ Intersect crops the picture to the new, smaller box (`recrop`), so the result looked blurred. The same happened to any picture with a large crop.

## Fix

Compute the destination rectangle (the whole image after crop and fill rect) first and size the decode from it. Tiled fills keep sizing from the box as before. The decode cache still buckets by power of two and caps the size.

## Tests

- New `a_cropped_picture_is_decoded_at_the_resolution_of_the_whole_image` (render): a 1024 px image of 2 px stripes, cropped to its top-left sixteenth in a 64 pt box at scale 1. Fails on main (0 of 1936 pixels black or white, all grey), passes with the fix.
- `cargo test -p deckcraft-render`: 172 passed.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy -D warnings, test, assets and layers pass locally. The wasm step was not run: the local (Gentoo) Rust toolchain has no wasm32 std. The change touches no wasm-specific code.

title: Preferences: Interface size applies when the slider is let go
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #767

## Cause

The Preferences dialog set `app.ui.ui_scale` on every frame the Interface size slider `changed()`. While dragging, the whole interface (the slider included) rescaled under the pointer, so the slider kept moving away from or towards the pointer and ran to one of its ends.

## Fix

While the pointer is held on the slider, its value waits in the dialog's fields (`uiScale`) and the interface size is left alone; it is applied on release. Keyboard changes (arrow keys on the focused slider) apply at once, as before.

User-visible change: the interface no longer resizes live during the drag; it resizes once when the slider is let go.

## Tests

- New `interface_size_applies_when_the_slider_is_let_go` (ui-egui, egui_kittest): opens Preferences, drags the slider from its left end to its right end, checks that `ui_scale` doesn't change while held and that it grows once the pointer is released. On main it fails with "nothing rescales while the slider is held"; with the fix it passes.

- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy -D warnings, test, assets and layers pass locally. The wasm step was not run: the local (Gentoo) Rust toolchain has no wasm32 std. The change touches no wasm-specific code.

## Note

#267 (shared craft-ui sliders) swaps this slider for `craft_ui::slider::Slider` and would conflict on these lines; the same pending-until-release handling carries over to that widget.

title: Add deckcraft-hub: the CraftHub client path (the v3 adapter, spec §3.6 phase C / §18.4 row 3)
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
## What this is

`deckcraft-hub` — the app-side binding that speaks the generalized collaboration core ([`craft-collab`](https://github.com/hasan-sdaif/crafthub), extracted from figcraft's proven `figcraft-collab` and proposed as `storytold/craft-libs#128`). This is DeckCraft's row of the adoption table — "frames like FigCraft", third in the §18.4 order, with the presence projection this row names: **the active slide**, and the live presentation riding the spotlight signal (`hub.follow`).

Nothing here changes user-visible behavior. The session wiring (a v3 `NetLink` behind the app's `crafthub` feature flag, default off) lands as the pilot follow-up once this contract is reviewed.

## The honest map

DeckCraft's model maps directly: slides hold shapes, groups hold shapes, every shape carries a persistent id.

- **Slides** hang under the root; their fields (`layout`, `background`, `transition`, speaker notes, slide comments, …) sync as properties with the compile-time guard that a new saved field must decide how it syncs.
- **Shapes** sync their 21 fields under their slide (or their group, recursively), ordered by fractional sibling keys — an insertion in the middle costs exactly one key (tested), never a renumbering.
- **A group's `kind` property carries its payload without its children** — the children sync as their own objects. Double-writing them (inside the kind payload *and* as child objects) duplicates the children on every remote apply; the integration suite caught exactly that and the tests pin it.
- The presentation level syncs as whole-value LWW scalars (`slideSize`, `show`, `sections`, the masters for the first cut — master edits during live sessions are rare; splitting per entry is the documented follow-up). `media` never syncs as data: media bytes ride the asset channel (spec §3.5).

DeckCraft's `u32` shape/slide ids have no room for the protocol's 64-bit client-space ids (which exist so two concurrently cre…

title: Text: edit equations inline and return to normal text with Right Arrow
author: hajdukste
body:
> **Status: draft interaction prototype.** The behavior has been ported onto #55's native OMML foundation in [shuff57/deckcraft#1](https://github.com/shuff57/deckcraft/pull/1). Please review that follow-up for the proposed shared implementation. This PR is retained for its discussion and working prototype; it is not proposed as a parallel equation system.

## Problem

Insert → Equation currently uses a one-off dialog and produces ordinary italic text. It does not provide an equation field that can be edited directly on the slide, and there is no clear boundary for returning to normal text.

- **Right Arrow at the equation's end** exits equation mode without inserting a space or skipping following text. Subsequent text uses the surrounding prose formatting, so math italics do not leak. Left Arrow at that boundary reenters the equation.
- Preserve regions through editing, undo/redo, native saves, and DeckCraft PPTX round-trips. Field shading is editor-only.

The engine owns insertion and caret behavior; the UI reads the active field for the ribbon and shading. Older `app.dialog` equation calls route to the new insertion command. Help and parity notes are updated.

title: Text: show gray list markers before typing
author: hajdukste
body:

title: Grow table merges to include merged areas they overlap
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/model/src/table.rs:224 (Table::merge)` (no existing issue): Table merge over an existing merge leaves orphaned hidden covered cells.

## Cause
`Table::merge` reset the span of every cell inside the requested rectangle but ignored existing merges reaching past its edge. When a new merge took in only the anchor of an older merge, that anchor went back to span 1. The older merge's other cells kept their `h_merge`/`v_merge` flags, so they stayed hidden with no anchor covering them, and their text could not be reached.

## Fix
Before resetting cells, `Table::merge` now keeps growing the target rectangle to the union of every anchor span that overlaps it, until the rectangle stops changing. Overlapped merges are absorbed whole and their text moves into the new anchor.

## Verified
- Regression test `merging_over_an_existing_merge_takes_it_in`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-model --lib merging_over_an_existing_merge_takes_it_in`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
Merges that do not overlap an existing merged area work exactly as before. `Table::split` and the `table.merge` command are unchanged.

title: Text: size empty lines by their line break or paragraph mark (#780)
author: GhostMitra
body:
### Summary
Fixes #780.

Previously, empty lines inside a paragraph (e.g. between two \<a:br/>\ line breaks, or trailing after a line break before paragraph end) were sized by the paragraph's first run font size (\lead_size\).

In PowerPoint, each line's height is determined by the mark that ends it:
- A line ended by \<a:br/>\ is sized by that break's run properties (\:rPr/@sz\).
- An empty line at the end of the paragraph (or an empty paragraph) is sized by the paragraph mark properties (\:endParaRPr/@sz\).

### Changes
1. **\crates/text/src/lib.rs\**:
   - Added \end_size\ and \end_face\ to \ParaShaped\, resolved via \esolve::run\ on \para.end_props\ in \shape_para\.
   - In \layout_scaled\, if a line ends at an \<a:br/>\ / \\n\ break cell, sized the line using that break's font size and font face.
   - For empty lines where \size == 0.0\, if the line ends at or past the cell buffer (\l.end >= p.cells.len()\), sized using \(&p.end_face, p.end_size)\ rather than falling back to \lead_size\.
2. **\crates/text/src/tests.rs\**:
   - Added comprehensive regression test \empty_line_height_follows_break_or_end_para_mark\ verifying all scenarios from #780 (Box A, Box B, Box C).

### Verification
- \cargo test -p deckcraft-text\ passed (all 81 tests).
- \cargo test -p deckcraft-pptx\ passed.
- \cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings\ passed cleanly.
- \cargo fmt --all -- --check\ passed.
- \cargo xtask assets\ & \cargo xtask layers\ passed.

title: Text: an empty line takes the size of the mark that ends it
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #780, reported by @KNUFFIXX.

## The bug

An empty line inside a paragraph — the line between two `a:br`, or the last line after a trailing one — was laid out at the size of the paragraph's **first run**. PowerPoint sizes it by the mark that *closes* the line: the `a:rPr` of the `a:br` that ends it, or `a:endParaRPr` for the paragraph's last line. Every line below then sits too high or too low by the difference, which in the reported poster deck drifted text by up to 173 pt.

`shape_para` resolved one `lead_size`/`lead_face` per paragraph, and `layout_scaled` used it for every line with no measured cells.

## The fix

The closing mark was already to hand. A break is a cell (`'\u{b}'`), and `break_lines` sets a line's `end` to that break's own index, so:

```rust
let brk = p.cells.get(rl.end).filter(|c| c.ch == '\u{b}').and_then(|c| p.styles.get(c.style));
let (face, sz) = match brk {
    Some(st) => (&st.face, st.size),
    None if rl.end >= p.cells.len() => (&p.end_face, p.end_size),
    // Anything else empty (a line of tabs alone) keeps the old measure.
    None => (&p.lead_face, p.lead_size),
};
```

`ParaShaped` now carries `end_size`/`end_face` for the paragraph mark, beside the existing lead pair. The third arm is deliberate: only the two cases PowerPoint defines change, so any other way a line can measure empty behaves exactly as before.

An empty **paragraph** already landed on `end_props` through `lead`, so it is untouched — it is the control case in the report, and its test passes both before and after this change.

23 lines of `crates/text/src/lib.rs`.

## Measured on the reported fixture

`deckcraft-cli render --slide 0 --scale 1`, top of the ink of the first and second text line in each box (1 px = 1 pt), against PowerPoint's own export of the same slide:

| Box | PowerPoint | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| A — empty line closed by a 10 pt break | 70, 131 | 70, **166** (+35) | 70, **130** (−1) |
| B — empty last line, `endParaRPr` 10 pt | 7…

title: format.font: set the East Asian and complex-script typefaces too
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #786.

## The bug

A run carries a typeface per script (ECMA-376 §21.1.2.3): `a:latin`, `a:ea` and `a:cs`. `font()` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs` assigned only `r.font`:

```rust
format_run(s, &move |r| r.font = Some(f.clone()))
```

So a CJK run kept drawing — and saving — in whatever `a:ea` named before. As the report puts it, an imported deck can look right in the editor while the saved PPTX still asks another viewer for the old East Asian font.

## The change

`eastAsia` and `complexScript` are settable beside `family`, as the reporter proposed:

```json
{"command":"format.font","params":{"family":"Lato","eastAsia":"Noto Sans CJK SC","complexScript":"Noto Sans Arabic"}}
```

**Additive on purpose.** Left out, the two keep their value, so a Latin-only call means exactly what it did before — that is pinned by a test rather than left to inspection. Names are trimmed and must be 1–200 characters, which is the bound `format.fontDialog` already applies to `family`, so the two commands agree on what a typeface name may be.

The catalog entry now reads `{family, eastAsia?: family, complexScript?: family}` and says which OOXML element each one sets, since the Latin-only behaviour was the surprise.

## Tests

Both fail without the change.

- `format_font_sets_the_east_asian_and_complex_script_typefaces` — sets all three, then checks a Latin-only call leaves the other two alone, then goes **end to end**: saves to PPTX, asserts `<a:ea typeface="Noto Sans CJK SC"/>` and `<a:cs .../>` are in the slide XML, reopens the bytes and asserts they survived. That last part is what the report is actually about, so it seemed worth asserting against the file rather than the model.
- `format_font_rejects_an_unusable_typeface_name` — a blank `family`, an empty `eastAsia`, a 201-character `complexScript`; and that `"  Lato  "` is accepted trimmed.

## Two things I left alone, deliberately

- **`format.fontDialog` has the same gap.** `FontEdits::write` also assigns only `r.font…

title: Keep bare '&' text when pasting HTML instead of dropping it
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/richclip.rs:257-283 (decode_text)` (no existing issue): HTML paste drops text from a bare '&' up to the next ';' (e.g. "R&D costs; up" becomes "R up").

## Cause
`decode_text` treated every '&' as the start of an entity and took everything up to the next ';' as its name. If that span wasn't a known entity or numeric reference, it was silently dropped, so `R&D costs; up` became `R up`.

## Fix
`decode_text` now consumes the text up to ';' only when it decodes to a known named entity or a valid numeric reference. Otherwise it emits the '&' literally and keeps scanning from the next character, so the rest of the text stays as typed.

## Verified
- Regression test `bare_ampersand_keeps_text_up_to_next_semicolon`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib bare_ampersand`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The named entities supported are unchanged (amp, lt, gt, quot, apos, nbsp). Unknown but well-formed entities such as `©` are now kept as typed instead of dropped. I did not add new entities.

title: Keep multi-paragraph slide titles on one line in outline export
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/format/src/lib.rs:490` (no existing issue): Outline export writes a multi-paragraph slide title as several lines, so re-importing the outline splits one slide into several.

## Cause
`slides_to_outline` wrote `Slide::title()` directly. That joins title paragraphs with '\n', so a two-paragraph title became two unindented lines. `outline_to_slides` starts a new slide at every unindented line, so re-importing split one slide into two.

## Fix
`slides_to_outline` now replaces '\n' in the title with a space. This matches how it already treats line breaks. Each title stays on one line, and the export→import round trip keeps the slide count.

## Verified
- Regression test `outline_export_keeps_multi_paragraph_title_on_one_line`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-format --lib outline_export_keeps_multi_paragraph_title_on_one_line`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`Slide::title()` and `TextBody::text()` are unchanged, because thumbnails and navigation use them and rely on the '\n' separator. Body paragraph export is unchanged.

title: Keep leading '-', '*' and '•' text when importing outlines
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/format/src/lib.rs:421` (no existing issue): Outline import deletes leading '-', '*' and '•' from slide titles and bullet text (e.g. "-5 °C" becomes "5 °C").

## Cause
`outline_to_slides` ran `trim_start_matches(['-', '*', '•'])` on every line. That removed every leading dash, asterisk and bullet even when no space followed, so real text was deleted: "-5 °C tonight" became "5 °C tonight" and "--verbose flag" became "verbose flag".

## Fix
Only one leading '-', '*' or '•' is now stripped, and only when a space or tab follows it, which matches how the Markdown importer's `md_list_item` treats list markers. Any other text is kept as it is.

## Verified
- Regression test `outline_keeps_leading_dash_text`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-format --lib outline_keeps_leading_dash_text`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The Markdown import path and `slides_to_outline` export stay the same. Lines that really start with a marker followed by a space (for example "- Point") are still read as bullets, so their marker is still dropped on import.

title: Don't paste HTML text as bold when <b> sets font-weight:normal
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/richclip.rs:187` (no existing issue): Paste from HTML: text inside <b style="font-weight:normal"> is pasted bold (affects all Google Docs pastes).

## Cause
`tag_style` made every `<b>` and `<strong>` bold, and it only used the `style` attribute to turn bold on, never off. Google Docs wraps every copied fragment in `<b style="font-weight:normal">`, so `html_to_body` marked all text pasted from Google Docs as bold.

## Fix
`weight_bold` now returns whether a `font-weight` value turns bold on, turns it off, or is not set. `bold` and numbers from 600 up turn bold on. `normal`, `lighter` and numbers below 600 turn it off. `tag_style` uses that result to override the tag's default bold, so `<b style="font-weight:normal">` and `<b style="font-weight:300">` are no longer bold. A plain `<b>` and a `<span style="font-weight:700">` are still bold.

## Verified
- Regression test `google_docs_normal_weight_wrapper_is_not_bold`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib google_docs_normal_weight_wrapper_is_not_bold`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
The counter-based nesting model is unchanged, so a non-bold span inside a bold `<b>` still inherits bold. `bolder` still turns bold on, as before, without looking at the parent's weight. No test was added for `edit.paste`, which passes the parsed body through as is.

body:
## Summary

Fixes to editing Korean text on slides.

- **Fonts named in Korean are found.** Decks made on Korean systems name fonts like "맑은 고딕" or "나눔고딕". The font catalog now keeps each family's names in other languages. `FontDb::canonical` maps them back to the family, so those runs no longer fall back to another face.
- **The Font box sets the East Asian font for East Asian fonts.** `format.font` used to set only the Latin font, so picking a Korean font left the Hangul unchanged. When the chosen family's own face has Hangul, kana or CJK ideographs, the run's `font_ea` is set too. A stand-in face for a missing family never counts. A Latin-only font still changes only the Latin font.
- **Korean words, not syllables.** Hangul counted as an ideograph, so Ctrl+arrow, Ctrl+Backspace/Delete and double-click worked one syllable at a time, and Ctrl+B inside a word didn't bold it. Korean separates words with spaces, so Hangul is now a word character. Line wrapping already treated it that way.
- **Spelling.** Typed Hangul usually carries the deck's English language tag, so an installed English dictionary flagged every Korean word. Hangul words are now checked as `ko-KR`:
  - They are skipped unless a Korean dictionary is installed.
  - A run counts as Korean by its primary language subtag, so `kok` (Konkani) is not Korean.
  - Hangul written next to other letters ("PPT발표") is checked separately from them.
- **Shaping and line breaking.**
  - Hangul shapes with language `ko` and kana with `ja`, so fonts pick their local forms.
  - Hangul Jamo Extended-B and halfwidth Hangul (U+FFA0–FFDC) count as Hangul.
  - Line breaking now uses the same Hangul check, so a halfwidth Korean word isn't split.

Hanja conversion (the Hanja key during composition) already works through the IME; it was checked by hand with the Windows 11 Korean IME (한 → 韓).

### Scope change

This PR first also fixed an IME bug. A click or command while a syllable was composing settled it in the slide but not i…

title: Preferences: checkboxes and slider rails show in light mode
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #766.

`theme::apply` fills inactive widgets with `field_bg`, which is white in the light theme, and draws them without an outline. An unchecked checkbox (and radio) box and a slider rail use exactly that fill, so in the white Preferences dialog "Dark appearance" and the "Interface size" rail disappeared (so did the zoom slider's rail in the status bar). This adds `control` tokens for those fills: light grey (#D6D6D6) at rest, a step darker under the pointer (#C8C8C8) and pressed (#BCBCBC), so hovering darkens the control instead of lightening it. Dark mode keeps its current values. Buttons and the ribbon are unchanged because they draw with `weak_bg_fill`, which this doesn't touch. Text fields are unchanged too, since they use `extreme_bg_color`. I went with a fill rather than an outline like GridCraft's because an inactive outline would also frame every ribbon button. Happy to switch to other greys or to an outline if you prefer.

Validation:
- `theme::tests::light_checkboxes_and_slider_rails_stand_out_from_their_background`: fails on main (`control fill #FF_FF_FF_FF is too close to the dialog background #FF_FF_FF_FF`), passes here. It also checks that rest, hover and pressed darken in turn
- Rendered the Preferences dialog and the main window offscreen with egui_kittest, before and after: the checkbox boxes and slider rails now show, and the ribbon looks the same
- `cargo test -p deckcraft-ui-egui --lib theme::tests::`, `cargo clippy -p deckcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Canvas: the resize cursor follows the handle's rotated diagonal (#745)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #745.

**What was wrong.** The resize cursor was picked from a fixed handle-to-cursor table: handle 0 always showed the NW-SE arrows, handle 2 the NE-SW arrows, and so on. That is correct for unrotated shapes, but resize handles sit on the shape's transformed corners - after rotating a shape 45°, the NW corner's drag axis runs along the *other* diagonal, and the cursor pointed the wrong way.

**The fix** (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`): the cursor is chosen from the handle's resize axis mapped through the shape's transform. For each handle the axis direction is rotated with the shape's affine (rotation and flips), and the closest of the four resize cursors is picked by angle. Unrotated shapes get exactly the same cursors as before (the affine's linear part is the identity for rotation = 0, no flips); rotated and flipped shapes get the cursor that matches where the drag actually goes.

Two details the first version of the fix got wrong, found by a review:

- The direction was taken from the box centre to the handle, so a wide rectangle's corner pointed almost along an edge - a 400x80 shape's NW corner showed a *horizontal* cursor. A corner drags along the diagonal whatever the shape's proportions, so the direction is normalised (the diagonal at 45 degrees) and only the rotation and flips turn it.
- The cursor read the shape's own box, but the handles are drawn from the effective one, which a placeholder inherits from its layout. Such a placeholder showed the default arrow instead of a resize cursor.

**Tests (red-proof).** Three tests in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`:

- `resize_cursor_tracks_rotation` - a square shape at 0°, 45° and 90° rotation across all eight handles. With the handle direction no longer mapped through the shape's transform (the old fixed mapping) the 45° and 90° assertions fail.
- `a_wide_shape_keeps_its_corner_cursors_diagonal` - a 400x80 rectangle keeps the diagonal cursors on its corners. With the aspect ratio back in the direction, th…

title: Design: Browse for Themes brings a template's slide master and layouts (#807)
author: Faabyy
body:
Closes #807

## What changes

Design › Browse for Themes… with a `.pptx` or `.potx` now brings the file's **slide master and layouts**, as PowerPoint does. Before, only the theme part (colours, fonts, effects) was taken, so a company template couldn't be applied to an existing deck.

- The file's first master and its layouts replace the master the current slide uses. A master marked Preserve stays beside the new one.
- A template made for another slide size (4:3 into 16:9, say) stretches to the deck's size, as Slide Size does for masters.
- Each slide on the old master moves to the new layout with the **same name**, else the **same kind**, else Title and Content, else the first. Content is kept and placeholders are matched with `slide::apply_layout`, the same code the Layout command uses.
- In Slide Master view the selection moves to the new master.
- One undo step.
- A `.thmx` still brings its theme only. Its master and layouts aren't read yet (noted in `docs/file-format-parity.md`).

Reuse Slides (Keep Source Formatting) already copied a source master with its media and fresh ids. That code moved into `reuse::import_master`, so both commands share it. Reuse Slides behaves as before.

## Open questions for maintainers

Happy to change any of these:

1. **Which masters are replaced.** Only the master the current slide uses (as `design.browseTheme` already chose for the theme). PowerPoint's Apply to All Slides would replace every master. Should there be an `all` parameter, or should that be the default?
2. **Slide-level placeholder positions.** `apply_layout` clears a matched placeholder's own `xfrm`, so a title moved by hand on one slide follows the new layout. Without that, many templates wouldn't take effect at all. Should they be kept instead?
3. **Stretching.** Master shapes stretch non-uniformly (like Slide Size), so a 4:3 logo gets wider on 16:9. Would you rather keep the aspect ratio of pictures?

title: Format: format.font accepts eastAsia and complexScript faces (#786)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #786.

**What was wrong.** `format.font` only set the Latin typeface. A CJK presentation edited through the CLI or MCP could look correct on screen while the saved PPTX still asked for the old East Asian font, because the model's `font_ea` and `font_cs` fields were never written by the command.

**The fix** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs`): `format.font` accepts optional `eastAsia` and `complexScript` parameters. Without them, the existing script faces are kept - the same Latin-only behaviour as before, so existing callers are unaffected. The pptx reader and writer already handle the ea/cs typefaces; this wires the command layer to them.

A script face that is not a family name is refused with a value error rather than ignored: the caller asked for a face and would otherwise get a silent "done" without it.

**Tests (red-proof).** `crates/engine/src/tests.rs`:

- `format_font_east_asian_and_complex_script` - explicit ea/cs sets all three faces, a Latin-only call keeps the existing script faces, and setting one script face leaves the other untouched. With the ea/cs assignment removed from the command, the first assertion fails (the East Asian face stays `None`).
- `format_font_refuses_a_script_face_that_is_not_a_name` - a number where a family name belongs is refused and nothing changes. With the value error removed, the test fails: the command reports success and changes the Latin face.

**Gate.** `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p deckcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the engine suite (334 tests, 1 ignored) pass locally on Windows. `gates (ubuntu-latest)` is the authority.

ROADMAP progress-log row added.

title: engine: a hostile text selection can't drive paragraph commands past the body
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A text selection is caller-controlled data: `text.select` stores the raw caret (`crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs:633`), and `clamp_selection` never touches `TextSel.anchor`/`caret` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs:687`). Paragraph commands then use those positions directly as loop bounds:

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs:695` (`format.case`): `for pi in a.0..=b.0`
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs:420` (`text.insert`): `for pi in at.0..=c.0`
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs:744` (`paste_body`): `for pi in at.0..=c.0`
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs:1331` (`format_para`, shared by every paragraph command): `for pi in a.0..=b.0`

With a selection like `{"anchor": [0,0], "caret": [18446744073709551615, 0]}` — reachable from any control-channel / MCP client — `a.0..=b.0` iterates toward `usize::MAX` on the UI thread (hang), and `text.selectParagraph` (`text.rs:1151`) evaluates `at.0 + 1`, an overflow panic in debug builds.

**Fix:** clamp each range at the edited body's last paragraph (`body.paragraphs.len().saturating_sub(1)`) and use `saturating_add(1)` for the single-position arithmetic. A hostile selection now resolves against the body instead of spinning.

**Regression test:** `paragraph_commands_clamp_a_hostile_text_selection` — on main it fails with `attempt to add with overflow` at `cmd/text.rs:1151`; with the patch it passes, and the full `deckcraft-engine` lib suite is green (313 passed).

This resolves the text-selection-hang finding from the retired audit #727 (the other findings there were superseded by #750).

title: Format: .txt and .md outline includes table cell text (#814)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #814.

**What was wrong.** `slides_to_outline` only looked at `sh.text`, which regular text boxes and placeholders carry. Tables store their text in cells inside `ShapeKind::Table`, so `convert to .txt` or `.md` silently skipped every table cell — exit 0, no warning.

**The fix** (`crates/format/src/lib.rs`, ~7 lines): the outline now walks into tables after the regular text: each table row becomes a tab-separated line (multi-paragraph cell text flattened with spaces, soft hyphens replaced as for body text).

**Tests:** a deck with a text box and a 2×2 table — the outline contains all three text sources, with the cell texts tab-separated per row. Verified with the issue's python-pptx repro: the four cell texts appear after the slide title and text box body. ROADMAP progress-log row added.

title: Read a newline in pasted HTML text as a space
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/richclip.rs:257-283 (decode_text)` (no existing issue): Paste from HTML: a newline inside text is deleted instead of read as a space, so words run together and bold/italic is lost. ## Cause `decode_text` deleted every `\n` and `\r` from HTML text, but HTML treats a line break as whitespace. `

Hello\nworld

` became "Helloworld", so `same_words` rejected the HTML against the plain text "Hello world". The paste then fell back to plain text and lost bold, italic and underline. ## Fix `decode_text` now collapses each run of HTML whitespace (spaces, tabs, line breaks) to one space. `html_to_body` drops a space at the start of a paragraph or after another space, and `new_para` and the end of parsing drop a trailing space. Source-wrapped HTML such as `

\nHello\nworld\n

` therefore gives "Hello world" with the formatting kept. ## Verified - Regression tests `cmd::richclip::tests::a_newline_in_html_text_is_a_space`, `tests::html_paste_with_a_source_newline_keeps_its_bold`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib newline`). - `cargo xtask ci` passes. ## Not changed Entity handling, `same_words`, and the paste logic in `edit.rs` are unchanged. ` ` still decodes to a plain space, so it can be trimmed when it sits at a paragraph edge or next to another space. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved whitespace handling when pasting HTML, including collapsing consecutive whitespace and trimming spaces at paragraph starts, before paragraph breaks, and at the end of the document. * Preserved nonbreaking spaces and blank paragraphs during HTML paste, while retaining surrounding rich-text formatting. * Fixed formatting loss when bold text includes a source newline.

title: Keep slide.duplicate copies next to their source in the section
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/slide.rs:217-220` (no existing issue): slide.duplicate appends the copy to the end of the section's slide list, so the sorter shows it away from the original.

## Cause
`slide.duplicate` inserted the copy into `doc.slides` right after the source, but pushed its id onto the end of the section's own `slides` list. For a section with several slides the two orders disagreed, so the sorter and section zoom showed the copy at the end of the section.

## Fix
After adding the copy to its section, `slide.duplicate` re-sorts that section's slide list by document order, the same way `slide.move` does. The copy now sits right after its source, including when several slides are duplicated at once.

## Verified
- Regression test `duplicate_keeps_section_order_in_step_with_slides`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib duplicate_keeps_section_order_in_step_with_slides`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`slide.new`, `slide.move` and the sorter and section-zoom code are unchanged. Sections that `slide.duplicate` doesn't touch are not re-sorted.

title: Canvas: the first click on a text box selects it - a second click enters text editing (#787, #764)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #787 and #764.

**What was wrong.** Clicking an unselected text box or placeholder took the caret straight into text editing, bypassing selection. The shape could not be moved, duplicated or deleted without pressing Escape first - the first click went to the caret instead of the selection.

**The fix** (`crates/engine/src/tools.rs`): `is_text_first`, which made text boxes and placeholders skip selection, is removed from the pointer-down hit-test condition. Text boxes now follow the same select-then-edit flow as every other shape: the first click selects the shape, a second click on the text enters edit mode. Tables already required selection before the caret could enter a cell; that path is unchanged.

**Tests (red-proof).**

- `crates/engine/src/tests.rs`: `click_into_placeholder_starts_editing` checks the first click selects and the second one starts editing. With `is_text_first` back it fails - the first click starts editing.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`: `empty_bullet_preview_follows_click_type_enter_and_toggle` now checks the same two steps in the editor. It only clicked twice before, which passed with the old behaviour too, because the first click went straight into text editing; it now asserts the first click selects and does not start typing, and fails on the old behaviour.
- `crates/engine/src/tests.rs`: `bullet_preview_after_enter` - the paragraph that Enter adds keeps the bullet. With the bullet not inherited by the new paragraph it fails.
- `crates/text/src/tests.rs`: `empty_bullet_paragraph_produces_a_preview_bullet` - the text crate produces the empty-paragraph bullet preview the editor draws. With the pre-#811 layout (no bullet on an empty paragraph) it fails.

**Gate.** `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p deckcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the engine (333 tests, 1 ignored), text (81 tests) and ui-egui (216 tests, 4 ignored) suites pass locally on Windows. One ui-egui run aborted in the test binary with `0xc0000005` …

title: Add slides from an outline to the section of the slide they follow
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/slide.rs:~393 (from_outline), crates/format/src/lib.rs:225 (add_outline_slides)` (no existing issue): slide.fromOutline (Insert > Slides from Outline) adds slides that belong to no section when the deck has sections.

## Cause
`slide.fromOutline` moved the imported slides into `doc.slides` after the current slide but never added their ids to any `Section.slides`. In a deck with sections, the imported slides belonged to no section.

## Fix
After moving the imported slides, `from_outline` inserts their ids into the section of the slide before them, right after that slide. If there is no preceding slide, or the preceding slide is in no section, the ids go to the start of the first section. This covers both plain and markdown import.

## Verified
- Regression test `slides_from_outline_join_the_section_of_the_slide_they_follow`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine slides_from_outline`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`add_outline_slides` in the format crate and `section.move` are unchanged. `section.move` still sorts slides that are in no section to the end of the deck.

title: Shapes: Edit Points — Straight/Curved Segment and Open/Close Path from the right-click menu
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
In Edit Points you can now right-click a segment for Straight Segment / Curved Segment, and a point for Open Path / Close Path.

This adds to the Edit Points menu that #514/#515 started. As in PowerPoint, right-clicking a segment gives the segment menu and right-clicking a point gives the point menu. Curved Segment adds handles at the segment's thirds, so it keeps its shape until you drag a handle. Straight Segment drops the handles. Open Path breaks a closed outline at the point: the outline then starts and ends there, as two points you can drag apart. Close Path joins the two ends with a straight segment, or merges them into one point if they already meet. Each change is one undo step. All of it goes through commands (`shape.segmentType`, `shape.openPath`, `shape.closePath`), and `shape.points` now also reports each segment's type. The right click records the point or segment in the engine (`context_click`), so the CLI and MCP pick it the same way. What's still missing from PowerPoint's menu is Delete Segment and Add Point (Ctrl/Cmd-click already adds a point), so the checklist row stays partial. Happy to follow up with Delete Segment / Add Point. Fill and line style don't change when a path is opened or closed. Happy to switch if you'd rather an open outline lose its fill. Docs: the gaps entry and the ui-parity row now list what's left, plus a ROADMAP log line.

Validation:
- `edit_points_straight_and_curved_segments`, `edit_points_open_and_close_path`, `edit_points_right_click_picks_the_point_or_the_segment`: fail on main (`segments` is null, `shape.openPath` is unknown, the right click picks no segment), pass here
- `canvas::tests::edit_points_menu_sets_segment_types_and_opens_the_path` (kittest): right-click a segment, then Curved Segment; right-click a point, then Open Path and Close Path
- `cargo clippy -p deckcraft-engine -p deckcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: Canvas layout: a canvas-first shell beside the ribbon
author: jason4short
body:
**PR 1 of 7** in a stack bringing the canvas layout to DeckCraft:

1. #835 Canvas layout: a canvas-first shell beside the ribbon (this PR)
2. #836 Editing shortcuts, paste, panel fields and document tabs
3. #837 Placeholders, slide masters and the states strip
4. #838 Groups, deep select and panel views
5. #839 Number fields, colour picker, distances, dialogs and the Mac menu bar
6. #840 One set of views, Find, and video in slide shows
7. #841 Animation states, in-canvas previews and Layers collapse

Adds a second, canvas-first layout beside the ribbon, in the style of canvas editors such as Figma Slides. The ribbon layout is unchanged and stays the library's default, so the tests and the web build behave as before. The desktop app opens in the canvas layout until a layout is saved, and `--shell canvas|classic`, `DECKCRAFT_SHELL` and Preferences switch between the two.

The canvas layout has:
- A left sidebar: the slide list, with Layers under it (the Selection pane's list).
- A compact Design inspector on the right (`inspector.rs`, `props.rs`). Its sections depend on what is selected: position and size, text, fill, stroke and effects for shapes, and layout and background for the slide.
- A bottom toolbar with the tools (V, T, shapes, picture and so on).
- An optional pixel unit (2 px per point, Figma Slides' scale) for the panel fields and rulers.

Text styles come from the slide master (`master.textStyle`, engine `cmd/textstyle.rs`). Title, Body, Body 2, Body 3 and Plain text can be edited for the whole deck from the panel, and applying one to selected text is a single command. A Morph-based States view in the Animate tab (`states.rs`) treats a run of slides joined by Morph as one slide with several states. Locked layers can let clicks pass through to what is below (`locked_click_through`).

Nothing changes for PPTX: every edit goes through existing or new commands, and new state is stored the way PowerPoint stores it (master text styles, Morph transitions).

title: Canvas: the Format and Animation Painter override the cursor (#830)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #830.

**What was wrong.** When the Format Painter or Animation Painter was armed, the mouse cursor stayed as the default arrow. The user had no visual indication that the tool was active and waiting for a click on a shape to apply the copied format.

**The fix** (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`): when either painter is armed (`session.painter` or `session.anim_painter` is `Some`), the canvas cursor becomes `CursorIcon::Copy` - the arrow-with-a-plus cursor that conventionally means "carrying something to apply here". The override takes precedence over all other cursor assignments (resize, move, crosshair, text), because the painter's whole purpose at that moment is to receive the next click.

**Tests (red-proof).** Two kittest tests, one per painter: each hovers over the canvas, checks the cursor is not the Copy one yet, arms the painter and checks it is. With the painter override removed, both fail - the cursor stays `Move` instead of `Copy`.

**Gate.** `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p deckcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the ui-egui suite (218 tests, 4 ignored) pass locally on Windows. One earlier run of that suite aborted in the test binary (cargo reported "error: test failed" with no test-result line - the known Windows kittest crash on this machine); three consecutive reruns were clean at 218 passed. `gates (ubuntu-latest)` is the authority.

title: Reject shape ids beyond u32 in shape.connect, sites and points
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/shape.rs:1154 (shape_id, used by connect/sites); same pattern at crates/engine/src/cmd/points.rs:358-359 and :432-433` (no existing issue): shape.connect (and shape.sites, points.* commands) truncate shape ids to u32, so an out-of-range id silently targets a different shape.

## Cause
`shape_id()` in shape.rs and the `target()`/`points()` helpers in points.rs cast the id with `as u32`, which wraps modulo 2^32. An id like `A + 2^32` therefore addressed shape `A` instead of being rejected, as `id_param` does.

## Fix
`shape.connect` (`from`, `to`, `id`), `shape.sites` and the points commands (`shape.points`, `shape.editPoints`, `shape.movePoint`, `shape.addPoint`, `shape.deletePoint`, `shape.pointType`, `shape.moveHandle`) now read ids with `id_param`. An id that is not a valid u32 returns a 'not a valid shape id' error. I removed the `shape_id` helper.

## Verified
- Regression test `shape_ids_beyond_u32_are_rejected_not_wrapped`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib shape_ids_beyond_u32_are_rejected_not_wrapped`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The id that `shape.connect` reads back from its own `shape.insert` call still uses `as u32`. The engine produced that id, so it is always in range. In-range ids and the selection fallback behave as before.

title: Render: quick styles render on empty placeholder text boxes (#832)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #832.

**What was wrong.** The render gate for an empty placeholder's fill checked only `s.fill.is_none()`. A quick style that sets a style reference without an explicit fill (several of the 41 presets return `fill: None`) left `s.fill` as `None`, so the gate skipped the fill even though the shape had been formatted. The style only appeared after text was added.

**The fix** (`crates/render/src/lib.rs`, 1 line): the gate now also checks `s.line.is_none()` and `s.style.is_none()`. If any of the three has a local override, the placeholder is considered formatted and the fill is drawn (resolved from the style reference). A truly unformatted empty placeholder still shows the dashed outline and prompt.

**Tests.** `crates/render/src/tests.rs`: `a_quick_style_fills_an_empty_placeholder` renders an empty body placeholder in the editor with a quick style and checks the accent fill is painted, and that the same placeholder without a style stays white. Red-proof: with the gate reverted to `s.fill.is_none()` alone the first assertion fails - the placeholder stays white (`[255, 255, 255, 255]` instead of the theme's accent) - so the test is red on the unfixed code and green with the fix.

**Gate.** `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p deckcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the render suite (175 tests) pass locally on Windows; `gates (ubuntu-latest)` is the authority.

ROADMAP progress-log row added.

title: PPTX: preserve separate click steps in trigger sequences
author: MMexicann
body:
Addresses the multi-click trigger save defect recorded in [docs/gaps.md](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/main/docs/gaps.md#interactive-decks-media-action-links-audio-triggered-effects-and-click-boxes). Contribution on behalf of @MMexicann.

## Problem and root cause
A button with On Click → Appear and On Click → Disappear should reveal an answer until its second click. Saving to PPTX converted the second effect to After Previous, so the answer disappeared on the first click. The writer explicitly converted every later On Click effect in an interactive sequence, including the expanded effects of a paragraph build.

## Changes
Keep later On Click effects as separate steps while retaining the first step's implicit button click and existing With/After Previous grouping. Add synthetic timing-XML and import → edit → save → reopen tests, plus a headless show regression that toggles the answer twice. title: Review: reject revisions after Compare, one or all
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Review › Compare: Reject and Reject All, the counterpart of Accept

In PowerPoint a change from the compared copy only lands if you accept it; rejecting leaves the original as it is, and Reject All Changes drops every one. DeckCraft lists revisions that disappear once accepted, so here Reject drops a revision from the list without touching the open deck: a rejected inserted slide is never added, a rejected deleted slide stays, a rejected changed slide keeps its current content. Accept All skips what was rejected, and End Review clears the rejections. `review.reject {index | all}` runs it from the CLI/MCP; the Revisions pane gets Reject next to each Accept, plus Reject All. Rejecting isn't an undo step (like Compare and End Review, it changes no slide); happy to make it one if you'd rather, though that means the undo history carrying compare state. Left out: per-object accept/reject, markers on the slide, and a ribbon Reject button (there's no reject glyph yet and End Review already uses the X); docs/gaps.md keeps those.

Validation:
- `compare::tests::reject_keeps_the_open_deck_and_accept_all_skips_rejected_revisions`, `rejecting_one_revision_keeps_the_others_in_order`: fail on main (`UnknownCommand("review.reject")`), pass here
- `compare_tests::reject_all_empties_the_pane_and_keeps_the_deck` (egui_kittest): fails on main (no "Reject All" in the pane), passes here
- `cargo clippy -p deckcraft-engine -p deckcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Format: retain imported chart parts through native saves

body:

Invalid, reused or mixed inline/reference forms are refused. Existing inline sidecars are read and migrated on save.

Current main was merged into this existing branch before the storage fix. Four documentation conflicts retain both the chart-preservation and upstream trigger-click work without changing scores, milestone IDs or estimates. The directly affected format, architecture and progress documentation now describes the ZIP layout and limits.

title: Text: AutoFormat superscripts ordinals (1st, 22nd) as you type
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Typing "1st", "22nd" or "103rd" followed by a space or punctuation now superscripts the suffix, and Tools ▸ AutoCorrect has an option to turn it off.

PowerPoint's AutoFormat as you type has "Ordinals (1st) with superscript", on by default: when a number with an ordinal suffix is followed by a space or punctuation, the suffix becomes superscript; a word like "first" is left alone. This follows it in the same place the fractions rule runs: only for typed text, only for a number with the suffix it takes (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 11th–13th, 21st, 102nd), and only while AutoCorrect is on. The option is `ordinals` in `text.autocorrect` and a checkbox in the AutoCorrect dialog. "1th" or "2st" stay as typed, which is my reading of the feature; happy to switch if you'd rather superscript any st/nd/rd/th after a number. Undoing just the formatting with Cmd+Z (rather than the typed character) is left out, like for the other corrections ("no undo of a single correction" in gaps.md), and automatic bulleted lists are left for another PR.

title: Pictures: crop with handles on the canvas (#823)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Pictures: crop with handles on the canvas, as in PowerPoint

In PowerPoint, Picture Format ▸ Crop puts black handles on the picture's sides and corners. Dragging one trims that side and the picture stays where it is on the slide. Dragging inside moves the picture under the frame, and Esc or a click outside ends cropping. This PR adds that as the first item of the Crop menu (`picture.cropMode`, so it also works from the CLI and MCP). Shift on a corner keeps the frame's proportions. Option trims the opposite side the same way, which is the modifier resizing already uses here for "from the centre". Enter and a double-click end cropping too. Each drag changes the frame and `srcRect` together, so the picture never stretches, and a whole crop session is one undo step. The handles work in the picture's own frame, so they also trim the right side on rotated and flipped pictures and on pictures with a `fillRect`. A crop that would leave nothing visible is not written.

Not covered yet: the cropped-away part is a dashed outline rather than a greyed copy of the picture, there are no white handles to scale the picture inside the crop, and Fill, Fit and Aspect Ratio are missing. Deleting the picture or changing slide ends cropping the same way Edit Points does. The 10%/20% items stay as they were. Happy to switch the Option/Shift mapping if you prefer the Windows Ctrl convention. One more thing I noticed: Size, Rotate and Edit Points also begin their undo step on the press, so a double-click there leaves the step open until the next release. Cropping closes it on the double-click; I left the others alone.

Closes #823

A rotated or flipped picture saved with `rotWithShape="0"` doesn't enter crop mode for now: the renderer doesn't draw it in the shape's frame, so the handles wouldn't line up with what you see. Happy to cover it in a follow-up.

title: Opening a .ppsx from the command line starts the slide show (#862)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Opening a `.ppsx` from the command line or the file association starts the slide show

In PowerPoint a PowerPoint Show (`.ppsx`) always opens in Slide Show view when the system hands it over (double-click, Open With, or passed at launch), while File › Open inside PowerPoint opens it for editing. This PR does the same for the files DeckCraft gets as arguments: when the last one is a `.ppsx` (any case), the show starts full screen from where Play from Start begins (so Set Up Slide Show's range or custom show and hidden slides count); a `.pptx`, or a `.ppsx` followed by another file, opens for editing as before, and File › Open is unchanged. That covers Windows and Linux (the installer and the desktop file already pass the path) and `deckcraft deck.ppsx` from a terminal on macOS. The Finder double-click on macOS arrives as an Apple event that DeckCraft doesn't handle yet; #432 adds that, and its handler can call the new `SlideApp::open_from_system` to get the same behaviour.

One choice: when the show ends (Esc, or a click past the end screen) PowerPoint closes the file, and on Windows quits if it had been started just for it. Here the deck stays open in the editor, which loses nothing and lets you play it again; happy to switch to closing the presentation (and the window when it was the only one) if you'd rather match PowerPoint.

Refs #862

title: Clamp huge index in table.insertRowBelow/insertColumnRight
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs:291` (no existing issue): table.insertRowBelow / insertColumnRight overflow on a huge row/col index (panic in debug, wrong row inserted in release).

## Cause
`rows_cols` computed `r + 1` and `c + 1` on a caller-supplied `usize`. With `usize::MAX` this overflows. Debug builds panic and the engine returns `Internal`. Release builds wrap to 0 and insert at the top.

## Fix
`rowBelow` and `colRight` now use `saturating_add(1)`. `Table::insert_row` and `insert_col` already clamp with `.min(len)`, so a huge index appends at the end. A regression test covers both commands with `u64::MAX`.

## Verified
- Regression test `table_insert_below_or_right_of_a_huge_index_appends_at_the_end`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib table_insert_below_or_right_of_a_huge_index_appends_at_the_end`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
The other table row and column commands (`rowAbove`, `colLeft`, delete) are unchanged. They don't add to the index.

title: Fonts: resolve localized family names and preserve line metrics
author: yuxiaoli
body:
PPTX text using an installed font's localized family name fell back to another face because lookup retained only its English-or-first family name. This could lose the requested family and real bold weight. Retain bounded aliases from OpenType name IDs 1 and 16 in loaded faces and the native catalog, while preserving canonical font menus and legacy weight-family behavior.

Exact canonical families win before alias matches, including available style lists, exact/nearest style ranking and cached variable instances. An alias from another family cannot shadow a canonical family even when its style is a closer match.

Line metrics resolve the configured script families and compare face identity, cached once per paragraph style. An unrelated fallback's matching alias cannot change baseline or line height; explicitly configured script faces still contribute their own metrics.

### Review and upstream integration

- Address the [maintainer asset review](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/pull/874#issuecomment-6251588562) with Rust runtime fixtures derived from the existing minimal sfnt. No new font binaries or Python generators are committed.

The sole conflicted file was `ROADMAP.md`; all upstream entries and the original font progress notes are retained. title: Show: Back leaves a slide whose first animation plays by itself
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #844.

The issue has two separate causes; this PR fixes the first one, Back getting stuck. On a slide whose first animation is With/After Previous, `ShowState::prev` undid that automatic first step, leaving the slide as it was before it appeared. On the same frame the show tick saw an unplayed automatic step and played it again, so Back never got past the slide. Since #631 `ShowState` already starts that step when the slide appears, so now Back treats it as part of the slide appearing: it undoes the click steps, then goes to the previous slide (fully built, as before). The tick no longer starts automatic steps on its own; autoplay previews still do. Left/Up/PageUp/Backspace/P, right-click and the swipe all go through the same `prev`.

What remains of #844 is the extra clicks on paragraph builds: the PPTX importer merges the per-paragraph effects of a build. That's a separate fix in `crates/pptx`, which I'll send next.

If you'd rather Back undo the automatic step on the first slide of the show (where there is nothing to go back to), happy to switch; right now it does nothing there.

Validation:
- `anim::tests::show_back_leaves_a_slide_whose_first_step_is_automatic`: fails on main (`prev` gives `StepBack(0)` instead of `Slide(0)`), passes here
- `ui-egui show::tests::back_leaves_a_slide_whose_first_animation_is_with_previous` (kittest, five ← presses): fails on main (still on slide 2), passes here
- #631's `a_first_animation_after_or_with_previous_plays_when_the_slide_appears` still passes

title: PPTX: paragraph builds edited in PowerPoint keep their clicks
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #844: #882 fixes Back getting stuck, this one the extra clicks; together they close it.

PowerPoint saves a paragraph build as one effect per paragraph, each with its own start, and the importer folded every run of them into a single by-paragraph animation, which the timeline then rebuilds with its own rule (each first-level paragraph on click, sub-points with their parent). That only matches the file when the build was never edited. On the reporter's deck, slide 19 (sub-points that come in with their parent, a picture between paragraphs) took 34 clicks instead of PowerPoint's 10, and slide 36 (a build by 2nd-level paragraphs) took 1 instead of 6. Now the importer folds a run only when the timeline would play exactly the same effects; otherwise it keeps one effect per paragraph with its own start, as it already did for files without `build="p"`. The rule for which paragraphs a build animates moved to `deckcraft_model::anim::paragraph_build_roles`, so the timeline, the reader and the writer all use the same one.

The writer needed two changes to keep the round trip:
- A by-paragraph build now writes sub-points With Previous of their parent. Before, every non-empty paragraph got its own click, and PowerPoint played it that way. Text with no paragraph to animate (only spaces) now gets a whole-shape effect; before, it got `build="p"` with one effect on paragraph 0 that the player ignored.
- Consecutive paragraph effects on one shape now share a `grpId` under one `bldP build="p"`, the way PowerPoint writes them. They used to get a group each, marked `animBg`. They share the group even when their effect or duration differ: reopening in DeckCraft keeps every effect as it was, but I haven't checked how PowerPoint handles mixed effects inside one group.

One side effect to know about: a PPTX saved by DeckCraft before this change, with a by-paragraph build on text with sub-points, will now reimport with one click per sub-point. That is how PowerPoint already plays tho…

title: Export: PNG with a transparent background (#784)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #784

## What

The renderer lays every slide background over white (#275, as PowerPoint does), so a PNG export was always opaque, even with the background's Transparency at 100%. This adds a **Transparent background** option to PNG export that leaves the slide background out (both the white underlay and the background fill), so only what is on the slide is drawn and the rest of the PNG is transparent. - **CLI**: `deckcraft-cli render --transparent`. `run --export out.png --export-params '{"transparentBackground":true}'` works through `file.export`.

Slide Show, PDF and the canvas keep the white underlay, so PowerPoint parity is unchanged.

The checkerboard preview the issue mentions as a bonus is not part of this PR: the canvas keeps showing what the slide show shows.

title: Limit shape.setBounds, shape.resize and shape.move size and position
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/shape.rs:215 (set_bounds; shape.resize at :~183 and shape.move at :~171 have the same problem)` (no existing issue): shape.setBounds / shape.resize accept any size, so a huge height aborts the whole process with an out-of-memory error when the slide is rendered or its points are edited.

## Cause
`shape.setBounds`, `shape.resize` and `shape.move` stored sizes and positions with no upper bound. They only rejected negative and non-finite values. A huge height such as 1e100 on a curved preset then made rendering or point editing try to allocate gigabytes. That aborts the process, and the engine's panic guard cannot catch an abort.

## Fix
Added `clamp_side` (0 to 15,840 pt) and `clamp_pos` (±100,000 pt), using the same `MAX_PT` and `POS_LIMIT` limits as `shape.sizePosition`. `shape.setBounds`, `shape.resize` (including the aspect-locked path, before the rotated re-centering) and `shape.move` now pass their results through these helpers.

## Verified
- Regression test `shape_geometry_commands_limit_size_and_position`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib shape_geometry_commands_limit_size_and_position`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`shape.sizePosition` still rejects out-of-range values with an error. The file loader's own clamping is unchanged. The new test checks the stored values and does not call the renderer.

body:
## What this adds

DrawingML run properties carry `kumimoji` on `a:rPr` (組み文字): per ISO/IEC 29500-1 it "specifies whether the numbers contained within vertical text continue vertically with the text or whether they are to be displayed horizontally while the surrounding characters continue in a vertical fashion. If this attribute is omitted, a value of 0, or false, is assumed."

DeckCraft read and wrote dozens of `a:rPr` attributes but not this one, so it was dropped on open (and therefore gone on save), and East Asian vertical text (`a:bodyPr/@vert="eaVert"`) laid ASCII digits on their side because only ideographs/kana stand upright. A Japanese vertical slide with 組み文字-marked numbers was both lossy and wrong on screen.

- **Model**: `RunProps.kumimoji: Option<bool>` in `crates/model/src/text.rs`, with the spec wording and the Japanese meaning in the doc comment; merged with the other run properties in `RunProps::inherit`.
- **Round trip**: read in `crates/pptx/src/read/dml.rs::rpr()`, written in `crates/pptx/src/write/dml.rs` next to `noProof` (only when `Some`), so `1`, `0` and absent all survive an open + save.
- **Layout**: the per-grapheme upright decision in `crates/text` now honours the flag in East Asian vertical text (`Upright::Cjk`): `is_upright(c) || kumimoji(i)`. Runs without the attribute behave exactly as before, and horizontal text and stacked (`Upright::All`) text are untouched — per the spec the attribute only concerns vertical text.
- **Command**: `format.kumimoji` (`{"on"?: bool}`, label *Combine Characters (Kumimoji)*, `menu: []` like `format.caps` since it is a run property with no ribbon button) toggles the selection's runs; off removes the attribute, which the spec reads as false. It is reachable from the command palette, the control channel, MCP and the CLI.

title: Remap slide links to the copies when reusing slides
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/reuse.rs:~150 (reuse; slides get fresh ids but Action::Slide targets are never remapped)` (no existing issue): Reuse Slides (slide.reuse) leaves internal slide links pointing at the source deck's slide ids, so they jump to an unrelated slide.

## Cause
slide.reuse gives each imported slide a fresh SlideId but left every `Action::Slide` target (shape click/hover actions and text-run links) at the source deck's id. Ids are allocated per document, so the stale id pointed at an unrelated destination slide, or at none.

## Fix
reuse() now records a source-to-copy SlideId map while copying the slides. After all copies exist, it rewrites `Action::Slide` targets and `zoom_return` on shape click/hover, text-run link/hover (shapes, groups, table cells, list styles, notes) to the copies, so forward and backward links both work.

## Verified

- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
Links to a slide that is not among the reused slides keep their old target. The `keepFormatting` master/layout copying is unchanged.
