title: fix(design): propagate Format Background Apply to All to slide masters (#891)
author: kk376
body:
Fixes #891

When invoking `design.background` with `"all": true` (or clicking "Apply to All" in the Format Background pane), it previously only mutated currently existing slides in `doc.slides`, leaving `doc.masters` untouched.

When a user subsequently added a slide (`slide.new`), the new slide had `slide.background = None` and resolved through `layout.background -> master.background`, causing it to revert to the default theme background (e.g. Nocturne's `#121826` instead of `#0D0D0D`).

## Cause
`write_background` only iterated through `doc.slides` when `Target::Slides` and `all == true` were set. Slide masters (`doc.masters`) and layout overrides remained as-is, breaking inheritance for newly created slides. Furthermore, `backgrounds_already` and `copy_slide_background` only checked `doc.slides`, omitting master verification when evaluating idempotent undo boundaries.

## Fix
1. In `write_background`: When `Target::Slides` and `all == true`, propagate the background to all masters in `doc.masters` (`m.background = bg.clone()`) and clear layout overrides (`l.background = None`), matching PowerPoint's "Apply to All" behavior where master inheritance takes over.
2. In `backgrounds_already` and `copy_slide_background`: When `all == true`, verify both slides and masters match `bg` before skipping to preserve idempotent undo steps.
3. Added unit test `background_all_applies_to_master_and_new_slides_inherit` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/design.rs` testing the full flow from #891 (Nocturne theme -> apply `#0D0D0D` to all -> add slide -> inspect verifies `#0D0D0D` -> idempotency -> undo).
4. Updated UI integration test `apply_to_all_copies_the_picture` in `crates/ui-egui/src/background_tests.rs` to verify master background update.

## Verified
- `cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib cmd::design` (8/8 passed)
- `cargo test -p deckcraft-ui-egui --lib background_tests` (3/3 passed)
- `cargo fmt --check` (clean)

title: text: remap symbol-font U+F0xx codes to the installed Symbol face's real Unicode
author: Bryson14
body:
## What

PowerPoint stores a Symbol-font character as U+F0xx with `<a:sym typeface="Symbol"/>` — e.g. U+F0DE is the Symbol font's double arrow (⇒). The layout drew that character from whichever installed face happened to map the private-use code (on macOS that was Wingdings, whose arrow points a different way), because **Apple's "Symbol" on macOS has no private-use cmap at all**: it maps its glyphs to **real Unicode** instead. The test that checked this (`symbol_font_characters_draw_in_the_sym_font`) simply skipped on macOS.

This PR makes DeckCraft **remap the private-use codes (U+F0xx) to the real Unicode characters** Apple's Symbol font draws them at:

- Adds the **Adobe Symbol encoding** table (`unicode.org/MAPPINGS/VENDORS/ADOBE/symbol.txt`; Apple's Mac OS Symbol is laid out identically) — code → real Unicode char.
- A `symbol_font_draw` helper returns the PUA code when the face has one, else the encoding's real character (U+F0DE → U+21D2 ⇒).
- Wired into every place a symbol-font character is drawn:
  - **text runs** with an `a:sym` font (`shape_cells` picks the face, `shape_item` remaps during shaping),
  - **bullets** (`symbol_font_char`),
  - **metafile text** (`symbol_char`).

The previously-skipped test now **runs on macOS** (its guard checks the remapped character), and a new test checks U+F0DE draws as U+21D2 on Apple's Symbol.

## Verification

- On this MacBook (Apple's Symbol installed): `x\u{F0DE}y` with `a:sym="Symbol"` lays out as `[("Arial",(0,1)), ("Symbol",(1,2)), ("Arial",(2,3))]` — the symbol char draws from **Symbol**, not Wingdings.
- `cargo test -p deckcraft-text` — 81 passed (was 80; +1 new test, and the previously-skipped one now runs).
- `cargo test -p deckcraft-geom -p deckcraft-render -p deckcraft-metafile` — all pass.
- `cargo clippy -p deckcraft-text --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.

## Docs

- `ROADMAP.md` progress log, revision history and header updated (minor).

title: Keep the run's bold and italic in the East Asian font fallback face
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #892

## Cause
`FontDb::cascade` used the run's style only for scripts that have a per-script `os_families` entry. For CJK it fell through to `fallback_for` and the plain/system coverage scans, which take no style and prefer the weight-400 upright face. So bold or italic CJK text in a font without CJK glyphs was drawn regular even when a bold face of the fallback family was installed.

## Fix
`cascade` still picks the fallback family by coverage, then a new `FontDb::styled` returns that family's face for the run's weight and italic. For a variable font without a matching named face it sets the `wght` axis to the run's weight. In the text layer, a bold run whose fallback face (from any fallback path, including the per-script Arabic, Hebrew, Thai and Devanagari faces) has no bold weight (below 550) is now drawn with synthetic bold. Faces from the run's own fonts keep the run's existing fake-bold setting.

## Verified
- Regression tests `bold_cjk_fallback_keeps_weight`, `bold_cjk_fallback_face_without_bold_is_made_bolder`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-fonts --lib bold_cjk_fallback_keeps_weight && cargo test -p deckcraft-text --lib bold_cjk_fallback_face_without_bold_is_made_bolder`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The order in which fallback families are picked by coverage is unchanged, and so is the face choice for the run's own fonts, including its explicit East Asian font. Colour (emoji) faces are never restyled.

title: Change case across formatting run boundaries
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs:693-715 (also the whole-shape path at :734-741)` (no existing issue): Change Case (Capitalize Each Word / Sentence case) restarts at every formatting run boundary, giving "HelLo World".

## Cause
format.case called `change_case` separately on each text run's slice, in both the text-range path and the whole-shape path. Title and sentence case depend on the previous character, so they started over at every run boundary. That turned mixed-format "hello world" into "HelLo World" and capitalized runs that begin mid-sentence.

## Fix
A new `deckcraft_model::edit::change_case_parts` changes the case of a paragraph's pieces as one string and carries the word or sentence state from piece to piece. It returns one output per input piece, so run boundaries and formatting survive changes that alter length, such as ß becoming SS. Both format.case paths now call it once per paragraph. Breaks and fields are read for context (a line break still starts a new word) but are not rewritten. `change_case` now delegates to the new function.

## Verified
- Regression test `change_case_spans_formatting_runs`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib change_case_spans_formatting_runs`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Each paragraph still starts in the start-of-word and start-of-sentence state, and the text before the selection is not used as context. This keeps the existing behaviour.

title: Mirror the rotation when flipping a rotated shape
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/shape.rs:400-412 (flip; used by arrange.flipHorizontal / arrange.flipVertical)` (no existing issue): Flip Horizontal / Flip Vertical on a rotated shape does not mirror it (the occupied region stays the same).

## Cause
`shape.flip` only toggled `flip_h` or `flip_v` and left `rot` unchanged. `Xfrm::affine` flips first and rotates second. A rotated shape therefore kept the same outline, and only its contents were mirrored in the shape's own frame.

## Fix
`flip` now also sets the rotation to `360° - rot`, normalised to 0..360, so 30° becomes 330°. Flip Horizontal and Flip Vertical on a rotated shape now give the true mirror image, and flipping twice restores the original outline. The regression test covers both commands.

## Verified

- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
`Xfrm::affine` and its flip-then-rotate order are unchanged. Unrotated shapes behave as before, because a rotation of 0 stays 0.

title: Reject invalid comment.delete index instead of clearing the slide
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/review.rs:140-155 (delete)` (no existing issue): comment.delete with an invalid `index` (e.g. -1, "2", 1.5) silently deletes every comment on the slide.

## Cause
`comment.delete` read `index` with `usize_param`, which returns `None` for any value that isn't a non-negative integer (-1, "2", 1.5). The `match` treated that `None` as an absent index and ran `sl.comments.clear()`, so a malformed index deleted every comment on the slide.

## Fix
`delete` now treats only a missing or null `index` as absent. A present value that isn't a valid non-negative integer returns a bad-params error before any edit happens, the way `id_param` handles ids. An absent `index` still clears the slide.

## Verified
- Regression test `delete_rejects_an_invalid_index_and_keeps_the_comments`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib delete_rejects_an_invalid_index`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`usize_param` and the other comment commands (`reply`, `resolve`, `next`, `prev`) are unchanged. `all: true` behaves as before.

title: Clamp text.selectParagraph paragraph index to avoid overflow
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs:1151 (select_para)` (no existing issue): text.selectParagraph panics (overflow) on a huge paragraph index in `at`.

## Cause
text.selectParagraph takes `at` from `pos_param`, which accepts any u64, and then computes `at.0 + 1` without a bounds check. With `at: [u64::MAX, 0]` the addition overflows. That gives an Internal error in debug builds and a wrapped, nonsensical selection in release builds.

## Fix
`select_para` now clamps the paragraph index to the last paragraph of the body before using it. The addition can no longer overflow, and the selection always stays inside the text.

## Verified
- Regression test `select_paragraph_huge_at`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine select_paragraph_huge_at`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`pos_param` and the other commands that read `at` (e.g. text.selectWord) are unchanged.

title: About: Contributors and Models get their own fixed-size block below the tabs (#843)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #843.

In Help > About, opening the Contributors or Models tab garbled the first row of text, and the About / Contributors / Models tabs stopped responding to clicks.

**Cause**

To make room for the credits table, the dialog called `set_min_size(640x380)` and `set_max_height(380)` on the dialog window's own `ui`. That `ui` already holds the tab row, so the tab row and the credits body had to share the same 380 px. The credits `ScrollArea` (`auto_shrink([false, false])`) then filled that space and overlapped the first row.

**Fix**

- The size calls on the dialog `ui` are removed.
- The new `credits_block` helper puts the Contributors or Models body in its own `allocate_ui` block, fixed at `CREDITS_SIZE` (640x380), below the tab row and the separator. The credits scroll inside that block, and the window grows to hold the tabs, the block and Close.
- The About tab is not changed, so it keeps its compact size.

This is the same idea as the PDFCraft About dialog: the size limit is on the credits body only, not on the dialog `ui`.

**Test**

`about_credits_tests::credits_get_their_own_block_below_the_tab_row` checks Contributors and Models. For each one it draws a tab-row label and then `credits_block`, and checks that:

- the block is exactly `CREDITS_SIZE`,
- the block starts below the tab row,
- the whole `ui` is taller than 380 px.

With the old code the tab row and the credits fit inside 380 px, so the last check fails.

title: Ecosystem: add-ins, Office add-ins, VBA through an add-in, live co-editing and document chat
author: sirmmo
body:
## What this changes

DeckCraft gets an add-in system, the same one as in GridCraft (storytold/gridcraft#1123) and WordCraft (storytold/wordcraft#2586), plus what is built on it:
- macro-enabled presentations;
- Office (Office.js) add-ins;
- VBA macros run by an external add-in;
- live co-editing with document chat;
- editing inside Nextcloud.

The reference docs are [docs/plugins.md](docs/plugins.md) (the protocol), [docs/officejs.md](docs/officejs.md) (Office add-ins) and [docs/collab.md](docs/collab.md) (co-editing and chat).

**This reverses the "add-ins and VBA out of scope" position** in the Ecosystem entry of [gaps.md](docs/gaps.md). The project owner asked for DeckCraft to follow the same approach as GridCraft and WordCraft; the gaps entry says so.

The add-ins are separate programs in any language. DeckCraft starts them and talks JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdin/stdout, so an add-in that crashes or hangs never takes the presentation with it. That follows the never-crash rule: timeouts, restarts, `failed` after 3 failures, bounded input everywhere, no panics. Everything is a command: the add-ins' features are reachable from the UI, the CLI, MCP and the control channel, and programmatic calls never open dialogs.

The protocol is shared with GridCraft and WordCraft, so one add-in can serve all three apps. The cross-app specs (co-editing, chat, add-in requirements) live in [sirmmo/craft-collab](https://github.com/sirmmo/craft-collab).

### Commit by commit

Each commit builds and passes the gates on its own:

1. **Macro-enabled presentations** (df2abf2): `.pptm`, `.potm` and `.ppsm` open and save, keeping the VBA project and its signatures byte for byte. `.potx` and `.ppsx` are written with their own main content types (`PptxKind`).
2. **Add-ins, Office add-ins and VBA** (0890b31):

title: Make edit.cut a no-op when only a text caret is set
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs:cut (about line 337) and delete (about line 523)` (no existing issue): edit.cut with only a text caret (no selection) deletes the character after the caret.

## Cause
`cut` always called `delete` after `copy_inner`, even when `copy_inner` copied nothing because the text selection was only a caret. While text is being edited, `delete` forwards to `text.delete_dir("forward")`, which removed the character after the caret.

## Fix
`cut` now returns early when the selection is only a caret. It returns the empty text and html that Copy returns, and it doesn't call `delete`. Cutting a real selection works as before.

## Verified
- Regression test `cut_with_only_a_caret_changes_nothing`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib cut_with_only_a_caret_changes_nothing`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
`edit.delete` and `copy_inner` are unchanged. Cut on shapes and slides is unchanged.

title: Fix add overflow panic in table.columnWidth for a huge column index
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs:540 (column_width)` (no existing issue): table.columnWidth panics (add overflow) when `col` is a huge index.

## Cause
`column_width` computed the right-neighbour column with a plain `c + 1`. With `col` = usize::MAX this overflows, which panics in debug builds and is reported as an Internal error. In release builds it wraps to 0.

## Fix
Both uses of `c + 1` in `column_width` (the `get` and the `get_mut` in the keepTotal branch) now use `c.saturating_add(1)`, as the insert commands already do. A huge column index finds no column, so the command succeeds and changes nothing.

## Verified

- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
The other table commands and the insert variants, which already saturate. A huge `col` is still ignored with Ok and not turned into a bad-params error.

title: Text: links take the hyperlink colour over the run's colour, unless ahyp:hlinkClr keeps it
author: xmaks82
body:
`resolve::run` kept a colour set on a hyperlinked run. The comment above it says PowerPoint 2019 and later honour that colour. I measured this on Windows and both versions draw such a run in the theme's hyperlink colour instead.

**Measured.** One slide with four runs, saved as PDF by PowerPoint through COM:

| run | PowerPoint 2016 (16.0.16327) | Microsoft 365 (16.0.17932) | `main` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `solidFill FF0000` + `hlinkClick` | hyperlink blue | hyperlink blue | red |
| `solidFill FF0000` + `hlinkClick` with `ahyp:hlinkClr val="tx"` | red | red | red |
| no fill + `hlinkClick` | hyperlink blue | hyperlink blue | hyperlink blue |
| `solidFill FF0000`, no link | red | red | red |

`ahyp:hlinkClr val="tx"` (`{A12FA001-AC4F-418D-AE19-62706E023703}`) is the extension PowerPoint writes when a user gives a link a colour of their own. Files without it, such as Google Slides exports, which put `srgbClr 000000` on every link run, open in PowerPoint with blue links. `main` showed them black.

**Change**
- `RunProps::link_keeps_color` is read from `a:hlinkClick/a:extLst/…/ahyp:hlinkClr val="tx"` and written back. Inside `hlinkClick` it goes after `a:snd`, in schema order.
- `resolve::run` paints a link in `hlink` unless the run (or the `defRPr` that carries the link) keeps its colour. In that case the inherited text colour applies, which is what `tx` means. Underline handling is unchanged.
- Tests: `hyperlinks_draw_in_the_hyperlink_colour_underlined` and `hyperlinked_runs_take_the_theme_hyperlink_look` now pin the measured rule, and `a_link_that_keeps_its_text_colour_survives_a_round_trip` is new.

**Checked**
- 31 real decks compared slide by slide with PDFs from PowerPoint 2016: 8 slides closer, none worse.
- `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` passes, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

title: Text: a word doesn't break after ?, !, } or + (URLs wrap as in PowerPoint)
author: xmaks82
body:
`break_opportunities` follows Unicode line breaking, which allows a break after `?`, `!`, `}` and `+` inside a word. A long URL therefore broke after its `?` and after each `+` of the query, and the rest of the line stayed empty. PowerPoint fills the line instead.

**Measured in PowerPoint 2016 for Windows** (16.0.16327, `latinLnBrk` off, which is its default). Text boxes held words joined by each of `? ! ) ] } ; : , » / . _ % = & + -`, plus a Yandex search URL, and were saved as PDF through COM. None of `?`, `!`, `}` or `+` is a break opportunity inside a word: the word fills the line and breaks where it no longer fits, as `main` already does after `/` and `\`. The other characters already matched.

| Yandex search URL in a 3-inch box, Arial 14 | first line |
|---|---|
| PowerPoint | `https://yandex.ru/search/?text=%` |
| `main` | `https://yandex.ru/search/?` |
| this branch | `https://yandex.ru/search/?text=%` |

On the synthetic slide every line now matches PowerPoint's PDF, where `main` differed on 9 lines. Across 31 real decks compared with PowerPoint PDFs, the slide of search links gets closer by 1.5 and one slide moves by 0.1 of rasterization noise; that slide's text lines are identical to PowerPoint's.

title: Header & Footer: the automatic date takes a format
author: Hamza0101
body:
Header & Footer's automatic date was always the short date, with no way to choose a format — and a `dateFormat` parameter was accepted and silently dropped.

## What was wrong

`HeaderFooter::date_format` exists in the model, documented as "`datetime1`…`datetime13` format for automatic dates". Nothing ever read it, wrote it or set it: `grep` finds exactly one hit, the field's own declaration. The placeholder was hardcoded:

```rust
PhType::Date if hf.date_text.is_empty() => TextBody {
    ... kind: RunKind::Field { field: "datetime1".into() } ...
```

Measured on `main` @ 1dc6972:

```
design.headerFooter {date: true, dateText: ""}                      -> "10/17/2026"  datetime1
design.headerFooter {date: true, dateFormat: "datetime5"}           -> "10/17/2026"  datetime1
                                                                       hf.date_format stayed ""
```

The second line is the worse half: the command returned `Ok`, so a caller had no way to tell the format had been ignored.

Everything else was already in place — `datetime::field_text` renders all thirteen types, and Insert ▸ Date & Time already offers them. Only the wiring from a choice to the placeholder was missing.

## The change

- `design.headerFooter` takes `dateFormat`, **refuses** anything outside the thirteen types rather than ignoring it, and stores it.
- A Date placeholder is created with that field type and its saved text.
- An existing Date placeholder follows a format that changed, the same way it already followed a changed `dateText`.
- `datetime::DATE_KINDS` is the canonical list, and `dialogs.rs` now uses it instead of keeping a second copy of the same thirteen strings.
- The Header & Footer dialog gains a **Format** dropdown, listing each type by what it would show right now (the same samples as Insert ▸ Date & Time), enabled while the date is automatic — a fixed date is the text as typed, so a format would mean nothing there.

title: Export: PDFs store each slide backdrop once (#845)
author: FabPei
body:
Opening this 438-slide deck as a PDF produced a 226 MB file where LibreOffice writes 4 MB (#845). Every slide repeats the same background design — the master and layout graphics, a water-texture frame in this deck — but the export rasterized each slide as one full-page bitmap at print resolution and embedded that bitmap per page, so the repeated artwork was stored once per slide instead of once.

The export now draws each slide as two rasters: the backdrop (background fill with the master and layout graphics) and the slide's own shapes over it. `deckcraft_render::render_slide_part` already splits the two this way for slide transitions, and the split is exact — the full renderer composes the same two passes. Equal backdrops become equal images, and the writer stores each one once through its content-addressed image cache, so a deck's shared design now costs one raster however many slides use it. The slide's own shapes keep their transparency: the renderer's premultiplied pixels are converted to straight RGBA for the PDF's colour channel and alpha mask.

What changed:
- `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs` — `Exporter::slide` renders `SlidePart::Backdrop` and `SlidePart::Content` and draws them as two images; new `backdrop` (composite onto white) and `straight` (premultiplied to straight RGBA) helpers.
- `crates/pdf/src/tests.rs` — new regression test.

Fixes storytold/deckcraft#845

Validation: `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, tests, layering, assets, wasm). The regression test `slides_share_one_backdrop_raster_and_keep_their_pixels` exports slides with different text and asserts the PDF has one backdrop object drawn by every page, that the stored backdrop is byte-for-byte what the renderer draws, and that a slide's content raster keeps straight RGBA plus its alpha mask — without this change the pages store full-page rasters that share nothing. Measured on the reporter's deck (Conception Web - 26-27 - Light.pptx): 226,695,248 bytes → 77,707,394 bytes (2.9x smal…

title: Theme: light-mode controls stand out on dialogs (#826)
author: FabPei
body:
The Preferences checkbox and the Interface size slider were invisible in light mode (#826): their fills come from the `field_bg` token, which was pure white, on a dialog that is also white and draws no border around its controls — white-on-white. The dark theme already used a `field_bg` slightly off its card colour, which is why only light mode looked broken. The reporter's suggested fix is exactly this: make the background colour of those controls darker.

What changed:
- `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` — light `field_bg` is `0xE3E3E3` (the palette's card-border grey) instead of white, so checkbox fills, slider troughs and field backgrounds stand out on the white card and the chrome.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` — new regression test `field_backgrounds_stand_out_on_dialogs` checks the effective egui visuals after `apply`: control fills must differ from the dialog background by a visible margin in both themes.

Note on the ticket title: the relay title says "text appears black in dark mode in some menus", which we could not reproduce — deterministic pixel sampling of the dark-mode Preferences dialog found no black text (175,000 samples, minimum luminance equal to the dialog background). The reporter's body describes the light-mode control backgrounds, and that is what this fixes.

Fixes storytold/deckcraft#826

Validation: `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, tests, layering, assets, wasm). The regression test `field_backgrounds_stand_out_on_dialogs` is proven red-green (it fails on white-on-white before this change). Verified in the running app: the light-mode Preferences dialog now shows the checkbox and slider clearly against the dialog.

title: Format: Asian typography paragraph options (禁則処理・句読点のぶら下げ) in the dialog and as commands
author: midasdf
body:
## What this adds

DeckCraft already modelled, read, wrote and (for two of them) honoured PowerPoint's East Asian paragraph properties — `a:pPr/@eaLnBrk`, `@hangingPunct`, `@latinLnBrk` — but **nothing could set them**: no command, no UI. A Japanese user could not turn 禁則処理 or 句読点のぶら下げ on or off, which PowerPoint exposes in Paragraph ▸ アジア言語の文字体裁.

- **Commands** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs`), each `{"on"?: bool}` toggling the selected paragraphs' property and `enabled` like the other paragraph commands:

| id | label | property |
|---|---|---|
| `format.eastAsianLineBreak` | East Asian Line Breaking (禁則処理) | `east_asian_line_break` → `@eaLnBrk` |
| `format.hangingPunctuation` | Hang Punctuation (句読点のぶら下げ) | `hanging_punct` → `@hangingPunct` |
| `format.latinLineBreak` | Allow Latin Text to Wrap Mid-word (英単語の途中で改行を許可) | `latin_line_break` → `@latinLnBrk` |

- **Paragraph dialog**: a bold **Asian Typography** section with the three checkboxes, applied with the dialog's other paragraph edits in one *Paragraph…* undo step; `format.paragraphDialog` takes `eastAsianLineBreak?`, `hangingPunctuation?`, `latinLineBreak?` (a present non-bool is rejected without editing; absent leaves the property alone).
- **The line breaker now honours `eaLnBrk`**: Unicode's line-break data offers no break before a small kana or the prolonged sound mark at all, so relaxing 禁則 means *adding* that opportunity, not keeping one — with the property off, a line may start with one (Word's 禁則処理なし). Absent still means on (PowerPoint's default), so the default layout is unchanged, and closing brackets and closing punctuation keep following the Unicode rule (they are protected by the Unicode classes, not by a deckcraft list — a follow-up if the maintainer wants them relaxed too).
- `latin_line_break` and `hanging_punct` were already honoured by the line breaker and are unchanged.

title: Dark appearance: follow the system setting (#41)
author: JeremyYao
body:
Fixes #41.

## Problem

DeckCraft never read the operating system's appearance. On Windows 11 with dark mode on, it still opened light, because `UiState.brightness` defaulted to Light and nothing compared it with the system. Preferences ▸ Dark appearance was a checkbox, so it couldn't say "follow the system" either.

## What this changes

**Preferences ▸ General ▸ Dark appearance** is now a dropdown with three choices:

| Choice | Appearance |
|---|---|
| **Use system setting** (default) | Dark while the system is dark, light while it is light. Follows changes made while DeckCraft runs, including macOS Auto. |
| **On** | Always dark |
| **Off** | Always light |

- **File ▸ Account ▸ Appearance** shows the same dropdown. It replaces the Light/Dark one that was there.
- When the system's setting can't be read, Use system setting falls back to **light**.
- The View ribbon's **Dark Mode** button and the title-bar **Light/Dark appearance** toggle are still one-click switches. They now switch to whichever of On or Off isn't showing. They don't offer the three-way choice that #41's first acceptance criterion asks for, because a dropdown didn't fit a one-click button. That is easy to add if you want it.
- **Command:** `view.dark` takes `{mode: "system"|"on"|"off"}` or `{on: bool}`, and toggles when given neither.
- **Saved state:** `darkMode` in `ui.json`. An older file with `"brightness": "dark"` loads as On. One with `"brightness": "light"`, which was the default before, loads as Use system setting, because a saved light value doesn't show whether the user picked it. #41 lists the default as a maintainer decision; this PR makes it Use system setting, as requested by the person filing this change.
- egui's style is now pinned to the appearance DeckCraft picks, through `ctx.set_theme`. Before, egui switched to its own unstyled light or dark style whenever the system theme changed. That also gives the native title bar the matching appearance.

title: Close the control port on the first line that isn't a request
author: skylartaylor
body:
# Close the control port on the first line that isn't a request

The control port closes the connection on the first line that isn't a request, rather than skipping
bad lines and continuing to read. An HTTP request line or the HTTP/2 preface ends the connection
before anything after it is dispatched.

## Credit

All commits on this branch are authored by **@aiongg**, who did the design and the implementation
across every app in this family. I have only opened the pull request, because they were unreachable
and the team was ready to build. Thank you for the work, and for the care taken over the test
coverage in particular.

## Testing

`cargo xtask ci` on the branch, plus the regression tests added in these commits, which fail
without the change. Please re-run the full gate on a current toolchain before merging.

---

title: Fonts: the CJK fallback path prefers faces matching the run's bold/italic (#892)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #892.

**What was wrong.** Bold Chinese, Japanese and Korean text was drawn in regular weight when the run's font had no CJK glyphs (Calibri, Aptos, Arial - the usual case). The CJK fallback path (`FontDb::cascade` -> `fallback_for`) never received the run's style: the fallback sort always preferred `weight = 400, italic = false`, so a regular CJK face beat a bold one every time.

**The fix** (`crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs` + `fallback.rs`, ~25 lines): `fallback_for_styled` and `loaded_fallback_styled` sort candidates by `(fallback_family, italic_match, weight_match)` where `italic_match` and `weight_match` compare the face against the requested style's italic and weight (via the existing `style_italic`/`style_weight` helpers). `cascade` passes the run's `style` through to the styled variant. Regular text gets the identical sort as before (`style_weight("Regular")` = 400, `style_italic("Regular")` = false), so non-CJK fallbacks are unchanged.

**Follow-up commit (2026-10-19)** - a review of the first version found two gaps that hit real machines, both fixed here:

- **The family's bold file could stay unloaded forever.** `fallback_for_styled` settled for a loaded face that doesn't carry the requested style before the system pass ever ran: a lookup by a Windows family name loads only that style's file, so if "Malgun Gothic" Regular was already loaded (any interface lookup does it), every bold run of that family fell back to Regular for the whole session - the system pass that loads the family's Bold file was unreachable. A style-mismatched loaded winner now triggers the family's own load (`load_cataloged`) plus the system scan, and the styled best is taken over everything then loaded. Verified on Windows: `cascade(ê°€, [Shippori Mincho], "Bold")` drew Malgun Gothic Regular before, Malgun Gothic Bold (700) after.
- **Double-emboldening.** `GlyphRun.fake_bold` copied the document face's flag: a bold run in a Regular-only font (Shippori Mincho - bundled, no Bold fil…

title: Header & Footer: an automatic date's format comes back on import
author: Hamza0101
body:
The read-side half I said I would send separately in #927. **Stacked on #927** — it needs `datetime::DATE_KINDS` from it, so please take that one first; the diff here is the top commit only.

## What was wrong

`header_footer()` in `crates/pptx/src/read/mod.rs` looked at a Date placeholder and recorded its *text* only when it held no field. It never looked at the field, so an automatic date's format was dropped on import: `date_format` came back empty whatever the deck used.

## Why it is not cosmetic

With #927's Format dropdown, opening a deck whose dates are `datetime5` showed **datetime1** selected, because that is what an empty `date_format` falls back to. Pressing Apply then sent `datetime1` back and reformatted the deck's dates — a silent change to a file the user had only opened to look at. That is the part that moved this from "nice to have" to worth sending.

## The change

The reader remembers which of the thirteen formats the field is, so the dialog opens on the deck's own choice.

- An unknown spelling is deliberately **not** recorded. `datetime` and `datetimeFigureOut` both render as the short date, but the command only accepts the thirteen and would refuse them, so claiming one as "the choice" would make Apply fail. They come back as no choice, exactly as before.
- A **fixed** date still comes back as its text, unchanged.

`crates/pptx` takes a dependency on `crates/text` for `DATE_KINDS` rather than keeping a second copy of the same thirteen strings. pptx is layer 3 and text is layer 2, so that direction is allowed; `cargo xtask layers` passes (28 crates, no violations).

## Tests

`crates/pptx/tests/header_footer_date.rs`, a real round trip through `export` then `import`:

| deck | `date_format` after import | `date_text` |
|---|---|---|
| `dateFormat: datetime5` | `datetime5` | empty |
| `dateFormat: datetime11` | `datetime11` | empty |
| no format asked for | `datetime1` (the placeholder's own field) | empty |
| `dateText: "4 July 1776"` | empty —…

title: Canvas: a shape in front of edited text takes the click (#931)
author: Zetenypapp
body:
Fixes #931.

**Upfront about how this was made:** I'm not a programmer. The fix, the test and this description were written by Claude (Claude Code, Opus 5.5), which reproduced the bug in the desktop app on Windows 11 and checked the fix there too.

## The bug

On a Title and Content slide, put a shape on top of the content placeholder, click the placeholder's edge, then click the shape: the placeholder stays selected and the shape can't be reached until you click somewhere else first.

Clicking an empty placeholder starts editing its text (as in PowerPoint). From then on, `Session::pointer` sent every click inside that text box to `place_caret`, which runs before the hit test, so a shape in front of the text never got the click.

## The fix

`place_caret` (crates/engine/src/tools.rs) now first walks the shapes in front of the one holding the text, topmost first, and leaves the click to the normal hit test when one of them is under the pointer. A click on the text where nothing is in front still moves the caret, and grouped text works the same way (the walk stops at the group that holds the edited shape). 9 lines, no other behaviour changes.

## Testing

- New engine test `a_shape_in_front_of_edited_text_takes_the_click`: the reporter's steps with pointer events. Without the fix it fails (the placeholder stays selected); with it, it passes. It also checks that a click on the text away from the shape keeps editing it.
- Reproduced in the desktop app over the control channel before the fix, and checked after.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes locally on Windows 11: fmt, pdf-deps, clippy, tests, assets, layers and wasm.
- `ROADMAP.md` progress-log line.

title: Media: fuzz the hand-written decoders (AV1, VP9, HEVC, H.264, Opus) at the bitstream level, with AV1 film grain clips
author: braiinz94
body:
Found while reviewing test coverage of the hand-written decoders (no existing issue).

## What was missing

The hand-written AV1, VP9, HEVC and H.264 video decoders and the Opus audio decoder read files from strangers, but some of their crates have few tests for their size (`av1`: 10 tests for ~20k lines) and none fuzz them. `damaged_media_neither_panics_nor_hangs` damages whole files, so most mutations stop in the container and never reach a decoder. AV1 film grain synthesis (`crates/av1/src/grain.rs`) was barely reached (14 % of its lines), because no fixture carries grain.

## What this adds

- **`crates/media/tests/codec_mutation.rs`.** It demuxes the fixture clips the way `video.rs` and `audio.rs` do, then damages the compressed samples themselves before they reach the decoder: truncate, flip bits, overwrite a run, set a byte, drop, repeat or reorder samples, and sometimes the configuration record (`av1C`, `hvcC`, `avcC`, `OpusHead`). Every mutation must give an error or output, never a panic or a hang (10 s per decode). It is seeded and deterministic: `DECKCRAFT_MUTATION_ITERS` (default 200 per clip) runs it longer, `DECKCRAFT_MUTATION_SEED` replays another seed, and a failure prints clip, seed, iteration and mutation.
- **Clips fuzzed:** `clip-av1.mkv`, the three grain clips below, `clip-vp9.webm`, `clip-hevc.mp4`, `clip-h264.mp4`, `clip-h264.mov`, and the Opus streams of `tone.opus` (Ogg) and `clip-vp9.webm`. An Opus packet truncated to nothing is passed as a lost packet (`decode(None)`), so packet loss concealment is fuzzed too.
- **`harness_reports_panics_and_hangs`.** A fuzzer that finds nothing proves nothing until it is seen to catch something, so this checks that the harness reports a panic (with its location) and a hang.
- **`clip-av1-grain-{4,6,15}.mkv`** (2–3 KB each). The same `make.sh` gradient, encoded with libaom's built-in film grain test vectors (`film-grain-test=N`), so they are contributor-original and CC0 like the other clips. `make.sh` reg…

title: Thumbnails: navigating slides scrolls the pane to keep the current slide visible (#917)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #917.

**What was wrong.** Navigating slides with the arrow keys never scrolled the thumbnail pane: past a screenful of slides, the current slide's thumbnail left the viewport and the pane gave no hint where you were.

**The fix** (`crates/ui-egui/src/thumbs.rs`): when the current slide changes, the pane scrolls its thumbnail into view - minimally, and only once it has left the viewport, as in PowerPoint. A thumbnail that is already on screen never moves the pane, so the user's own scrolling stands, and opening a document never scrolls (the first frame only records the slide). `ui.scroll_to_rect(rect, None)` gives exactly that: egui scrolls only when the rect is outside the clip rect. An `Align::Center` would have re-centred the pane - animated - on every keystroke.

`show()` also records the pane's scroll offset in `UiState.thumbs_scroll` (`#[serde(skip)]`, so it is not persisted). This is the same pattern as `slide_rect`/`canvas_scale` and flows into the control channel's `inspect` output automatically, so the pane is observable from end-to-end automation too.

**Tests (red-proof).** `thumbs::tests::navigating_slides_keeps_the_current_thumbnail_visible` builds a 31-slide deck, jumps to the last slide and asserts the pane scrolled, then steps one slide up - already on screen - and asserts the pane held still. With the fix reverted the offset stayed 0, so the test is red on the unfixed code.

**Gate.** `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p deckcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the ui-egui suite (217 tests, 4 ignored) pass locally on Windows; the assets, layers and wasm checks are green too. The ui-egui test binary crashes intermittently on this machine with `0xc0000005` (STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION) - pre-existing on clean `main`, and the Linux gate is unaffected. `gates (ubuntu-latest)` is the authority.

ROADMAP progress-log row added.

title: Edit Points: turning a shape into a freeform is one undo step
author: Zetenypapp
body:
**Upfront about how this was made:** I'm not a programmer. The fix, the test and this description were written by Claude (Claude Code, Opus 5.5). It found this bug while break-testing DeckCraft (random command sequences, then Undo all the way back, which should restore the deck exactly), on Windows 11.

## The bug

Right-click a shape (a star, an arrow…) → **Edit Points**, then press Ctrl+Z: the shape stays a freeform. Edit Points turns a preset into custom geometry, but `shape.editPoints` was a `noundo` command, so that conversion never became an undo step, and the first Ctrl+Z took back whatever came *before* it instead (in the test, the insertion of the shape itself).

## The fix

- `shape.editPoints` is an ordinary undoable command now. `Session::execute` only records a step when the document actually changed, so entering Edit Points on a shape that is already a freeform, or leaving Edit Points, still adds nothing; only the conversion is a step ("Edit Points").
- `ToolState::editing_points` only counts a shape that is a freeform, so when Undo turns it back into a preset, Edit Points ends instead of showing a point editor with no points.

## Testing

- New engine test `edit_points_conversion_is_one_undo_step`: convert, leave, Undo (the star is back), Redo (freeform again), Undo while still editing (Edit Points ends), and re-entering on a freeform adds no step. Without the fix it fails: Ctrl+Z removes the inserted shape instead.
- The existing Edit Points tests still pass.

title: Open: cap absurd effect sizes from a file (a huge glow made rendering ask for 34 GB)
author: Zetenypapp
body:
**Upfront about how this was made:** I'm not a programmer. The fix, the test and this description were written by Claude (Claude Code, Opus 5.5). It found this while break-testing DeckCraft on Windows 11: damaged copies of the sample deck saved as .pptx, opened, rendered and saved again.

## The bug

A `.pptx` (or `.deckcraft`) can give an effect any size. Format Shape and `shape.effects` keep a glow to 150 pt, but a file is read as is, so a slide with `<a:glow rad="99999999999999999999">` reached the renderer with a glow of ~7.9 × 10^15 pt:

- at some sizes `vello_common` panics (`flatten_simd.rs:581`, range end index 8 out of range for slice of length 6). The command guard catches it, but the slide doesn't draw
- at others (a glow of 10^18 pt) rendering asked for **34 GB** in one allocation and the process aborted, which no guard can catch, so the app closes and unsaved work is lost

One bad file is enough.

## The fix

`deckcraft_format::sane_numbers`, which `repair` already runs on every opened file (`.pptx` and `.deckcraft`), now also caps effect sizes at what Format Shape allows, the way it already caps line widths and font sizes: glow 150 pt, soft edges 100 pt, shadow blur and distance 200 pt, reflection blur and distance 100 pt. Shadow scale and skew are kept to ±1000% and ±89°, and anything that isn't a number becomes 0. This covers shape effects and run effects in text and in table cells.

## Testing

- New engine test `opening_a_file_caps_absurd_effect_sizes`: a deck with every effect at 10^18 pt or NaN (shape, text and table-cell text), saved as `.deckcraft` and as `.pptx` and opened again. Every size comes back within the limits, and only then is the slide rendered, so the test can't trigger the huge allocation even when the cap is missing. Without the fix it fails on the first check (a shadow of 10^18 pt survives the load).

title: Open: give shapes that repeat an id in a .deckcraft file fresh ones
author: Zetenypapp
body:
**Upfront about how this was made:** I'm not a programmer. The fix, the test and this description were written by Claude (Claude Code, Opus 5.5). It found this while break-testing DeckCraft on Windows 11: the sample deck saved as `.deckcraft`, with its numbers changed one kind at a time, then opened, rendered and saved again.

## The bug

A `.deckcraft` file whose shapes repeat an id (hand-edited, written by another tool, or damaged) opens as is, and the deck fails its own `Presentation::validate` ("slide N: duplicate shape id M"). Everything that finds a shape by id (selection, `id`/`ids` command params, the Selection Pane, the control channel and MCP) then gets the first of the shapes that share it, so the others can't be reached or edited by id. `repair` already gives repeated *slide* ids fresh ones, but not repeated shape ids. A `.pptx` isn't affected: its importer assigns ids itself.

## The fix

`repair` (run on every opened file) now gives each shape that repeats an id already used on its slide, layout or master, groups included, a fresh id from the deck's counter. The first shape keeps its id, and with it whatever animations and connectors point at. Decks without repeats aren't copied or changed. An exhausted id space leaves the rest as they are, as `repair` already does for slides (#407).

## Testing

- New engine test `opening_a_file_gives_repeated_shape_ids_fresh_ones`: a group of four shapes and an ellipse, all given the same id, saved as `.deckcraft` and opened again. The deck validates, all six shapes are there, the first keeps its id, the new ids come from the deck's counter, and the last shape can be selected by its own id. Without the fix it fails: five "duplicate shape id" problems.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes locally on Windows 11: fmt, pdf-deps, clippy, tests, assets, layers and wasm.

title: Charts: a series' own data-label setting decides whether its labels show (#868)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #868.

**What was wrong.** The reader stored a series-level `c:dLbls/c:showVal` in `Series.data_labels`, but every drawing path tested only the chart-wide `Chart.data_labels`: a series that asked for labels got none, and a series that asked for none got them.

**The fix**

- `crates/model/src/chart.rs`: the model gains `Chart::series_data_labels` - the one place that decides whether a series' labels show: the series' own `c:dLbls/c:showVal` wins, an explicit `false` hides them even when the chart-wide setting is on, and a series that says nothing follows the chart.
- `crates/pptx/src/read/chart.rs`: the reader reads the setting, and a bare `<c:showVal/>` (no `val` attribute) means true, as the schema's default. The plot group's own setting is respected too: a group that asks for no labels keeps them off, even when another group of a combo chart asks for them. Before, any group that asked turned the chart-wide setting on and the group that said no inherited it.
- `crates/render/src/{chart,chartex,radar}.rs`: the drawing paths (bar, column, line, area, pie, doughnut, radar, scatter) call the model instead of testing the chart-wide flag.

**Tests (red-proof).** `crates/pptx/tests/chart_data_labels.rs`:

- `bare_series_showval_shows_labels` - a bare series `showVal` shows that series' labels while its siblings stay quiet. With the series-level setting ignored, it fails.
- `series_showval_false_hides_labels` - an explicit `val="0"` on the first series keeps it quiet under a chart-wide on. With the series-level setting ignored, it fails.
- `a_combo_chart_keeps_each_groups_own_label_setting` - the bar group asks for no labels and the line group for labels; the bars stay quiet. With the group's setting ignored, the bar group shows labels it asked to keep quiet.

title: PPTX: media playback options survive a save and reopen through the timing tree (#74)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #74.

**What was wrong.** #74 reports that `media.options` - volume, play-across-slides, hide-while-not-playing, loop, rewind and automatic start - are lost when a deck is saved. The cause: PowerPoint stores those in the slide's timing tree as `p:video`/`p:audio` `cMediaNode` children, while DeckCraft's writer only emitted `p14:media` (trim, fades, bookmarks) and only ran `timing()` for slides with animations - so a media clip with playback options but no animations saved no timing tree at all.

**The fix**

- **Write** (`crates/pptx/src/write/timing.rs`): a media shape with any non-default option gets a `p:video`/`p:audio` node under `tmRoot` - `vol` in thousandths of a percent, `numSld` for the slide span, `showWhenStopped` for hide-while-not-playing, `repeatCount="indefinite"` for loop, `fill="remove"` for rewind (mirroring how #77 encodes rewind), and a zero-delay start condition for automatic start. The nothing-to-write early return now also counts media nodes, so the writer call site no longer needs an animations gate.
- **Read** (`crates/pptx/src/read/timing.rs`): those nodes are parsed back onto the clip, whether or not the slide has animations. A node standing alone under `tmRoot` rather than nested in `mainSeq` (how PowerPoint authors click-to-play) is handled the same way - playback goes through the pic's `PlayMedia` hyperlink action regardless.

A review of the fix found four gaps in reading and writing those nodes, now closed:

- A volume that is not a number was stored as one: `vol="NaN"` parses, and the clip kept a NaN volume. Such a volume is ignored, and the writer keeps the full volume rather than writing a number that is not one.
- `showWhenStopped` is an XML boolean, so `"false"` means the same as `"0"`. Only `"0"` was read as false, so a file that spells it out was read as "the clip stays on screen".
- A clip that starts on a click is not automatic, whatever its delay says: a condition with `evt="onClick"` waits for the click, and the clip…

author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #967.

During a slide show the GIF corner button already hides after 2.5 s without pointer movement (`now - show.last_move < 2.5`), but the video/audio playback bar stayed on screen for as long as the pointer rested on the clip.

- New `Show::pointer_awake(now)` holds the existing 2.5 s idle check; the GIF button now uses it too, so both controls hide on the same rule.

Moving the pointer brings the bar back at once, as with the GIF button.

title: Hide the idle cursor over clickable clips during a slideshow (#968)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #968.

**Cause.** In `show.rs` the slide show picks the cursor in one `if`/`else if` chain, and the pointing-hand branch (`pointing`: the shape under the pointer acts on a click) came before the idle-hide branch (pointer still for over 2.5 s). A video from PowerPoint carries a play trigger on itself, so the pointer over it counts as "pointing". The hand therefore won every frame, and a still cursor never hid over the playing clip. The same thing happened over any linked or trigger shape.

**Fix.** The idle-hide check now comes before the pointing hand. When the pointer moves, the hand shows again as before. The pointing branch also asks for a repaint after 500 ms, as the idle branch already does. Without that, a still pointer over a static clickable shape gets no new frame, so the hide would never be drawn.

Nothing else changes: pen, laser, zoom and grid still pick their cursors first, and Reading View still never hides the cursor.

**Test.** `a_still_cursor_hides_over_a_clickable_shape` runs the real `SlideApp` in an `egui_kittest` harness. It puts a linked rectangle over the whole slide, starts the show, hovers the slide, checks that the cursor is the pointing hand, then keeps the pointer still for 3 s and checks that the cursor is `None`. Without the fix the last assertion fails, because the cursor stays `PointingHand`.

title: deckcraft-web: postMessage host bridge (?host=parent), same protocol …
author: alexeyvolkoff
body:
…as GridCraft

For pages embedding DeckCraft in an iframe (same-origin parent):
- deckcraft:ready/failed — handshake at start
- deckcraft:open {name, bytes} — the parent sends the deck to open
- deckcraft:save {name, bytes} — Save/Save As and PDF/PNG/GIF exports go to the parent instead of a download
- deckcraft:dirty {dirty} — on change
- deckcraft:cmd {id, params?} (answers deckcraft:response) — run engine commands
- deckcraft:docClosed — once File › Close disposes of the deck (matched by the host-opened deck's uid; the session keeps a blank deck around)

Also fixes, related to apps embedded this way:
- Ctrl+S on the web suggested .deckcraft for a deck opened from a .pptx: SlideApp.web_save_format lets a host open a deck and keep its format
- a QAT file.close runs the guarded close_presentation() (Save/Don't Save/ Cancel), like Ctrl+W — a host-added Close button never discards silently
- the web message listener wakes the egui context, so commands queuing up while the app is idle run in the next frame

Cover the Slide Master layout verbs and placeholder inserts

`master.insertLayout`, `master.renameLayout`, `master.deleteLayout` and

Slide Master view; `insertPlaceholder` is the Insert Placeholder dropdown next to them, and its

title: Duplicate: a copy that was moved is duplicated the same distance further on (#966)
author: Zetenypapp
body:
**Upfront about how this was made:** I'm not a programmer. The fix, the test and this description were written by Claude (Claude Code, Opus 5.5), on Windows 11.

Fixes #966.

## The issue

In PowerPoint, Ctrl+D a shape, move the copy, and Ctrl+D again: the next copy lands the same distance further on, so a row of evenly spaced copies takes a few keystrokes. In DeckCraft every Duplicate used the fixed offset (12 pt down and right), whatever you had done with the last copy.

## The change

`edit.duplicate` remembers, per presentation, its last originals and their copies, along with the slide and the shape tree (slide or Slide Master). When the shapes duplicated next are exactly those copies, on the same slide, each new copy is placed at the copy's distance from its original (taken from the first pair). Otherwise, Duplicate uses the usual offset (`prefs.duplicate_offset`), as before:

- after duplicating something else
- after Undo removed the copies
- when the originals are gone
- on another slide

Nothing changes in the file format or in other commands.

## Testing

- New engine test `duplicating_a_moved_copy_repeats_the_move`: the first copy gets the usual offset; after the copy is moved 80 pt right, the next two Duplicates land 80 pt further each. Duplicating the original again uses the usual offset, and so does duplicating after an Undo. The deck validates. Without the change the test fails: the second copy lands at (192, 112) instead of (260, 100).
- The existing Duplicate tests still pass.

title: MCP: say that indices are 0-based, return the editor's slide number, and refuse an index past the end everywhere
author: zberry
body:
An agent told "change slide 3" over MCP passed `index: 3` and edited the slide the editor calls 4.
Every slide, section, animation and table index is 0-based while the editor counts from 1, and
nothing said so: the server instructions and tool descriptions said only "Slide index",
`inspect_document` listed `index` 0..n with no displayed number, an index past the end answered
"no slide 8", and several commands (`slide.hide`, `slide.duplicate`, `slide.layout`,
`slide.selectSlides`, `transition.*`, `animation.clear`, a PDF export's `slides` list) took an
index past the end and answered ok having done nothing, so an agent passing the editor's number
for the last slide was told it had succeeded.

title: PPTX: paragraph builds play the clicks the file asks for
author: incrhst
body:
A `bldP build="p"` build was always folded into one `TextBuild::ByParagraph` animation that kept only the first paragraph's start, and the timeline then re-expanded it to one step per top-level paragraph. Paragraph-by-paragraph builds of any other shape played the wrong number of clicks. Examples from Apache POI's `test-data/slideshow` decks (1-based slide numbers, clicks in the file vs in DeckCraft before this PR):

| Deck | Slide | Pattern | File | Before |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| customGeo | 18 | first paragraph After Previous, the other five On Click | 5 | 0 |
| HowWeRefactor | 9 | three paragraphs on one click (click + 2 With Previous) | 1 | 4 |
| HowWeRefactor | 21 | only paragraphs 3–4 built | 2 | 1 |
| HowWeRefactor | 27 | two build groups interleaved on one shape | 6 | 18 |

- **Import** (`read/timing.rs`): a paragraph build is folded into one by-paragraph animation only when it is exactly what such an animation saves as: the same effect on every non-empty paragraph, top-level paragraphs taking turns (On Click after an On Click start, After Previous otherwise), sub-levels With Previous on their parent's click. title: Equations: drawn as equations, typed in place, saved with their font (#148, #296)
author: hajdukste
body:
Fixes #148. Fixes #296. Also covers the typing half of #604: an equation typed in LaTeX is drawn as an equation and stays editable. Insert ▸ Symbol is unchanged.

## The problem

- Equations in a .pptx are drawn as their plain text, so fractions, integrals and exponents come out flat (#148). One deck reported there has 427 equations on 61 of its 68 slides, and it can't be presented.
- Insert ▸ Equation opens a dialog and inserts styled text, not an equation. It isn't saved as an equation and can't be edited as one (#296, #604).

## What this does

**Equations are drawn as equations.** Every OMML equation is laid out in 2-D: fractions, sub- and superscripts, radicals, big operators with limits, brackets that grow with their content, matrices, equation arrays, functions, accents, bars and boxes. It's set in the run's own font through DeckCraft's font database and fallback, so no font is added.

**Insert ▸ Equation types one in place**, at the insertion point or in a new, centred text box:
- With text selected, that text becomes the equation. Otherwise a selected *Type equation here* prompt appears, and typing replaces it.
- You type its linear form: `a/b`, `x^2`, `sqrt(x)`, `\frac{a}{b}`, `\sum_(i=1)^n i`. While the caret is in the equation it shows as that text on a gray field; elsewhere it's drawn in 2-D.
- `\alpha` followed by a space becomes α.
- Right Arrow at the end leaves the equation, so what you type next is ordinary text in the surrounding formatting. Left Arrow there goes back in. A caret just before an equation is outside it, so you can type in front of it or press Enter to move it down. Clicking an equation puts the caret in it.
- Backspace, Delete, paste and input methods edit it. Smart quotes, AutoCorrect and spelling leave it alone. An emptied equation is removed.
- Home ▸ Font, size and colour apply to the whole equation.

**Equations round-trip.** They stay the existing `RunKind::Math { omml }` run, with no new run kind or file field.

title: Clear animation triggers that point at deleted shapes
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs:573-585 (delete)` (no existing issue): Deleting a shape that is an animation trigger leaves the animation pointing at the deleted shape.

## Cause
`edit.delete` only dropped animations whose own `shape` was in the deleted ids. It never looked at `trigger`, so an effect triggered by a deleted shape kept a trigger id that no longer exists. Group descendants were also missing from the check, because only the group id is in `ids`.

## Fix
`edit.delete` now works out every shape id that was actually removed: the given ids, all group descendants, and groups that became empty. Animations on those shapes are dropped, and any trigger pointing at one is set to `None`, so the effect falls back to the main sequence. That matches what the PPTX writer already does.

## Verified
- Regression tests `deleting_a_trigger_shape_clears_the_trigger`, `deleting_a_group_clears_triggers_of_its_children`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib deleting_a_`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The PPTX writer and the animation engine are unchanged. Other commands that remove shapes, such as cut, are not touched.

title: Media: look a clip up on the slide it belongs to (#994)
author: Faabyy
body:
Fixes #994.

The PPTX import numbers shapes per slide, so two slides can hold different videos under one shape id. `find_clip` searched the whole deck and took the first match. The show's media cues, the keep-across-slides filter and the `media.*` requests all use it, so from slide 3 on, video 2 played.

`find_clip` now takes the slide the request comes from and searches it first, then the rest of the deck. Test: two slides, one id, different clips.

One open question: the other option would be to make media ids unique across the deck at import. That touches animation references too, so I kept the lookup fix small. Happy to change it if you prefer that.

Checked: fmt, clippy, ui-egui tests (the replace-fonts ribbon test fails on main too). I did not play a video in the window.

- Exit codes: 0 = clean, 1 = findings present, 2 = audit could not run.

title: Count line breaks as one char in Find/Replace
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/find.rs:107-121 (para_chars / para_matches; splice at :124)` (no existing issue): Find/Replace ignores line breaks: it matches across them and reports offsets that are too small.

## Cause
`para_chars`, `para_matches` and `splice` in `find.rs` built paragraph text from `r.text`. A `RunKind::Break` run has empty text, so a line break counted as zero characters. Searching `ab` matched `a<break>b`, and match offsets were too low after every break. The rest of the editor counts a break as one `\u{b}`.

## Fix
These three functions now use `Run::content()` and `Run::char_len()`, so a break is one `\u{b}` char. Matches no longer span a break, and offsets agree with `Paragraph::text()`.

## Verified
- Regression tests `a_match_never_spans_a_line_break`, `offsets_count_a_line_break_as_one_char`, `splice_after_a_line_break_keeps_the_break`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine cmd::find::tests`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Other commands, such as `review.spellingChange`, already use `Paragraph::text()` and are unchanged. Searching for a pattern that contains a line break is not supported and is unchanged.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved text matching and replacement across line breaks, including correct character offsets and preservation of line breaks.

title: Canvas: resizing snaps the edge being dragged (#961)
author: Faabyy
body:
Fixes #961, as far as I can reproduce it: resizing did snap, but not the edge being dragged.

`snap_resize` ran `snap_rect` on the whole box, which looks at all three edges per axis and takes the nearest line. A fixed edge that already sits on a line (distance 0) always won, so the dragged edge never snapped. A fixed edge near a line moved the dragged edge by its own distance instead.

Resizing now looks only at the edges being dragged (new `snap_edges`, which `snap_rect` calls with all edges, so moving is unchanged). The grid fallback uses the dragged edge too.

Tests: dragging the east handle with the left edge already aligned with another shape (the right edge now snaps: 197 → 200), and with a fixed edge 3 pt from a line (no shift: 324 → 321). Both fail on main.

Open question: should the centre line also snap when only one side is dragged? I left it out. Not checked: dragging in the window, and Shift/Alt while resizing. #838 also touches `snap_resize` (aspect ratio), so the two may need a rebase.

  * When no guide or shape alignment is available, grid snapping during resize follows the active handle rather than always snapping from the top-left corner.

title: Keep the crop of a PPTX video and apply it in the poster and playback (#972)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #972.

A video in PowerPoint can be cropped like a picture: the crop is the `a:srcRect` in the video's `p:blipFill`. The reader built the poster `PictureFill` with that crop but then copied only the poster's media id into `MediaClip`, so the crop was lost. The poster was then stretched over the whole frame in the editor (distortion), and the playing frame was letterboxed in the slide show (black bars).

Changes:
- `MediaClip` gets a `crop: [f64; 4]` (left, top, right, bottom fractions, the same layout as `PictureFill::crop`). It is `#[serde(default)]` like the rest of the struct, so older files open unchanged.
- PPTX import reads it from the video's `blipFill`; export writes it back through the same `dml::blip_fill` path that pictures use.
- The renderer draws the poster with the crop and clips it to the shape outline, the same way `ShapeKind::Picture` is drawn.
- `media::paint_frame` (editor canvas and slide show) shows only the cropped part of a playing frame, stretched over the box as PowerPoint does. Uncropped videos keep the current letterboxing.
- The file loader repairs a video crop the same way it repairs a picture crop (non-finite to 0, clamped to -10..1).

Tests:
- `pictures_media_and_ink_round_trip`: a cropped video keeps its crop through a PPTX round trip (fails without the fix: the crop came back as zeros).
- `a_video_crop_shows_only_the_cropped_part_of_the_frame`: the frame UV rectangle for a crop.
- `a_video_crop_is_repaired_like_a_picture_crop`: a broken video crop in a saved file is repaired on load.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Video crops are now preserved when opening and saving presentations, and applied to video frames and poster images in the editor and slideshow.
  * Invalid crop values are repaired when saving, and cropped images remain clipped to their shape boundaries.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: Show: draw shapes stacked above a playing video over its frame (#1005)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1005.

In the slide show, the playing video's current frame was painted after the whole slide texture, so it covered every shape on the slide, including the ones stacked above the video. PowerPoint keeps those shapes visible over the playing video.

What changes (in `crates/ui-egui/src/show.rs` only):

- After painting the video frames, the show now finds the lowest video on the slide that has a frame on screen (`below_playing_video`). If shapes are stacked above it, the slide's own shapes are rendered again over transparency (`render_slide_part` with `SlidePart::Content`), leaving out that video, everything below it and the other videos, and this overlay is painted over the frames.
- The overlay uses the same animation state, hidden media and GIF frames as the slide frame, and is cached by the same key as the slide texture, so a resting slide does not render it again on every frame.
- When no shape is above a video, nothing changes: the frame is painted last, as before. A video playing full screen still covers the whole slide.

Test: `shapes_above_a_playing_video_are_the_overlay` checks which shapes go into the overlay: with the video in the middle of the stack, the shape above it is drawn over it; with the video on top, or with no video playing, there is no overlay.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Slide shapes now appear above playing videos where appropriate, while full-screen videos continue to cover the entire slide.

title: Connector default sites face the other shape; formatting set on an empty shape survives text.set
author: zberry
body:
Two engine fixes, both found by an AI agent building decks through the MCP server.

`shape.connect` with no `fromSite`/`toSite` picked the closest pair of connection sites. For two
boxes stacked or side by side that is the pair a person would pick, but for a diagonal
neighbour it chose a side site and the arrow ran across the box; agents drawing a diagram
rebuilt their connectors two or three times per deck, reading `shape.sites` and passing the
sites by hand. Now each shape uses the site that faces the other along the dominant direction
between their centres (a box mostly below is left from the bottom), which is where a person
glues an arrow; explicit sites are honoured as before. The params doc says so and names the
numbering (a box has 0 top, 1 left, 2 bottom, 3 right; `shape.sites` lists them). Dense graphs

title: Render: table body text on tinted cells picks the theme colour that contrasts with the fill, so default tables stay readable on dark themes
author: zberry
body:
A table in the default style (medium2-accent1; also medium4 and the banded rows of light1)
draws its body cells in light tints of the accent colour but gives their text no colour, so the
text inherits the theme's text colour. On a dark theme such as Nocturne that is light, and the
body text is nearly invisible on the light tint; the header (accent fill, white text) is fine.

change beyond body cells: medium4's tinted header now also gets the contrasting text.

body:

title: Chart value axis ends near the data maximum; chart.options {axisMin, axisMax}
author: zberry
body:
Found by an AI agent building a deck through the MCP server: a bar chart whose largest value
was 59.7 drew its value axis to 100, leaving the bars in the left 60 % of the plot, and there
was no command to set the axis bounds.

The automatic scale picks the smallest 1-2-5 unit that fits the labels the axis has room for.
On a horizontal value axis that room was a fixed six characters per label, so a 400 pt bar
chart had room for three labels and the unit jumped from 10 to 50. The horizontal axis now
measures the widest label of the scale the data asks for, and no axis gets fewer than four
intervals, so the same chart ends at 70 by tens (a column chart of that size already did).
Charts with fixed bounds or a fixed major unit are unchanged.

`chart.options {axisMin?, axisMax?: n|null}` fixes the value axis' bounds: the model's existing
y_min/y_max, which the .pptx writer already exports as c:min/c:max and the reader imports.
`null` returns a bound to automatic; a value that is not a number, or a minimum at or above the
maximum, is refused and changes nothing.

Tests: the pixel test `value_axis_ends_near_the_data_maximum` (render) draws a 400x300 bar chart
and a column chart with values up to 59.7 and checks the longest bar reaches at least 80 % of
the plot between the zero line and the outermost gridline (the bar chart reached 0.596 before);
`chart_options_axis_bounds_set_clear_and_refuse` (engine) sets, clears and refuses the bounds.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p deckcraft-engine -p deckcraft-render --all-targets --

title: macOS: open documents from Finder and Open With (#138)
author: rizky-rahmad
body:
Closes #138.

## Problem

Double-clicking a `.pptx` in Finder (or Open With, a Dock drop, `open -a DeckCraft talk.pptx`) fails with
"DeckCraft cannot open files in the Office Open XML presentation format".

Root cause, two parts:

1. The macOS app never handles the `kAEOpenDocuments` ('odoc') Apple event that LaunchServices sends
   to the running (or just-launched) app instead of passing paths on the command line. winit 0.30
   doesn't handle it and owns the `NSApplicationDelegate`, so AppKit answers with the error dialog.
   Handling it ourselves needs Objective-C class declarations, i.e. `unsafe`, which this workspace
   forbids — the same problem WordCraft fixed by pinning `fmv-macos-events = "=0.1.0"` (PdfCraft has
   the same fix).
2. `packaging/macos/Info.plist.in` declares no `CFBundleDocumentTypes` at all, so LaunchServices has
   no reason to offer DeckCraft for presentations (only the file-dialog/Open-panel claim from the
   exported type declarations).

## Fix

- `apps/deckcraft/src/apple_events.rs` — module copied from WordCraft's `apple_events.rs`:
  `AppleEvents::install()` registers the handlers on the main thread before the event loop starts
  (so the launch event from Finder is caught too); the app drains the inbox every frame. The
  document case is adapted to DeckCraft: paths go through `SlideApp::open_from_system`, the same
  path the command line takes, so a `.ppsx` given last starts its slide show exactly as the
  module docs promise. Quit events close the window, which asks about unsaved changes first.
- `apps/deckcraft/src/main.rs` — install the registration before `eframe::run_native`, store a
  cloned `Inbox` in `App` (only on macOS, `Option` behind `cfg` so the test keeps compiling) and
  `poll` it at the top of `App::logic`.
- `apps/deckcraft/Cargo.toml` — `fmv-macos-events = "=0.1.0"` under the macOS target, pinned
  exactly like the sibling apps (review the diff before bumping).

title: Reject non-hex characters such as '+' in Rgba::from_hex
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/color/src/lib.rs:41` (no existing issue): Rgba::from_hex accepts '+' signs inside hex digits and returns a colour for malformed input.

## Cause
`Rgba::from_hex` parsed each chunk with `u8::from_str_radix(h, 16)`, which accepts a leading '+'. Malformed input like "+12345" therefore produced a colour instead of `None`.

## Fix
`from_hex` now requires every byte to be an ASCII hex digit before parsing. This replaces the old `is_ascii` check and covers the 3, 6 and 8-digit forms. The regression test `tests::from_hex_rejects_signs` covers the `+` cases.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::from_hex_rejects_signs`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-color from_hex_rejects_signs`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
I did not change any callers and did not audit them. Malformed input now returns `None`, the same result callers already get for other invalid colours. The issue does not list which callers depend on the old behaviour, so they should be checked if that matters.

title: macOS: open presentations from Finder (double-click, Open With, Dock)
author: eskimoburger
body:
## Problem

On macOS (0.8.0 DMG), double-clicking a `.pptx` in Finder, using **Open With**, dropping a file on the Dock icon, or running `open -a DeckCraft talk.pptx` launches DeckCraft on **File › Home** with nothing open. DeckCraft also isn't offered in Finder's Open With list for presentations.

Two causes:

1. `packaging/macos/Info.plist.in` declares the UTIs (`UTExportedTypeDeclarations` / `UTImportedTypeDeclarations`) but no `CFBundleDocumentTypes`, so LaunchServices doesn't know DeckCraft can open them.
2. Finder doesn't pass paths on the command line. It sends a `kAEOpenDocuments` ('odoc') Apple event, which winit 0.30 doesn't handle. Only `open --args file.pptx` worked.

WordCraft and GridCraft already handle both; DeckCraft was missing them.

## Fix

- **`Info.plist.in`**: add `CFBundleDocumentTypes`: `.deckcraft` (`Owner`) and the Open XML presentation, template and slideshow types (`Alternate`, as WordCraft does for `.docx`).
- **`apps/deckcraft/src/apple_events.rs`** (new): register an `NSAppleEventManager` handler through `fmv-macos-events = "=0.1.0"`, the same crate and pattern as `apps/wordcraft/src/apple_events.rs`. It's installed before the event loop, so it also catches the event that launched the app, and the frame loop drains it. No `unsafe` in this workspace.
- Opened paths go through `SlideApp::open_from_system`, the same path the command-line files take, so a `.ppsx` given last still starts its slide show. Failures are logged and shown in the status bar. A quit Apple event closes the window, so the unsaved-changes prompt still runs.
- The new dependency is macOS-only.

title: Equations: drawn as equations, typed in place, saved with their font (#148, #296)
author: hajdukste
body:
Fixes #148. Fixes #296. Also covers the typing half of #604: an equation typed in LaTeX is drawn as an equation and stays editable. Insert ▸ Symbol is unchanged.

## The problem

- Equations in a .pptx are drawn as their plain text, so fractions, integrals and exponents come out flat (#148). One deck reported there has 427 equations on 61 of its 68 slides, and it can't be presented.
- Insert ▸ Equation opens a dialog and inserts styled text, not an equation. It isn't saved as an equation and can't be edited as one (#296, #604).

## What this does

**Equations are drawn as equations.** Every OMML equation is laid out in 2-D: fractions, sub- and superscripts, radicals, big operators with limits, brackets that grow with their content, matrices, equation arrays, functions, accents, bars and boxes. It's set in the run's own font through DeckCraft's font database and fallback, so no font is added.

**Insert ▸ Equation types one in place**, at the insertion point or in a new, centred text box:
- With text selected, that text becomes the equation. Otherwise a selected *Type equation here* prompt appears, and typing replaces it.
- You type its linear form: `a/b`, `x^2`, `sqrt(x)`, `\frac{a}{b}`, `\sum_(i=1)^n i`. While the caret is in the equation it shows as that text on a gray field; elsewhere it's drawn in 2-D.
- `\alpha` followed by a space becomes α.
- Right Arrow at the end leaves the equation, so what you type next is ordinary text in the surrounding formatting. Left Arrow there goes back in. A caret just before an equation is outside it, so you can type in front of it or press Enter to move it down. Clicking an equation puts the caret in it.

title: Round chart number format halves away from zero like Excel
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/model/src/numfmt.rs:265` (no existing issue): Chart number formats round halves to even instead of half-up (Excel behaviour).

## Cause
Found while testing `crates/model/src/numfmt.rs:265` (no existing issue): chart number formats round halves to even instead of half-up (Excel behaviour).

`fixed()` in numfmt.rs formats with `format!("{x:.max_frac$}")`. Rust rounds exact binary halves to even, so 2.5 with format `0` gave `2` and 0.125 with `0.00` gave `0.12`. Excel and PowerPoint round halves away from zero.

## Fix
Before formatting, `fixed()` now scales the value by 10^max_frac, rounds it half away from zero, and scales it back. It skips this when the scaled value is 1e15 or more, where f64 spacing is too coarse for the scale-and-round step to be exact. The new test `numfmt::tests::rounds_halves_away_from_zero` covers 2.5, 0.5, 0.125 and -2.5.

## Verified
- Regression test `numfmt::tests::rounds_halves_away_from_zero`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-model rounds_halves_away_from_zero`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Other number format paths, such as scientific and General, are unchanged. Negative values reach `fixed()` as their absolute value, so the sign handling is unchanged.
