title: Presenter view: slide strip with scrollbar along the bottom (#975)
author: RealRules
body:
Fixes #975.

**What.** Presenter view gets a slide strip along the bottom. It shows the previous slide, the current one (outlined in the accent colour) and at least five coming up, with slide numbers underneath. Hidden slides are dimmed and labelled.

- A click on a thumbnail goes to that slide (`ShowState::goto`, as See All Slides does). Clicking the slide already showing does nothing, except from the end screen.
- A scrollbar under the strip moves through the whole deck, by click or drag, without moving the show. When the show moves on, the strip lines up again with the previous slide first.
- It is on by default. A **Slide strip** button next to All slides / Zoom turns it off. The choice is kept in `UiState.presenter_strip` (remembered between shows and sessions) and is also the `show.presenterStrip {on?: bool}` command. The showing state reports `strip`, `stripFirst`, `stripCells` and `stripBar` for the control channel.
- Turning the strip on or off leaves the current-slide and Next previews at the same size when there is room for them. They only shrink when the window is too short for them and the strip.

**How.** All of it is in `crates/ui-egui/src/show.rs` (`presenter_strip` and small pure layout helpers) plus the setting and command in `lib.rs`. Thumbnails are rendered at most three per frame and cached (64 kept, the farthest from the strip evicted first), so a jump across a long deck does not stall the presenter window. Thumbnail sizes go through `textures::fit_size`, and the layout guards NaN and extreme slide shapes (a 1 × 56 slide still fits). There is no `unwrap` outside tests.

title: Keep empty-title slides with a body when importing an exported outline
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/format/src/lib.rs:548 (outline_to_slides) and :628 (slides_to_outline)` (no existing issue): Outline export/import merges a slide with an empty title into the previous slide.

## Cause

title: Format General scientific notation like Excel (1.5E+12)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/model/src/numfmt.rs:115-116 (general)` (no existing issue): General number format writes large and small values as '1.50000E12' instead of '1.5E+12'.

## Cause
`general` formatted values with |v| >= 1e11 or < 1e-9 using `format!("{v:.5E}")`. That gives Rust-style output such as `1.50000E12`, with trailing zeros, no `+` on positive exponents and an unpadded exponent.

## Fix
The scientific branch of `general` now trims trailing zeros from the mantissa. It then writes the exponent with an explicit sign and at least two digits, so the output is `1.5E+12`, `1E-10` and `1E+100`. If the formatted string has no `E`, it is returned unchanged. Zero is already handled earlier in `general`. In the new tests, `format` returned an empty string for infinity, so non-finite values never reach this branch.

## Verified
- Regression test `numfmt::tests::common_codes`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-model numfmt::tests::common_codes`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
Formatting for values between 1e-9 and 1e11, and all other number format codes, is unchanged.

title: README: Linux runtime libraries for tarball and musl installs (#955)
author: FabPei
body:
DeckCraft opens its window-system, GPU and file-dialog libraries when it starts — `x11-dl`,
`xkbcommon-dl`, `ash`, `glutin` and `rfd` reach them through `dlopen` — so none of them is part of
the binary's linked dependencies: `ldd` shows nothing to install, and a machine that satisfies the
`.deb`/`.rpm` dependency list can still die at start-up with a loader error that says nothing about
what is missing. That is the trap a tarball install or a musl system walks into, and the packages
nobody writes down (#955).

The README now writes them down next to the Linux downloads: the libraries that are loaded at run
time — the same set `packaging/linux/nfpm.yaml` declares, and the packages a tarball install or a
musl system has to provide itself — with the `apk` line for Alpine and the `xbps` names for Void's
musl variant, which uses the same loader. The entries that are not self-explanatory are spelled
out: `mesa-vulkan-swrast` as the software Vulkan driver that runs anywhere, Mesa's GL drivers as
the slow CPU fallback rather than a DeckCraft bug, `xdg-desktop-portal` as what the Open and Save
dialogs talk to, and `xkeyboard-config` as the XKB data `libxkbcommon` reads. It also records what
is *not* needed: fontconfig and freetype, because DeckCraft scans `/usr/share/fonts` itself and
embeds its presentation fonts, and `libasound.so.2` is the only linked library of them all —
`deckcraft-cli` needs neither sound nor a display.

Fixes storytold/deckcraft#955

wasm). Every package name was checked against Alpine v3.22 and against `void-packages`, and every

title: Thumbnails: only the slides on screen are rendered
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #969.

The thumbnail bar lays out every slide every frame (`for i in 0..doc.slides.len()` inside a plain `ScrollArea`) and asked `textures.thumb` for each one. The cache holds 600 thumbnails and evicts the 200 least recently used, so on a deck longer than that the bar evicted the thumbnails it had just rendered and started over — for ever. That is the white flashing in the video: every evicted row draws a white placeholder, and `need_more` asks for another frame, so the renderer never goes idle either.

### Measured

A 901-slide deck of blank slides in `egui_kittest`, with the bar showing about six rows:

| frames | cached thumbnails | renders so far |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 30 | 105 | 105 |
| 150 | 465 | 465 |
| 270 | 425 | **825** |
| 330 | 495 | **1095** |
| 390 | 475 | **1275** |

The cache oscillates between about 400 and 600 while the render count climbs without bound — it never settles. After this change, the same deck over the same 400 frames:

| frames | cached thumbnails | renders so far |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 30 | 6 | 6 |
| 400 | 6 | 6 |
| 600 | 6 | 6 |

### What changed

A row that is not on screen asks for nothing: `ui.is_rect_visible(row)` guards the `textures.thumb` call, and only a visible row that is still waiting sets `need_more`. The outline pane already culls this way (`show_viewport` with a 300 px margin, "laying out every slide's editors each frame made a 2000-slide outline crawl") — this is the same idea for the two panes that missed it.

The slide **sorter** has the same unguarded call inside its own plain `ScrollArea`, so it is fixed too; a long deck churned the cache there as well.

### Tests

`the_thumbnail_bar_settles_on_a_deck_longer_than_its_cache` — 900 slides, 400 frames: fewer than 100 thumbnails cached, and 200 further frames with nothing moving render nothing new. On `main` it fails at 424 cached and climbing.

`textures.thumb_renders` is new, alongside the existing `canvas_renders`, so the test can see re-rendering rather th…

title: Control server: a rejected line's reason survives a pipelined peer
author: Hamza0101
body:
A client that sends another line while its previous one is being rejected never sees the reason: the connection is reset and the reply, already written, is discarded. That also makes `a_line_that_is_not_a_request_closes_the_connection` fail about four times in five, which is how I found it.

### Measured

The test opens a client per junk line, writes the junk, then writes a second line, then reads until the connection closes. Running it alone, twelve times:

| | failures |
| --- | --- |
| `main` | **10 of 12** |
| with the second line removed | 0 of 12 |
| with this change (second line kept) | 0 of 12 |

It fails at a random iteration with no replies at all (`assertion left == right failed: []`, `left: 0, right: 1`): the error reply was written and then thrown away.

### Why

`serve` writes the reason and breaks, dropping the socket. The client's second write lands on a socket the server has already closed, the kernel answers it with RST, and an RST discards what it had queued for the client — including the reply. The client reads a connection reset instead of being told why its line was rejected.

The comment there reads "a peer that can't read the reason loses nothing", which is true of a peer that stopped reading; a peer that *is* reading loses the reason, and it is the one that gets reset.

### What changed

`close_politely` shuts the write side down (so the FIN goes out after the reply), then reads and discards for up to the write timeout and at most 64 KiB, so the peer's pipelined line is absorbed rather than answered with RST. Both paths that reject and close use it: a line that is not a request, and a line over the length limit. A peer that keeps talking is still dropped at the deadline.

### Tests

`a_pipelined_peer_still_reads_why_its_line_was_rejected` — twelve rounds of the two-write sequence, each of which must read exactly one reply naming the reason, with nothing dispatched. Without the two `close_politely` calls it fails 9 times in 10; with them, 0 i…

title: Web: the host page supplies fonts through fonts/manifest.txt (#957)
author: FabPei
body:
On the web, DeckCraft only has the faces compiled into the wasm: a deck that needs a brand or
corporate typeface is drawn with a substitute, and a `.pptx` opened in the browser loses its
intended look. Until now the only way in was to rebuild the app, and to redo that at every
release (#957).

This adds the mechanism PhotoCraft already documents in its HOSTING.md, so a host that serves
several crafting apps keeps one fonts directory: the page puts a `fonts/manifest.txt` next to
`index.html`, one face per line as `Family | Style | path/to/file.otf`, and the app fetches those
files before it starts, so the first slide already has them.

- Only the first three fields are read; blank lines and `#` comments are skipped, and the path is
  relative to the page (`crates/fonts::parse_host_manifest`).
- A face is filed under the family it **declares** (name id 16 when the file has one, else id 1,
  through the new `crates/fonts::declared_faces`). When the manifest names it something else the
  browser console says so and the file's own name is kept — that is the name a deck's text asks
  for.
- A page without a manifest starts exactly as it always has: one 404 for `fonts/manifest.txt` and
  the embedded faces only. Files are served as they are; nothing is transcoded or rewritten.
- Documented in `packaging/web/README.md` under Fonts, with the same file name and layout as the
  sibling apps.

Fixes storytold/deckcraft#957

title: Fonts: the macOS scan leaves Office's CloudFonts container alone (#981)
author: FabPei
body:
`deckcraft-cli render` could hang for minutes — for good, in a scripted run — on a Mac with
Microsoft Office installed, behind a macOS "would like to access data from other apps" prompt
nobody was there to answer (#981). The font scan adds
`~/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/FontCache/4/CloudFonts`, and on macOS 14+ that
folder is another app's data: `opendir` blocks until the prompt is dismissed. The scan runs on the
main thread before the first lookup, so the whole render waits behind it — the reported stack is
`FontDb::face → try_family → load_cataloged → ensure_catalog → scan_font_dirs → read_dir →
__opendir2`, at 0 % CPU, with a plain `ls` of the same folder timing out beside it.

The macOS list now lives in `fontdb::macos_font_dirs(home)` and leaves Office's **containers** out —
the narrowest of the issue's three suggestions, and the only one that needs no new timing or
threading. Everything else stays: the system and user font folders, the fonts Office installs
*inside its own app bundles* (bundle data, readable without a prompt), and the
`com_apple_MobileAsset_Font*` assets. The families that lived in the container are still covered —
`substitutes()` maps Aptos and its kin to open faces, which is what DeckCraft would draw with
anyway (the asset policy never ships or depends on Microsoft fonts).

Fixes storytold/deckcraft#981

Validation: `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, pdf-deps, clippy `-D warnings`, tests, assets, layering,
wasm). The regression test `the_macos_scan_leaves_other_apps_data_alone` drives
`macos_font_dirs()` with a fake home, so it runs on every host rather than only on a Mac, and it
was proved red and green: with the CloudFonts line restored it fails at `crates/fonts/src/lib.rs:189`,
without it it passes. It pins what stays (system folders, `~/Library/Fonts`, Office's own app
bundles) as well as what goes (any `UBF8T346G9.Office` path, any `CloudFonts` path).

title: Replace Fonts test: a window wide enough to hold Home's ribbon
author: Hamza0101
body:
`cargo xtask ci` fails at `test` on `main` (9859da3):

```
test replacefonts_tests::ribbon_button_opens_the_dialog_and_replaces ... FAILED
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: None
 right: Some("replaceFonts")
```

Not a regression in the dialog or in `font.replace` — the test's window has become too narrow for the ribbon it clicks in.

**What happens.** `harness()` builds the app at 1400×900. Home's ribbon is now wider than that. Measured at several widths, with the button's rect printed from the harness:

| window | Replace Fonts button rect | dialog after the click |
|---|---|---|
| 1400 | `[[1398.0 127.0] - [1533.8 149.0]]` | `None` |
| 1800 | same | `Some("replaceFonts")` |
| 2200 | same | `Some("replaceFonts")` |

The Editing group begins at x=1398, so in a 1400-wide window two pixels of the button are on screen and its centre, where kittest clicks, is off it. The node is still there and still enabled — `get_by_label` finds exactly one, and `enabled(app, "font.replace")` is `true` — so the test clicks something real and nothing happens. `app.dialog` stays `None` through five further frames.

**The fix.** Give the harness 1800×1100, which the other full-ribbon tests in this crate already use, and say in a comment why the width matters. No non-test code changes.

`cargo xtask ci`: all 7 steps passed (fmt, pdf-deps, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

**One thing for the maintainers, not fixed here.** The ribbon does not scroll sideways, so this is also what a person sees on a 1400-px-wide window: Home's Editing group, the Selection Pane and Design Ideas are partly or wholly unreachable, with nothing to scroll or collapse. PowerPoint collapses groups into a menu as the window narrows. That is a feature decision rather than a gate fix, so I have left it out of this PR — happy to open an issue for it if you'd like.

title: Animations: Anvil, the Keynote-style entrance
author: SimonGadgeteer
body:
## What

A new entrance effect, **Anvil**, the one Keynote users know and miss in PowerPoint. The shape
free-falls from above the slide, squashes on landing (its base stays on the ground), springs back,
and kicks up a puff of dust that billows out sideways. It's in the Animations ribbon's quick gallery
next to Zoom, and in the full gallery and `animation.list`, like any other entrance.

## How

- **anim** (`effects.rs`, `lib.rs`): the `anvil` entrance. A gravity drop (distance ∝ t²) over the
  first 45 % of the effect, then a squash that rings out (`scale_y` down, `scale_x` up, offset so
  the base stays put). New `AnimState::dust` (0..1 puff progress, `#[serde(default)]`); `compose`
  keeps the larger puff, and `sanitized` clamps it.
- **render** (`lib.rs`): `ShapeState::dust` draws soft radial-gradient clouds at the base of the
  shape's (possibly rotated) box. It's deterministic, so every frame and export of a moment match,
  and it uses no filters. Preview and slide show pass `dust` through.
- **pptx** (`write/timing.rs`): PowerPoint has no Anvil, so the catalogue gives it preset id
  **1001** (outside PowerPoint's range) and the writer emits behaviours PowerPoint can play: the
  drop as `ppt_y` key times and an `animScale` squash with `autoRev`. There's no dust in PowerPoint.
  DeckCraft reads 1001 back as Anvil, with no reader change.
- **docs**: `animation-parity.md` gets a "Beyond PowerPoint" note (not counted in the parity
  scores) and a revision row, and `ROADMAP.md` gets a progress-log row.

No new assets, and nothing taken from Keynote: the effect is drawn in code.

## Tests

- New: `anvil_drops_from_above_squashes_and_puffs_dust` checks that the shape starts above the
  slide and accelerates, that it squashes on landing with the base on the ground, that dust appears
  only after landing, and that the end state is identity.
- Existing tests that now cover Anvil: `every_animation_evaluates_finite` and

title: Text: Latin-slot neutrals, centipoint advances, metafile symbol fallback
author: amosarc
body:
## What

Three parity fixes for text in mixed CJK/Latin decks and for WMF equation previews, found on a real Chinese math course deck where an overlaid-equation layout broke: the body text wraps where PowerPoint does not, so the absolutely-positioned equation objects (reserved with runs of spaces) land on the wrong lines.

### 1. ASCII / high-ANSI neutrals take the Latin typeface

Mixed CJK/Latin runs drew spaces, digits and math symbols (`≥`, quotes) with the East Asian typeface: the neutral face assignment inherited the previous character's face, and a CJK punctuation followed by spaces pulled the whole space run into the `a:ea` font. On a real deck that inflated a line by ~43 pt and flipped a wrap.

ECMA-376 classifies those characters by code range: ASCII (spaces, digits, punctuation) and every Common code point outside the East Asian and Arabic ranges draw with the run's Latin typeface whatever surrounds them. `script::latin_neutral` encodes that class; only the Arabic punctuation set, the harakat and BOM-like marks keep following their neighbours (their old path).

### 2. Glyph advances quantize down to hundredths of a point

Office lays text out in hundredths of a point (the `sz`/`spc` unit), quantizing each advance down. With exact font units a knife-edge line (645.26 pt against a 645.2 pt box) wrapped one word early where PowerPoint keeps it; quantized it measures 645.08 pt and fits. Verified against a pixel-measured PowerPoint render: every cluster position on the line matches the Times New Roman advances (including `≥` at 17.56 pt, Latin slot).

### 3. Metafile SYMBOL_CHARSET text falls back to the byte's character

MathType equations write their text with "Times New Roman" in the symbol character set: the bytes decode to U+F000+byte, and where the resolved face has no glyph there (font not installed) the text drew .notdef boxes — or, for the Adobe Symbol font, `map_symbol_bullet` collapsed every unknown code to a bullet (`+` became `•`). `text::metafile_…

title: fix(wasm): instance_id panics on wasm32 — process::id is unsupported there
author: amosarc
body:
## What

PR #390 made every document uid mint go through `recovery::instance_id()`, which calls `std::process::id()` unconditionally. On `wasm32-unknown-unknown` that panics at runtime, so deckcraft-web (and any embedded SlideApp) traps the moment it creates a document. The compile-only wasm gate can't see it.

Move `process::id` (and the `SystemTime` write, already cfg'd) behind `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]`: `RandomState`'s per-process seed keeps the id unique on wasm.

## Tests

`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine recovery` (5 passed); `cargo check -p deckcraft-engine --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` clean.

Found while embedding SlideApp in ppt-live-svr (a lecture-streaming server that embeds the engine in the browser).

title: Order and merge font names by base letter, then accent (NFC = NFD, case-insensitive)
author: nhdai111983
body:
This is not tied to an upstream issue. It is a small gap noted under Localization in `docs/gaps.md`.

## What changes

DeckCraft's font-name lists were ordered by code point after `to_lowercase()` (full Unicode lower-casing, but still code point order), and names were merged by `eq_ignore_ascii_case`, so only ASCII case differences counted as the same name. For a non-ASCII name that is wrong in two ways: `Đồ Hoạ` sorts after `Zapfino` (U+0110 is past `z`), and the same name typed as base letter plus combining marks (NFD, which macOS file names and some IMEs produce) is a different string from the precomposed one (NFC), so it showed up twice. This PR adds a small collation crate and uses it for the three lists:

- **The installed-family list** (`FontDb::families`), **`font.used`** (fonts the deck uses) and the **missing-fonts list** all go through one helper, `sorted_unique_names` (`crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs`, re-exported). It sorts by base letter first, then accent marks (`Ánh` beside `Anh`; `đ` is `d` plus a mark; case ignored; NFC equals NFD; the sort is stable), with every other character (for example `ø`, `ł`, `ß`, Cyrillic, CJK, digits, punctuation) by code point, and, when two names are the same text, keeps the first spelling met. This is the crate's `Root` order; it is not the CLDR/UCA root order. The ribbon font menu is not one of these lists (see Known limits).
- **`font.replace`** (Replace Fonts) matches `from` with canonical equivalence and case-insensitively. The match key for `from` is built once, not per candidate. `from` is limited to 256 bytes like `to`; a longer one returns an error and adds no undo step. title: Charts: a chart's number formats and text sizes survive an edit (#1046)
author: albayazid
body:
First slices of #1046 (the ticket lists three losses; this covers the number formats and the text sizes - the automatic title is a separate fix).

**What was wrong.** `chart.data` rebuilds a chart's XML from the model, and the model did not carry what the file had:

- the number formats - the data labels' own format (`c:dLbls/c:numFmt`) and the format the values are written and read with (the values' cache, `c:numCache/c:formatCode`). Every format became `General`, so PowerPoint showed `50.5%` as `50.5`;
- the text sizes - the data labels' own size (16 pt), the legend's own size (18 pt), the axis labels' size and the title's size. The reader had the axes', the legend's and the title's - collapsed into one `Chart.text_size` - and the writer wrote no `c:txPr` at all, so PowerPoint fell back to its defaults.

DeckCraft's own render of an edited chart still looked right, so only PowerPoint showed the loss. A plain open -> save (`deckcraft-cli convert`) keeps both; only `chart.data` lost them.

**The fix** (`crates/model/src/chart.rs`, `crates/pptx/src/read/chart.rs`, `crates/pptx/src/write/chart.rs`):

- the model keeps the chart's own labels' format and size, the series' own labels' format and size, the legend's own size, the axis labels' size, the title's size, and the format the series' values are written and read with;
- the reader reads them from the file - the labels' and the legend's from their `c:txPr`, the title's from its rich text or `c:txPr`, the values' format from the values' cache;
- the writer writes them back where the file had them: the labels' format and size into the `c:dLbls` it writes, the legend's, the axis labels' and the title's sizes as their `c:txPr`, and the values' format into the values' cache.

The effective label format (the series' own, else the chart group's, else the source data's) is unchanged, so the labels still draw as before.

title: Fix extra empty histogram bin with a fixed bin count
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/model/src/chart.rs:1129-1135 (histogram_bins)` (no existing issue): Histogram with a fixed bin count draws an extra empty bin because of floating-point rounding.

## Cause
With `bin_count = Some(k)`, `histogram_bins` set the width to `span / k` and then computed the bin count as `ceil(span / width)`. Floating-point rounding can push that quotient slightly above `k`, which adds an extra empty last bin.

## Fix
When a fixed `bin_count` is in effect (no valid `bin_size` set), the bin count is now `k` directly, still clamped to `MAX_BINS`. The `ceil(span / width)` computation is kept for `bin_size` and Scott's rule.

## Verified
- Regression test `chart::chartex_tests::histogram_fixed_bin_count_is_exact_despite_float_rounding`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-model --lib histogram_fixed_bin_count_is_exact_despite_float_rounding`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
Bin-size and Scott's-rule binning, the zero-span and degenerate-width fallback to one bin, and the bin-assignment loop are unchanged.

title: Fix Windows clipboard image paste blocker (CF_DIB / CF_DIBV5 decoding)
author: boycececil666gmailcom
body:
## Summary
Resolves #53 and #763 by implementing native Windows clipboard bitmap ingestion (`CF_DIB`, `CF_DIBV5`, and registered `PNG`/`image/png` formats) and enabling image paste via Ctrl+V as well as Ribbon/Context/Edit menu Paste commands.

## Background & Root Cause
On Windows, pasting copied screenshots (Snipping Tool, `Win + Shift + S`, PrintScreen) or browser-copied images into DeckCraft failed:
1. `arboard` only attempts reading registered format `PNG` and `CF_DIBV5`. Most Windows applications and screenshots place `CF_DIB` (standard 40-byte `BITMAPINFOHEADER`) on the clipboard, which `arboard` does not inspect.
2. Even when `CF_DIBV5` is present, `arboard`'s BITMAPV5HEADER tweaking introduces an offset miscalculation with `image::codecs::bmp::BmpDecoder::new_without_file_header`, causing EOF errors.
3. Windows GDI tools (e.g. Snipping Tool) often leave the alpha byte set to 0 on 32-bit BGRx bitmaps, causing decoders that treat 32-bit DIBs as RGBA to generate completely transparent images.
4. When pasting via the UI (Ribbon button, canvas right-click context menu, or Edit menu `edit.paste`), `SlideApp::run` forwarded directly to the engine without checking `services.clipboard_image`.

## Solution
1. **Windows Clipboard Bitmap Parsing (`apps/deckcraft/src/pasteboard.rs`)**:
   - Queries native Windows clipboard formats in priority order: registered `"PNG"`/`"image/png"`, `CF_DIBV5` (17), and `CF_DIB` (8).
   - Reconstructs a valid standard in-memory BMP file by synthesizing a 14-byte `BITMAPFILEHEADER` with exact data offsets for headers, masks, and palettes, avoiding decoder offset mismatches.
   - Provides a fallback uncompressed direct DIB decoder supporting 24-bit and 32-bit bitmaps with custom bitfields and row padding.
   - Handles the GDI zero-alpha quirk: if all pixels in a 32-bit DIB have zero alpha, alpha values are restored to 255 (fully opaque) while preserving genuine transparency when alpha is present.
   - Preserves existing `arboard` behavior…

title: Control server: wait after a failed accept instead of retrying at once
author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

The control server's accepting thread (`apps/deckcraft/src/control_server.rs`) read `listener.incoming().flatten()`, which drops a failed accept and asks again at once. When accepting keeps failing, for example while the process has run out of file descriptors, that thread keeps a core busy until it recovers.

It now waits 100 ms after a failed accept. Accepted connections, the limits and everything after the accept are unchanged. The loop goes through a small `accepted` helper, so the wait can be tested without exhausting file descriptors.

The same change is open in PdfCraft as storytold/pdfcraft#3631, where the single-instance listener already waits like this.

## How you verified it

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy -p deckcraft -j 3 --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test -p deckcraft -j 3 control_server`: 10 passed

**Test.** New `a_failed_accept_waits_before_the_next` feeds the helper two connections around three failed accepts and checks that both come through and that it waits three times. With the old `flatten()` put back into the helper it fails: `left: 0`, `right: 3`.

## Anything a reviewer should look at first

There is no log line on a failed accept: while accepting keeps failing that would be ten lines a second. Happy to add one if you prefer.

title: Make ColorScheme::set accept alias slots like get
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/color/src/lib.rs:266-272 (ColorScheme::set)` (no existing issue): ColorScheme::set silently ignores the alias slots (Bg1, Tx1, Bg2, Tx2, PhClr) that get() accepts.

title: Reject invalid slide index params instead of using the selection
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/slide.rs:234 (delete); same pattern in index_of :182, move_slide :269, duplicate :193 and section_add :534` (no existing issue): slide.delete with an invalid (negative or non-integer) index deletes the currently selected slide.

## Cause
`usize_param` returns `None` for a present but invalid value such as -1 or 1.5. `slide.delete`, `slide.duplicate`, `slide.move` (`from`), `section.add` (`at`) and `index_of` treated that as an absent parameter. title: Escape carriage return as  in XML text content
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/pptx/src/xml.rs:363 (esc)` (no existing issue): XML text escaping writes carriage returns raw, so they turn into line feeds on reload.

`esc` wrote '\r' as a raw character in text content because `xml_char` allows it. The reader normalises every literal CR or CRLF to LF (XML 1.0 §2.11), so text containing '\r' came back with '\n' after a write and re-read.

## Verified

title: PPTX: text keeps the colours of the deck's default text style (#810)
author: FabPei
body:
Opening this .pptx turned every text colour black: white, yellow and light blue text on a dark background came back unreadable, while the same file kept its colours in Google Slides (#810).

A run that sets its own colour is imported; a run that takes its colour from the deck's default text style was not, so it resolved with no fill at all and drew the plain default. A plain text box has no placeholder of its own, which makes it exactly this case: `resolve::master_list_style` falls back to the presentation's default text style and `resolve::level_style` adds it as the base of every level.

`crates/pptx/src/read/dml.rs` parsed only the per-level `a:lvl1pPr`…`a:lvl9pPr` entries of an `a:lstStyle`-like element and dropped `a:defPPr`, the element ECMA-376 defines as the defaults every level inherits. `a:defPPr` is now read into the same `ListStyle` and applied as the base of all nine levels, for every element `list_style` maps — `p:defaultTextStyle`, the master's `p:titleStyle`/`p:bodyStyle`/`p:otherStyle`, the notes style and a shape's own `a:lstStyle`. A level that carries its own `a:lvlNpPr` still wins; it inherits whatever it leaves unset instead of starting from nothing.

What changed:
- `crates/pptx/src/read/dml.rs` — `list_style` parses `a:defPPr` and uses it as the base of every level.
- `crates/pptx/tests/default_text_style.rs` — new regression test.

title: Strip URI fragment before percent-decoding OPC targets

title: macOS: open documents from Finder (double-click, Open With, Dock)
author: fedehsq
body:
Finder hands files to an app through a kAEOpenDocuments ('odoc') Apple event, not argv. DeckCraft declared no CFBundleDocumentTypes and winit 0.30 doesn't handle the event, so AppKit refused every double-click with "DeckCraft cannot open files in the Office Open XML presentation format", even with DeckCraft set as the default app for .pptx.

- apple_events.rs: register an NSAppleEventManager handler before the event loop through fmv-macos-events (as GridCraft does, since the workspace forbids unsafe) and open the paths via open_from_system, so a double-clicked .ppsx starts its slide show like it does from argv. title: Packaging: pin the signing client and appimagetool, and check their hashes
author: aiongg
body:
Both release tools were downloaded at whatever version was current, with no check. They are now pinned the same way as in designcraft:

- `packaging/windows/sign.ps1` downloads Microsoft.Trusted.Signing.Client 1.0.95 from NuGet and stops unless its SHA-256 is `3bfcf1e0a3cb42af1692f0a8ed45c15de070c2de86f28a59b2795d904d8a920f`. The working folder gets a random name and must not exist yet.

title: Keep rounded corners round in non-uniformly scaled groups
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1083

## Cause
Shape geometry was built from the shape's size in the group's child coordinates. The group's uneven scale was then applied to the finished path, so a roundRect's circular corners were stretched into ellipses.

title: text: CJK document families resolve to their open twins; spAutoFit single-line labels never wrap
author: amosarc
body:
## What

Chinese course decks set their Latin runs in Times New Roman and their CJK in 黑体/微软雅黑.
When those proprietary families are missing, 黑体 et al fell down the Calibri chain: the CJK
1em glyphs still broke lines the same way, but **spaces and digits narrowed**, so space-padded
layouts shifted and the overlaid labels (归纳, equation objects) were covered.

- `substitutes()` / `has_metric_twin()` gain the CJK mainstays: 黑体/SimHei, 微软雅黑/等线 →
  Noto Sans CJK SC (+Source Han Sans SC); 宋体/SimSun → Noto Serif CJK SC. CJK glyphs are 1em
  in both, so line breaking is unchanged; spaces/digits widen to the open face.
- A `spAutoFit` text box whose saved height fits exactly one line renders **unwrapped**: it is
  a single-line label the author sized by fit-to-text, and folding it at the stored width broke
  WPS-authored labels (变式3：) in half. Boxes saved with more lines keep wrapping.

## Tests

- `cjk_document_families_resolve_to_their_open_twin` (skips when no Noto/Source Han face exists)
- `single_line_autofit_labels_never_wrap` (one-line autofit label stays one line; a two-line
  saved box keeps wrapping)

title: Fix scientific number format for subnormal values
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/model/src/numfmt.rs:204-211 (sci)` (no existing issue): Scientific number format prints 0.00E-01 for very small (subnormal) values.

## Cause
In `sci`, the mantissa was computed as `v / 10f64.powi(exp)`. For subnormal values, `10f64.powi(exp)` underflows to 0, so the mantissa became infinite. The `!m.is_finite()` fallback then zeroed the mantissa and exponent, and `5e-324` printed as `0.00E-01`.

## Fix
For `exp < -300`, the mantissa is now computed in two steps, `v * 1e300 / 10f64.powi(exp + 300)`, so the divisor no longer underflows. `5e-324` now formats as `4.94E-324`, and `f64::MIN_POSITIVE` formats as `2.23E-308`. A regression test covers both values.

## Verified
- Regression test `scientific_subnormal`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-model scientific_subnormal`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
The `!m.is_finite()` fallback and the normal-range path are unchanged. I did not test negative subnormal values.

title: Add angle adjust handles to partial-circle presets
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1094

## Cause
`build()` creates the pie, chord, arc and blockArc presets with an empty handle list, so the canvas has no yellow dots to draw even though the presets have adjust values. `Handle` also only supported straight-line handles (`origin + dir * value`), so it had no way to represent start and end angle handles.

`Handle` now has an `angle` kind: its position sits on the ellipse at the visual angle of the adjust value, and `value_at` turns the pointer's angle around the centre back into 1/60000-degree units. title: Use chrono instead of hand-rolled UTC conversion
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary

DeckCraft had hand-rolled copies of Howard Hinnant's `civil_from_days` /
`civil` (the `146_097` / `719_468` magic numbers) and a hand-written
weekday / leap-year / days-in-month calendar in the date-field code. This
routes them through `chrono`.

chrono is **already** a workspace dependency (used by `crates/text`), so this
reuses that entry rather than adding a second version — the engine and the
desktop app now carry `chrono = { workspace = true }`.

Follow-up to storytold/cadcraft#1785 (reference PR storytold/cadcraft#1789).

Functions replaced and their formats:

- `apps/deckcraft/src/logging.rs` — `timestamp`
  (`2026-10-08T07:59:17.728Z`, UTC, ms; pre-1970 clamped to the epoch). Deleted
  the private `civil_from_days`.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/design.rs` — `civil` (days since 1970 → (y, m, d)),
  used by `review.rs` for comment timestamps (`2026-10-10T13:10:35Z`), now uses
  `chrono::NaiveDate`.
- `crates/text/src/datetime.rs` — `DateTime::is_valid` (was a hand-rolled
  leap-year / month-length check) and `DateTime::weekday` (was a hand-rolled
  days-since-1970 + weekday computation) now use `chrono::NaiveDate`
  (`from_ymd_opt`, `weekday().num_days_from_sunday()`). The date-field output
  strings (`datetime1`…`datetime13`, locale ordering) are unchanged.

Each converted helper keeps a small proleptic-Gregorian fallback for dates
outside `chrono::NaiveDate`'s range (year ≤ 0 or > 262143), so nothing the old
code accepted changes or panics. `DateTime::now_local` already used chrono's
clock (gated off wasm); that is untouched.

## Testing

With `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` on a scratch dir, building and testing only the
affected packages:

- `cargo test -p deckcraft-text` — all pass (every `datetime*` field-format
  test, locale ordering, and the impossible-date / weekday tests).
- `cargo test -p deckcraft-engine` — all pass, including `design::civil_dates`
  and the review comment-timestamp paths.

title: Show: hold the left mouse button for the laser pointer (#1012)
author: Zetenypapp
body:
**Upfront about how this was made:** I'm not a programmer. The change, the test and this description were written by Claude (Claude Code, Opus 5.5), on Windows 11.

Closes #1012.

## The request

In PowerPoint, holding the left mouse button during a slide show shows the laser dot for as long as it's held, and letting go doesn't advance. In DeckCraft, the laser needed Ctrl+L or the on-screen button, which is awkward with a mouse or clicker in hand.

## The change

In the slide show, pressing the left button on the slide and holding it for 0.3 s shows the laser dot in the show's laser colour. The dot follows the pointer and leaves no ink. Letting go hides it, and that release is not a click, so the slide doesn't advance and no build or trigger runs. A quicker click advances exactly as before.

The hold only applies where a click on the slide would: not with the pen (it keeps drawing), not with the Ctrl+L laser already on, and not on See All Slides, a black or white screen, a zoom, the reading-view bar or the media controls. The dot also appears if the pointer doesn't move during the hold.

The pieces of the request I left out:
- the setting to turn the gesture off
- long-press on touch
- the dot in Presenter View and on recordings

Presenter View and recordings are close to #636, which is still open.

## Testing

- New UI test `show::tests::holding_the_left_button_shows_the_laser_without_advancing` (egui_kittest, real pointer events):
  - a quick click advances
  - a hold shows nothing before 0.3 s and the dot after it, and letting go hides the dot without advancing

title: Render: 3-D sizes in a scaled group stay in points
author: pick2510
body:
## What

A group's child coordinates scale its shapes' boxes, but 3-D sizes kept in points (extrusion depth `sp3d extrusionH`, contour width `contourW`, bevel `bevelT w/h`) stay points, as PowerPoint draws them. DeckCraft applied them in the group's child space, so the child-coordinate scale multiplied them.

Found on a real-world deck (not attached, private): small 3-D icons drawn in a legacy group whose child space is 1360 units across 61 pt. Each icon's 1 pt contour was drawn several hundred points wide, a curved band across the whole slide, and the extruded bars ran off towards the vanishing point. PowerPoint shows small cubes on domes.

## How

`per_point()` (next to `line_space`/`text_space` in `crates/render/src/lib.rs`) gives the shape-space units per point, i.e. the inverse of the child-coordinate scale that `line_space` already separates out for line widths. The extrusion depth, the contour width and the bevel's width and height go through it before drawing. Outside a group it is 1, so ungrouped shapes draw exactly as before.

## Tests

`group_child_scale_does_not_scale_3d_depth_contours_or_bevels`: the extruded, contoured and bevelled shapes of `extruded_deck()` plus a bevelled rectangle are drawn in a group at 1:1 and again in a child space scaled by 100. The two must match within 5% of the inked pixels. Before the fix: 381,014 inked pixels against 94,820.

PowerPoint still draws long extrusions on very small shapes longer than DeckCraft does. The perspective distance in `camera.rs` is fitted in multiples of the shape's size (`D = dist · max(w, h)`), which foreshortens a depth many times the shape's size more than PowerPoint does. That's a …

title: Open PowerPoint 97-2003 .ppt/.pot/.pps files (#239)
author: OliWoly
body:
Closes #239.

DeckCraft can now open the legacy binary PowerPoint formats. It's import only: there is no `.ppt` writer.

## What's in it

- **New crate `deckcraft-ppt` (L3)**, written from Microsoft's published Open Specifications [MS-CFB], [MS-PPT] and [MS-ODRAW]:
  - a compound-file reader, ported from FilmCraft's clean-room `filmcraft-cfb` (same owner and licence), with every read checked and every chain bounded
  - the edit chain and persist directory, and the slide, master and notes lists
  - OfficeArt drawings: shape types mapped to presets, freeform paths, groups (children placed in slide points), rotation, flips, fills (solid, gradient, picture, texture), lines and arrowheads, shadows
  - text with its paragraph and character formatting, with the master's text styles resolved into it; bullets; slide-number and date fields
  - pictures (PNG, JPEG, DIB, TIFF, and deflated EMF/WMF), speaker notes, hidden slides
  - each main master becomes a master with the standard layouts, carrying its colours, fonts, text styles, background and decorations; a title master becomes a layout of its master
- **Engine:** `open_checked` tries the importer after the PPTX checks. An encrypted `.ppt` gets the same "password-protected" message as an encrypted `.pptx`. Like an outline import, an opened `.ppt` has no save path, so Save asks for a new name and never writes another format under the `.ppt` name.
- **UI:** File › Open filters, drag and drop, and the web shell accept `.ppt`, `.pot` and `.pps`. A `.pps` handed over by the system starts the slide show, as a `.ppsx` does.
- **Packaging:** the macOS document type (Viewer role) and `com.microsoft.powerpoint.ppt`, the Windows `SupportedTypes` and `OpenWithProgids` entries, and the Linux `application/vnd.ms-powerpoint` MIME type. `every_desktop_offers_the_same_file_types` now maps one MIME type to several extensions.

title: security: enforce HTTPS on curl downloads (SonarCloud S6506)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Enforces HTTPS on `curl` downloads flagged by SonarCloud rule **S6506** (`shell:S6506`, `docker:S6506`, `githubactions:S6506`, Security).

These `curl` calls use `-L`/`-fsSL` (follow redirects). A redirect could transparently downgrade to plaintext HTTP, exposing the download to MITM tampering. Adding `--proto '=https'` forces curl to refuse any non-HTTPS protocol, including across redirects, without changing behavior for the legitimate HTTPS endpoints already in use.

## Change
`curl <args>` → `curl --proto '=https' <args>` on each flagged line.

🤖 Generated to address SonarCloud findings.

title: Text: table text takes the master's other-text style
author: pick2510
body:
## What

PowerPoint lays out a table's text in the master's other-text style (`p:otherStyle`), while shapes and text boxes take the presentation's default text style (`p:defaultTextStyle`). DeckCraft gave table cells the default text style too.

The two styles usually share a size, so the difference rarely shows. Where they differ, the table text comes out at the wrong size. On a real-world deck (private, not attached) whose `defaultTextStyle` is 20 pt and `otherStyle` 18 pt, a table's text was drawn 2 pt too large, its cells wrapped, and its rows grew past the slide's footer. PowerPoint's PDF of the same slide measures 18 pt: Arial's ascent plus descent is 20.1 pt high there, with 21.1 pt between lines.

## Evidence

A synthetic deck written by DeckCraft, with `defaultTextStyle` at 26 pt and the master's `otherStyle` at 14 pt, holding a table, a rectangle with text and a text box, none of them with a size of their own. In PowerPoint for Mac 16.114's PDF export, the table cell is 14 pt and the rectangle's and text box's text is 26 pt.

On a private corpus of 166 real-world decks (3,690 visible slides), compared with PowerPoint's PDF exports, exactly one slide changes, from 6.7% of pixels differing to 0.4%. The other decks use the same size in both styles.

## How

- `resolve::master_list_style`: a shape whose kind is `Table` takes `master.other_style`, also when it sits in a content placeholder (checked with a second probe, see the review thread). `level_style` takes nothing from placeholder parents for a table. Other placeholders keep their own groups, and other shapes keep `default_text_style`. `level_style` still adds `default_text_style` after it, so anything `otherStyle` leaves unset still comes from there.
- `Shape::table_cell(body)` builds the throwaway shape every cell layout goes through as a table: drawing and row heights (`render/table.rs`), text placement (`render/placed.rs`), and the caret and selection in a cell (`engine/cmd/text.rs`). The table shape …

author: pick2510
body:
## What

Bar and column series that PowerPoint draws hatched, or empty with an outline, came out in the palette's accent colours:

- **Pattern fills** (`c:ser/c:spPr/a:pattFill`) weren't read at all.
- **`a:noFill`** was read, but the chart renderer reduces every fill to one colour and fell back to the palette for anything but a solid fill, so an empty series was filled anyway.
- **Bar outlines** (`c:spPr/a:ln`) weren't drawn.

## Evidence

A synthetic column chart written by DeckCraft, with three series edited to have a red-on-yellow `dkDnDiag` pattern, `a:noFill` with a 3 pt blue `a:ln`, and `a:noFill` with no line. In PowerPoint for Mac 16.114's PDF export, the first is the pattern, the second an empty bar with a blue outline, and the third nothing at all, with legend keys to match. DeckCraft now draws the same.

On a private corpus of 166 real-world decks (3,690 visible slides; not attached), compared with PowerPoint's PDF exports, five chart slides of one deck (hatched "embodied carbon" series next to empty "operational" ones) improve, from about 5–7% of pixels differing to 3–4%. No slide gets worse. What's left on those slides is the axis scale and the `openDmnd` tile's look, both separate from this change.

title: Use a relative coefficient threshold in trendline equations
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/model/src/trendline.rs:~507 (poly_equation)` (no existing issue): Trendline equation label shows 'y = 0' for small-valued data because of an absolute coefficient threshold.

## Cause
poly_equation set the term-skip threshold to `max(|coeff|).max(1.0) * 1e-8`. Because of the `.max(1.0)` floor, any coefficient below 1e-8 was always dropped, however small the data was. As a result, linear, polynomial and log trendlines fitted to tiny-valued data displayed `y = 0`.

## Fix
The skip threshold is now relative to the largest coefficient magnitude, with no floor. It uses `<=`, so an all-zero fit still shows `y = 0`. The check that shows a coefficient of about 1 as a bare `x` keeps its old tolerance of `scale.max(1.0) * 1e-8`.

## Verified
- Regression test `trendline::tests::equation_keeps_tiny_coefficients`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-model --lib trendline::tests::equation_keeps_tiny_coefficients`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `control_server::tests::a_line_that_is_not_a_request_closes_the_connection`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
Number formatting (`num`) and the exponential and power equation paths are unchanged.

title: fix(cli): support --cmd-file for batch commands (#1098)
author: Zaxaerith
body:
## Problem
`deckcraft-cli run` requires each command in a separate `--cmd` argument. Large scripts exceed Windows' command-line length limit before the CLI can start, and JSON must also be quoted for the shell.

## Implementation
- Add repeatable `run --cmd-file FILE`, retaining command sources in argument order alongside existing `--cmd` values.
- Read UTF-8 files one line at a time with the standard library. Skip blank lines and full-line `#` comments, trim surrounding whitespace, and accept CRLF and an optional initial UTF-8 BOM.
- Extract the existing `id[=JSON]` parsing and `Session::execute` path into a small helper used by both sources. Bare command ids still receive an empty JSON object; inline command syntax, diagnostics and `--print` output are preserved.
- Attach the file path to open errors and the physical, one-based line number to line-reading, JSON and execution errors.
- Propagate the first error immediately, so later commands and final `--save`/`--export` actions are not reached.
- Update CLI usage/details and the required minimal ROADMAP entry. No dependencies, engine changes or unrelated refactoring.

The existing input/sample selection, output-format validation, save and export paths remain in place.

## Regression coverage added
Five integration tests in the existing CLI test module cover:
- Multiple file commands executing in order, with bare ids and JSON parameters.
- Unicode text, filenames containing spaces, embedded `=` and `#` inside JSON strings, skipped blank/comments, whitespace, BOM, CRLF and a final line without a newline.

title: Show: Presenter View only with a second display
author: melandur
body:
With one display the presenter window opened on the same screen as the show. Under Hyprland's focus-follows-mouse, whichever window the pointer was over took full screen, and the hidden one stalled every frame: the show lagged, dropped key presses or froze.

One display now shows only the slides; Presenter View needs a second display.

Will be rebased onto #433 once it lands, using its `SlideApp::displays` instead of the separate count below (see the discussion in the comments).

title: Thumbnails: count the renders, not only the thumbnails held (#969)
author: Hamza0101
body:
The follow-up @skylartaylor asked for on #1038:

> Your `thumb_renders` counter is still a good idea, and it would be welcome as a small follow-up to strengthen the test.

#1011 was the right fix, and its test asserts the number of thumbnails **held** settles. That number cannot see the thing #969 actually was: a pane that renders the same rows *over and over*. The held count settles at the rows in view whether the pane rendered them once or a thousand times — the flashing white was the rendering, not the holding.

`Textures::thumb_renders()` counts the renders, so a settled pane is one that has stopped asking for them.

### What the new tests assert

```
at rest, 800-slide deck:   8 held, 8 rendered
ten more frames:           0 further renders                 ← the new assertion
after a 40,000 pt scroll:  24 rendered in total              (the rows it landed on and
                                                              passed over, not the deck)
ten more frames:           0 further renders
```

plus the same settle check for the Slide Sorter.

### Why the counter earns its keep

With the cache made to thrash — its 600-entry limit cut to 4, so the rows in view are evicted and re-rendered every frame — **#1011's Slide Sorter test still passes** (the held count settles at 4) while this one fails:

```
the_sorter_of_a_huge_deck_renders_only_the_slides_in_view ... ok        ← false green
a_settled_sorter_renders_nothing_more ................... FAILED
    255 renders for 4 thumbnails
```

```
title: Keep the slide backdrop while animations play
author: kbarni
body:
In an animation each frame is completely re-rendered, backdrop included. 
This can take a long time especially when the slide background is long to render - for example when there's an effect.
A full-slide layout picture with an 18 pt glow cost ~345 ms of the ~390 ms frame (2-3 fps at 1080p). 

This PR will render the background once (it doesn't change during the animation), and draw only the slide's shapes during animation.

Solves issue #1147

### Change (`crates/ui-egui/src/show.rs`)

- While a step or triggered animation plays, a frame renders only the slide's shapes (`SlidePart::Content`) and lays them over the slide's backdrop, rendered once and kept. The overlay is a premultiplied "over" blend.
- The backdrop is stored per slide, frame size and document, so an edit, a resize or another slide renders it again.
- While a slide that has animations is waiting for the next click, its backdrop is rendered on another thread, so the first animation frame doesn't wait for it. On the web, which has no threads, the first animation frame renders it.
- Frames that aren't animating and the next-slide prefetch still render the whole slide, as before.

Backdrop graphics no longer take shape states during animations. This matches Morph, whose frames already leave them out, because their ids can clash with the slide's shapes.

### Result

- About **28 ms a frame** instead of about 390 ms (rendering plus compositing for a master slide containing a 18 px glow effect).
- In the app, with Presenter View off: **21 frames** during a 1 s fade, against 3 before.

title: Better dual screen and Wayland handling
author: kbarni
body:
While working on https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/pull/1161 I noticed other issues affecting the presentation performance.

The **Presenter View** opened whenever its setting was on, which is the default, however many screens were connected.
DeckCraft never chose a screen for either window, so both usually landed on the same screen and one covered the other. Rendering with vsync, a covered window waits up to about a second for the compositor to let it draw. Presenter View is drawn within the main window's update, so the whole show stalled: an animation drew one or two frames and looked like it never played.

Another thing I noticed is that **DeckCraft prefers X11** whenever `DISPLAY` was set, so on a Wayland desktop it ran through Xwayland.

### Change

**Multiple monitor handling as in PowerPoint** (`crates/ui-egui`, `apps/deckcraft`):
- **Two screens or more:** the slides go fullscreen on another screen (`ViewportCommand::SetMonitor`), and Presenter View goes fullscreen on the presenter's screen (`ViewportBuilder::with_monitor`). That's the screen DeckCraft is on, or else the system's main screen.
- **One screen:** only the slides are shown.
- **After the show:** the main window goes back to where it was, at its old size. X11 otherwise brought it back on the slides' screen.
- **Screen list:** the desktop app provides it through a new `Services::screens` hook, built on winit's `available_monitors`. Wayland can list a screen twice; such duplicates count once. `winit` becomes a dependency on all desktop platforms; it's the same 0.30 that eframe already uses.

**Start on Wayland in a Wayland session** (`apps/deckcraft/src/display.rs`):
- Deckcraft now starts on Wayland when `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set, and on X11 when it's the only display server.
- `DECKCRAFT_X11=1` asks for X11 anyway. `DECKCRAFT_WAYLAND` is no longer read, since Wayland is now the default.
- The workaround for a leftover `DISPLAY` with no X server behind it is gone; it no longer matters.

title: Reject invalid row/col index in table row and column commands
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs:234-238 (at), via crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs:318 (usize_param)` (no existing issue): table.deleteRow and the other table row/col commands treat an invalid (negative or non-integer) index as absent and edit the selected cell or row 0.

## Cause
`at()` in the table commands read `row` and `col` with `usize_param`, which returns None for a negative, fractional or string value just as it does for a missing key. A present but invalid index therefore fell back to the selected cell or to 0, so `table.deleteRow {row: -1}` deleted row 0.

## Fix
`at()` now returns a Result and reads `row` and `col` with `opt_usize_param`. A present but invalid index returns an error and leaves the table unchanged. The selection fallback applies only when the key is absent. The callers are the row/column insert and delete commands, `table.split`, `table.columnWidth` and `table.rowHeight`. All of them propagate the error.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::table_row_col_commands_reject_an_invalid_index`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib table_row_col_commands_reject_an_invalid_index`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The error message for the insert and delete commands names the internal operation (for example `table.rowAbove`) instead of the full command name. I did not change how `rows_cols` is called. Other commands that use `usize_param` were not changed.

title: Use scale-relative degeneracy check in linear trendline fit
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/model/src/trendline.rs:281-313 (linreg)` (no existing issue): Linear trendline fit fails for data with very small x values because of an absolute determinant threshold.

## Cause
`linreg` rejected fits when the determinant `n*sxx - sx*sx` was below an absolute 1e-18. The determinant scales with x², so valid data with tiny x values (around 1e-10) was treated as degenerate and no trendline was produced. The fixed-intercept branch had the same problem with its absolute check on `sxx`.

## Fix
The determinant is now compared against `1e-12 * n * sxx`, so the check scales with the data. The fixed-intercept branch now only rejects `sxx <= 0`. A regression test fits x = 1e-10..5e-10 against y = 1..5.

## Verified
- Regression test `trendline::tests::linear_fits_tiny_x_values`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-model linear_fits_tiny_x_values`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The other trendline types (polynomial, exponential, log, power, moving average) are unchanged.

title: Use evaluated field values in the placed text so the PDF text layer shows the slide number (#1153)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1153.

## Cause

`place_text` (`crates/render/src/placed.rs`) laid the text out with the slide's field values (`deckcraft_text::layout` swaps each `RunKind::Field` run for `fields.field_in(..)`), but stored the original body in `PlacedText`. A slide-number field keeps its saved text (`‹#›`) in `run.text`, so the PDF text layer (`text_layer` in `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs`) cut the layout's character ranges out of the saved placeholder: page 2 drew "2" but its text layer said `‹`.

## Fix

`place_text` now gives `PlacedText` a copy of the body where each field run holds the value the layout drew. It uses the same lookup as the layout: the run's resolved language and `field_in`, and it keeps the saved text when there is no value. The body text and the layout's character offsets now match. Date and footer fields get the same treatment, because they go through the same lookup. Links still come from the original body, so they are unchanged.

## Test

`placed_text_holds_the_field_value_not_the_saved_placeholder` (crates/render): a slide-number field on slide 2 now places the body text "2", and the layout runs end at offset 1. Without the fix the body text is the saved `<#>`.

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Text fields now display their resolved values when placed on a slide. For example, slide-number fields show the number for the current slide, while unresolved fields remain unchanged.
  * PDF text layers now include resolved text field values and preserve text across line breaks. Date fields and other time-based content use a consistent time when rendered and placed, avoiding discrepancies between displayed and extracted text.

title: Cap the PDF slide raster by total pixel count (#1178)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1178.

`Exporter::slide()` in `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs` rendered each slide at the requested dpi, limited only by the renderer's per-side clamp (`MAX_SIDE`, 16,000 px). A slide at the 20,000 pt `sane_len` limit exported at 600 dpi became 16,000 x 16,000 px: about 1 GB of RGBA for each of the two rasters per page (backdrop and content), plus the copies made on the way to the PDF writer.

The scale now comes from a small `raster_scale` helper. It computes the same dpi-based scale as before, and if width x height would pass 64M pixels it scales both sides down by the same factor, so the slide's aspect ratio stays the same. 64M is the budget `cmd/compress.rs` already uses for decoded images. Ordinary slides are not affected: a 16:9 slide at the 600 dpi maximum is 8,000 x 4,500 px (36M), so it keeps its requested dpi. The `PdfOptions::dpi` doc comment now mentions the cap.

Test: `raster_scale_caps_total_pixels_not_each_side` checks that a 20,000 pt square slide at 600 dpi stays within the pixel budget, and that a normal 960 x 540 slide at 200 dpi keeps exactly the scale it had before.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

  * Slides within the limit continue to use the requested resolution.

title: fix(pptx): keep pictures that carry an SVG through Office's SVG extension
author: arc-uri-el
body:
PowerPoint stores an SVG picture as an `a:blip` whose extension list holds an `asvg:svgBlip`, usually with a PNG fallback in the blip's own `r:embed`; some generators write no fallback. The reader only looked at `r:embed`, so saving turned an SVG-only picture into an empty shape and dropped the SVG, leaving PowerPoint an empty slide. A picture with a fallback lost its SVG and kept only the PNG. `PictureFill::svg` now keeps it, and the writer writes the extension back as PowerPoint does. Changing the picture, applying an artistic effect, removing the background or cropping the raster drops the SVG so the old image doesn't show through. Displaying SVGs is still #297.

title: PDF export: a slide number is searchable as its number, not the saved field text (#1153)
author: Zetenypapp
body:
**Upfront about how this was made:** I'm not a programmer. The fix, the test and this description were written by Claude (Claude Code, Opus 5.5), on Windows 11.

Fixes #1153.

## The bug

A slide with a slide-number field, exported to PDF, draws its number ("2"), but the invisible text layer holds the field's saved text `‹#›`. So `pdftotext`, search and copy find `‹` instead of the number.

The PDF text layer (and the notes and handout pages' master text) built each run's text from the model runs' saved `text`. The text engine lays out something different: a field's current value, and a line break as `\u{b}`. The glyph runs' character ranges index into that laid-out text.

## The fix

- `deckcraft_text::shown_paragraphs` returns each paragraph's text as `layout` lays it out. It shares one function (`shown_run`) with layout, so the two can't drift apart.
- `PlacedText` carries that text (`shown`).
- Both PDF text-layer writers take their text from it instead of the saved runs.

What's drawn doesn't change. Only the text layer does: it now matches the page.

  - a three-slide deck with "Page " plus a `slidenum` field on each slide, exported as slides
  - the text read back from each page through the font's ToUnicode map is "Page 1", "Page 2" and "Page 3"

title: Make chart axis flatness thresholds relative to data magnitude
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/model/src/chart.rs:775-794 (axis_scale); same pattern in nice_scale :817` (no existing issue): Chart axis scale ignores tiny data: an absolute 1e-12 threshold turns an axis for values around 1e-13 into 0..1.

The flatness checks now compare against `1e-12` times the data magnitude. The `max(1.0)` fallbacks, including the fixed-limit branch in `axis_scale`, now use the data magnitude and fall back to 1 only when the data is all zero. The file's original CRLF line endings are kept, so the diff contains only these edits and the new test.

title: Animation Pane: Play From the selected effect
author: marcoarnulfo
body:

DeckCraft's pane always played the whole slide from the start. This is the "Preview from the selected effect" row in `docs/animation-parity.md` and the open part of gap 10 in `docs/gaps.md`.

title: Design Ideas: no ideas for slides with diagrams, connectors or other graphics (#1200)
author: xc4pr
body:
## Summary
Design Ideas offered its text arrangements on slides that also hold a diagram, and applying one broke the slide. Each filled box with text was restacked as a body paragraph, while arrows, connectors and other shapes without text stayed where they were, on top of the moved title and text. Now ideas are offered only when everything visible on the slide is something an idea can arrange.

## Root cause
`roles()` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/ideas.rs` sorts a slide's shapes into the title, the largest picture and "text", which is any other shape with non-empty text. Nothing looked at the rest of the slide. A diagram box counted as text. Connectors, groups (including SmartArt), tables, charts and shapes without text were ignored and left in place while the idea moved everything around them.

## Fix

In the sample deck, the title slide (gradient band) and the closing slide (moon) lose their ideas along with the diagram slide, because every text idea would put the title or text box over those shapes. title: fix(engine): isolate embedded fonts per presentation
author: mrzv
body:
## Problem

DeckCraft's process-wide font database deduplicates loaded faces by family/style. Two presentations embedding different subsets or metrics under the same family/style therefore collide: the later document can render with the earlier document's face.

## Change

This now includes the application integration requested in review, not just a caller-facing font API.

- Add `FontDb::add_document_fonts(Vec<(Vec<u8>, String, String)>)` for bytes, declared source family and private alias. Select matching collection families before the renamed-single-family fallback; preserve styles and weights.
- Install supported embedded fonts when constructing each engine document, using distinct runtime aliases. Resolve explicit, theme, script-slot, bullet and metafile font lookups through that document's aliases without rewriting semantic font names.
- Keep private faces out of global family discovery and implicit fallback. Retain source-family identity for symbol remapping and style selection.
- Keep the active document's original embedded-family names available in the font picker, without exposing aliases or another document's private families.
- Scope WMF/EMF raster caching by font-map identity while continuing to share ordinary raster-image caches.
- Preserve source font scope for Paste Special → Picture. Formatting-preserving paste transfers needed source-only embedded families and their media, retains an existing destination family, and resolves the actual inserted formatting before text fitting. Plain-text paste does not import discarded formatting.
- Preserve original family names in the model, UI, native files and PPTX exports. Runtime aliases are not serialized. Unsupported MicroType handling remains unchanged; this does not unload registered faces.
- Merge current upstream `main` and retain both sides of the documentation updates.

## Coverage

author: xc4pr
body:
## Summary
Choosing another Design Idea after "Full-bleed picture, title on a band" now takes the band away again, so the title has no fill of its own. Before, the 86% white fill stayed on the title and showed as a stray white box beside the picture or over the text.

## Root cause
`apply_idea` gave the title the band fill for Full-bleed and left the title's fill alone for every other idea, so the fill outlived the idea that added it.

Not covered: a title that had its own fill before Full-bleed does not get that fill back when you switch (Full-bleed replaces it, as before, and Undo restores it). title: Slide show: play media actions and action sounds on click
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
`docs/gaps.md` ▸ "Interactive decks" says a click on a shape whose action plays media does nothing in the show. Action sounds didn't work either: the reader keeps `a:snd` and `endSnd` on a link, but the show never used them. This PR makes both work, in two commits. The second one can be reverted on its own.

### 1. Slide show: play media actions and action sounds on click

- `ShowState::click` (anim) returns `Click::Media(shape)` when the clicked shape's action is `PlayMedia`. `follow` only sees the action, so it can't name the shape. The show stays on the slide.
- The show (ui-egui) starts that clip the same way a Play effect in the click sequence does. Clicking a clip that sits directly on the slide already toggled play/pause (`media_hit`), and I left that alone. What's new is a clip inside a group, which no click reached before.
- When you click a shape or a text link that has a sound, the sound plays on the voice the show already uses for transition sounds. There is one voice, so a new sound replaces the one playing. The action itself still runs.
- The sound starts before the next slide's media starts. So if the click goes to a slide with a transition sound, the transition sound is the one you hear.
- Stop Previous Sound (`endSnd`) stops that voice and every audio clip the show is playing. Videos keep playing.

### 2. Keep sound-only actions (`Action::NoAction`)

- In Action Settings, Action: None + Play sound is saved as `ppaction://noaction` with an `a:snd`. Until now the reader dropped the whole link, so the sound was lost too.
- Now the link is kept when its sound resolves (a part in the package or a linked file), or when it has `endSnd`. A bare `noaction`, or one whose `a:snd` points at a missing part, is still dropped. Otherwise it would be a dead link that eats the click and stops the slide from advancing.
- The writer saves `NoAction` as `ppaction://noaction`. The Action dialog shows it as None.

Presenter View drew the notes from `Slide::notes_text()` as a single plain label, so bullets, numbers, indents and bold/italic were lost, while the notes pane (from #168) lays them out with `bullets()` and `galley()` in `notes.rs`. body:
Makes `cargo xtask ci` faster and its target dir smaller, following the measurements in storytold/craft-common-actions#60.

title: CI: shared gate workflow; FreeBSD nightly and on release
author: aiongg
body:
Switches DeckCraft's CI to the suite's shared gate workflow and takes the slow platform builds off the pull-request path. **Depends on storytold/craft-common-actions#69**; merge after it. Until then this PR's CI fails, because `gate.yml` doesn't exist yet.

- `ci.yml` calls `storytold/craft-common-actions/.github/workflows/gate.yml@main`. That workflow brings the cached apt install, nextest, rust-cache saved only from main (keyed on the root `Cargo.toml`, so profile changes start a fresh cache), and a check that `Cargo.lock` is unchanged. Every push to main now runs to the end, and pushes to a PR branch cancel its older run.
- `freebsd.yml` runs nightly, on pushes to `release`, and on PRs that change the workflow itself, instead of on every dependency change. Same pattern as storytold/designcraft#455.
- `windows-arm64.yml` runs nightly instead of weekly.

The speed changes to `cargo xtask ci` are in #1213. Every craft app gets the same pair of PRs. Background: storytold/craft-common-actions#60.

title: PDF export keeps only web and mail links
author: oracola91
body:
## What users risk today

PDF export turns every slide hyperlink into a PDF link, whatever it points at (`ClickAction::Url { url } => LinkAction::new(url.clone())` in `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs`). A .pptx can carry any link target. So a deck from someone else can put a `javascript:`, `vbscript:` or `data:` link into a PDF that I then export and share, a link that starts an OS protocol handler (`ms-msdt:`, the Follina handler; `ms-word:ofe|u|\\host\…`; `ldap:`), or a link to another machine: a UNC path, `//host/share`, `file://host/...`, `smb://host/...`, or a Windows Search link whose `crumb=location:` names a share. On Windows, opening a link to a share makes the system connect to that host over SMB, which can leak the reader's NTLM credentials.

## The fix

PDF export now writes a URL link only when `safe_url` allows it: `http`/`https` with a host, and `mailto`. That is the check the slide show already uses before it opens a clicked link, so the show and the exported PDF agree. `safe_url` moves from `deckcraft-anim` (`show.rs`) to `deckcraft-model` (`text.rs`, next to `Action`), which both crates already depend on; `deckcraft_anim::safe_url` stays as a re-export.

Only the link annotation is left out: the text and the slide look the same, and links between slides are unchanged. Local `file:` and relative links are left out for now, as asked in review; whether they should export is a maintainer call.

An earlier version of this PR used a denylist. It is replaced: a denylist can't keep up with protocol handlers.

## Test

- `unsafe_url_links_are_not_exported` (`crates/pdf/src/tests.rs`) builds one slide with 2 safe links (https, mailto) and 18 that must not export: scripts, `data:`, network shares, Windows Search, `ms-msdt:`, `ms-word:` with a share, `ldap:`, `file:///%5C%5Chost/share`, a local `file:///` path and a relative path, with case and control-character variants. It exports the deck and reads the URI of every link annotation back. Only the 2 safe ones may be th…

title: Save as Picture… on a shape's right-click menu writes the selection as one picture
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1073.

Right-clicking a shape, or a selection of shapes, now offers **Save as Picture…**, between Link… and Edit Alt Text… as in PowerPoint. It asks where to save, suggesting `Picture.png`, and writes the selected shapes as one picture cut to them, not the slide. Microsoft's page ([Save a picture or other graphic as a separate file](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/graphics-visuals/save-a-picture-or-other-graphic-as-a-separate-file)) puts it on the right-click menu for "photos, shapes, charts, SmartArt graphics, digital ink, and text boxes": you then pick the file format in the "Save as type" list.

There's no new renderer. The new `shape.saveAsPicture` command (`{path, format?, ids?, scale?}`, so MCP and the CLI can use it too) draws with `render_shapes`, at the same 2 px per pt that File › Export uses for pictures. It writes through `io::write_file`, which keeps the automation write root, and I added it to that list in `docs/mcp.md`.

How it behaves:
- **Formats:** PNG (the default) and TIFF keep the background see-through. JPEG, GIF and BMP put the shapes on white the way the GIF export does; otherwise the dropped alpha channel would make the background black.
- **Shapes inside a group:** a shape picked inside a group is saved as the slide shows it. It is lifted out of its groups with the same transform Ungroup uses (`child_to_parent`), so a resized or rotated group gives the shape its size and turn.
- **Stacking:** the shapes keep their stacking order on the page, whatever order they were picked in. A shape picked together with its own group is drawn once, with the group.
- **Ids:** an id that isn't on the page is an error, and nothing is written.
- **Size and resolution:** the picture's longer side stops at `render_shapes`' 2048 px. The PNG and JPEG then record the resolution the shapes were actually drawn at, which is 144 dpi below the cap. TIFF and BMP carry no density.
- **Margin:** the picture takes in what each shape draws outside its box:…

title: Show: refuse a show.start from that is not a slide
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
`show.start` now refuses a `from` that is not a slide of the deck instead of quietly playing something else.

Before, `{"from": -1}`, `{"from": 1.5}` or `{"from": "1"}` started the show on slide 0, and a `from` past the end opened a show already on the end screen, with an ok answer both through the command and the control channel. Both paths now go through one check and answer with an error (`` `from` is not a valid index: -1 ``, `no slide 3`), the same way the slide commands reject a bad index since #1063. A hidden slide is still accepted, since From Current Slide plays a hidden slide. `from: null` now means "no `from`" (the first slide of the show order) rather than slide 0; happy to switch if you'd rather keep that. With no document open, `{"from": 0}` now answers `no slide 0` instead of an ok that did nothing; `show.start {}` is unchanged. An unknown `custom` show name still does nothing silently; I left that alone here.
```
