author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1217.

Set Transparent Color was a submenu with a colour grid. Its Eyedropper never started: the submenu is not a `color_popup`, so it never notes itself as the open colour menu, and `eyedropper::begin` returned early (or, if another colour menu had been open before, handed the colour to that one). The grid colours did reach `picture.transparentColor`, but the renderer clears only pixels within a few levels of the chosen colour, so a theme colour almost never matches anything in a photo — hence "no effect".

PowerPoint has no grid there: choosing Set Transparent Color changes the pointer and you click the colour in the picture ("Select Set Transparent Color. When the pointer changes, select the color you want to make transparent", [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-gb/office/make-a-picture-transparent-in-word-128bfdb6-9906-4f9d-b4c6-e5aa22ba082f) — the Word page; it's the same Picture Format ▸ Color command in PowerPoint). This PR does the same, reusing the Eyedropper pointer from #367/#834 with a second mode:

- `picture.transparentColor` accepts `at: [x, y]` (slide units) and takes the colour of the picture's **own** pixel under that point, mapping back through rotation, flips, groups, the stretch rect and the crop. Sampling the drawn slide instead would pick up corrections, recolouring and resampling and miss the stored pixel again. A spot that is already transparent is refused ("that spot of the picture is already transparent"): its hidden RGB is usually black, and taking it would clear the black drawn elsewhere, e.g. the text of a logo on a transparent background. `color` and `none` work as before.
- Picture Format ▸ Color ▸ Set Transparent Color is now a plain entry that arms the pointer; a click on the picture runs the command, Esc or a click off the slide cancels.

The grid's "None" entry goes away with the grid, as PowerPoint's menu has none either: Reset Picture or Undo removes the transparent colour, and `{"none": true}` stays in …

title: Shape Fill and Shape Outline: the button applies the last colour picked from its menu
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1080.

Shape Fill and Shape Outline now remember the last colour picked from their menu, and a click on the button itself applies it to the current selection again, in both Home and Shape Format. Before a colour has been picked the buttons keep applying Accent 1 and Text 1 as they did. Picks made through More Colors and the Eyedropper count too, since they come back through the same grid. On Shape Format the Outline button's main click was ignored; it now does what the Home one does. The Outline button on Home used to force 1 pt; it now sets only the colour and leaves the weight alone (a shape with no outline gets one with the default weight).

This follows what Microsoft Office does with its split colour buttons: the button applies the last colour used. I could not find a Microsoft page that states this for Shape Fill, so the references are third-party: Daktronics' Venus 1500 training handout on changing font colour in Office ("The Font Color button always displays the color that was used most recently", https://c-5762-20150521-www-daktronics-com.i.icims.com/Web%20Documents/Venus-1500-Tutorials/Changing-Font-Color.pdf) and Indezine's PowerPoint shape-fill tutorial (https://www.indezine.com/products/powerpoint/learn/fillslinesandeffects/2016/add-solid-fills-to-shapes.html). Happy to adjust if you have a first-party source or see the behaviour differently.

Left out of this PR, to keep it small: line weight and dashes as things the button remembers (the issue also mentions the line style), and the same scheme for Font Color and Highlight, which still apply a fixed colour. No Fill / No Outline chosen from the menu do not become the remembered value (not verified against PowerPoint). The remembered colour lasts for the session; it is not saved in preferences. No colour bar is drawn on the icon (the Font Color buttons have one).

title: Compute RBSP stop bit once instead of per more_rbsp_data call
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1168

## Cause
`BitReader::more_rbsp_data` scanned the buffer backwards from the end to find the stop bit on every call. The H.264 slice decoder calls it once or twice per macroblock. A slice padded with megabytes of zero bytes therefore cost O(macroblocks × padding) CPU time.

## Fix
`BitReader::new` now finds the stop-bit position once and stores it in a `stop_bit` field. `more_rbsp_data` compares the current position against that stored value.

Verified: `tests::more_rbsp_data_does_not_rescan_trailing_zeros` fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it. `tests::more_rbsp_data_positions` checks the stop-bit position semantics and passes with and without the fix. Run with `cargo test -p deckcraft-bitstream more_rbsp_data`. `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Verified
- Regression tests `tests::more_rbsp_data_does_not_rescan_trailing_zeros`, `tests::more_rbsp_data_positions`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-bitstream more_rbsp_data`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
The H.264 slice decoder callers are unchanged. The separate `BitReader` in the av1 crate is also unchanged.

title: Canvas: scroll bars when the zoomed slide is larger than the window
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1157.

A slide zoomed past the window now gets a horizontal and/or a vertical scroll bar, one per axis that overflows. Dragging a thumb pans the slide to every edge, and a click on the track beside the thumb moves one window's length toward it. The bars drive the same offset the wheel and trackpad already use, so wheel panning and the zoom anchor from #106 keep working, and the wheel also pans while the pointer is over a bar. When the slide fits there are no bars, so the wheel still turns the page as before.

PowerPoint's Normal view shows scroll bars on the slide pane when zoomed in. I couldn't find a Microsoft support page that describes them, only Microsoft Q&A threads from users ([1](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5369593/how-do-i-stop-powerpoints-vertical-scroll-bar-from), [2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5265932/horizontal-scroll-on-power-point)). One thing I left out on purpose: in PowerPoint the vertical bar also moves to the next slide when it hits the end. Here it only pans the zoomed slide; happy to add that if you want it.

The bars are drawn over the canvas edge (10 pt, inside the area around the slide) rather than shrinking the canvas, so the fit and the zoom layout don't change, and they stay clear of the rulers when those are on. Happy to switch to a reserved strip if you prefer.

title: H.264: the inverse transforms clamp coefficients to the spec r range
author: SusieeTheLinuxUser
body:
Refs #1183 (extends its grouped codec-overflow list; the transforms were not on it)

## What was wrong

Opening a crafted H.264 stream panicked a debug build inside the inverse transforms. The
dequantisation deliberately wraps (`scale4`/`scale8`/`luma_dc_dequant` use `wrapping_mul`,
pinned by the existing `huge_levels_dequantise_without_overflow_panics` test), so the
coefficients reaching `idct4_add` and `idct8_add` (`crates/h264/src/transform.rs`) can be any
i32 — and their butterflies add in plain i32. `idct4_add(&[i32::MAX; 16], …)` panics at the
first `r[0] + r[2]` with "attempt to add with overflow"; `idct8_add` likewise at `d[0] + d[4]`.
Release builds wrap (memory-safe, wrong output); debug builds — including UI-thread decodes
per #1166/#1183 — abort.

Unreported before: audit #1183 lists debug-only codec overflows at the POC (`slice.rs`),
MMCO/ref-list (`dpb.rs`) and HEVC sites, but not the transforms. The sibling SoundCraft
decoder had the same class (its H.264 arithmetic audit item; fixed there with the same
approach), which is where the pattern was proven reachable from crafted streams.

## What changed

`idct4_add` and `idct8_add` clamp their transform-domain input to −2^15..2^15−1 before the
butterflies (new `r_clamp` helper). ITU-T H.264 8.5.12.1 / 8.5.13.1 leave the transforms'
output unspecified for a dequantised r outside that range, so conforming streams are
bit-exact (the clamp is a no-op for every in-range coefficient, including the huge-but-in-range
levels of lossy-but-valid streams); out-of-range values produce defined clamped output instead
of a panic. Downstream intermediates from clamped inputs stay far inside i32 in both passes.

## Test added

`transform::tests::huge_coefficients_are_clamped_to_the_spec_r_range` — idct4 with
`[i32::MAX; 16]`, `[i32::MIN; 16]` and alternating extremes, idct8 with `i32::MIN`/`i32::MAX`
coefficients; asserts each result equals the transform of the spec-clamped input. **Panicked
before the fix** with "attempt …

title: H.264: temporal direct mvs are scaled in i32 and clipped to the spec range
author: SusieeTheLinuxUser
body:
Refs #1183 (extends its grouped codec-overflow list) · **Refs storytold/soundcraft#994**
(the same decoder code's reviewed fix; its mvL1-derivation shape is followed exactly)

## What was wrong

Opening a crafted B-slice panicked a debug build in the temporal direct motion derivation
(`crates/h264/src/slicedec.rs`, inline in `derive_direct`): the scale
`(dsf · mvCol + 128) >> 8` was truncated with `as i16`, wrapping mvL0 past the spec's
motion-vector range, and `m0[0] − mv_col[0]` (plain i16 subtraction) then panicked with
"attempt to subtract with overflow". `dsf` is clamped to [−1024, 1023] in `SliceDecoder` and
co-located mvs are i16, so crafted streams reach e.g. dsf 1023 × mvCol 32767 → a truncated
mvL0 of −49, and −49 − 32767 overflows. Unreported before (audit #1183 lists POC/MMCO/HEVC
overflow sites, not this one); the sibling SoundCraft decoder hit the same defect and fixed
it first — including a review correction (storytold/soundcraft#994): **mvL1 must be scaled from the
unclamped mvL0 with only the results clipped** (dsf 512, mvCol [32767, 0] keeps mvL1 at
[32767, 0]; deriving it from the clipped mvL0 wrongly gave [0, 0]).

## What changed

The derivation moved into a small testable associated fn,
`SliceDecoder::temporal_direct_mvs(dsf, mv_col)` (8.4.1.2.4): the scale and the mvL1
subtraction run in i32 (cannot overflow with |dsf| ≤ 1024), and only the two results are
clipped to −2^15..2^15−1 — the storytold/soundcraft#994 shape. For every input whose results were
already in range the values are unchanged (the old `as i16` was an identity there and the
old subtraction did not overflow), so conforming streams decode exactly as before.

## Test added

`slicedec::tests::temporal_direct_mvs_at_i16_extremes_stay_in_the_spec_range` — sweeps
DistScaleFactor extremes (−1024, −1, 256, 1023) with i16-extreme co-located mvs and asserts
every derived mv stays in the spec range; checks dsf 256 is the identity scale (mvL0 = mvCol,
mvL1 = 0); and pins the storytold/soun…

title: Media: a clip opened from a .pptx gets its length and size from its headers
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #1241.

A `.pptx` doesn't store a clip's length or picture size, so a video or audio clip opened from one had `duration_ms`, `width` and `height` at 0. `media.info` reported zeros, and the media control bar showed a 0 length until the clip first played.

- `deckcraft-media`: `probe_headers` is `probe` without the decode that measures a raw MP3 or ADTS stream with no length in its headers. `probe` calls it, then decodes as before.
- `deckcraft-engine`: opening a `.pptx` fills each clip's missing length and size from `probe_headers`, once per media item. This covers `file.open`, `file.openBytes`, `slide.reuse` and compare, which all read `.pptx` through `open_checked`. Opening never decodes a whole audio file (#1162), and `read_presentation_file` still runs off the UI thread.
- Test: insert a video, save to `.pptx`, reopen; `media.info` reports the same `durationMs`, `width` and `height`. It fails without the fix.

## Checks

`cargo xtask ci` at `29b2450` on Linux, with craft-fonts at `43913056` (the ref CI uses): all 8 steps passed. 1,789 tests passed, 6 skipped; wasm ok for 23 crates.

title: Fix arrange.distribute span to use the selection's full extent
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/arrange.rs:325-327 (distribute)` (no existing issue): arrange.distribute uses the last shape's right edge as the span end, pushing a wide middle shape outside the selection.

## Cause
When distributing relative to the selection, `distribute` took the span end from the right (or bottom) edge of the last shape sorted by left (or top) edge. A wide middle shape can extend past that edge. The span then came out smaller than the combined shape sizes, the gap went negative, and shapes were packed outside the original bounds.

## Fix
The span now runs from the minimum left (or top) edge to the maximum right (or bottom) edge across all selected shapes. A regression test covers the case of a wide middle shape.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::distribute_wide_middle_stays_in_selection_bounds`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib distribute_wide_middle`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
Distributing relative to the slide, and the gap and positioning logic, are unchanged.

title: Reject '+'-signed numeric character references in HTML paste
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/richclip.rs:301-304 (numeric_char, used by decode_text)` (no existing issue): HTML paste decodes numeric entities with a '+' sign (&#+65; becomes 'A').

## Cause
`numeric_char` parsed entity digits with `str::parse::<u32>()` and `u32::from_str_radix(.., 16)`. Both accept a leading '+', so the malformed references `&#+65;` and `&#x+41;` were decoded as 'A' instead of being kept as typed.

## Fix
`numeric_char` now returns None unless the digits are non-empty and every character is a valid digit for the radix (decimal, or hex after the x/X prefix). Malformed references then fall through to the existing keep-as-typed path in `decode_text`. The new test covers both '+' cases and checks that `A` and `A` still decode to 'A'.

## Verified
- Regression test `cmd::richclip::tests::signed_numeric_entities_are_kept_as_typed`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib signed_numeric_entities_are_kept_as_typed`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
The similar '+' issue in `Rgba::from_hex` is a separate parser and is not changed here.

title: Reject invalid index in slide.hide and slide.layout
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/slide.rs:376 (hide); same pattern at slide.rs:445` (no existing issue): slide.hide with a negative or non-integer index hides the currently selected slide.

## Cause
`slide.hide` and `slide.layout` read `index` with `usize_param`. That helper turns a negative or non-integer value into `None`, the same as a missing key. Both commands then fell back to the selected slides, so a bad index acted on the selected slides and reported success.

## Fix
Both commands now read `index` with `opt_usize_param`. A present but invalid index returns a "not a valid index" error. A missing or null index still falls back to the selection. The regression test checks `-1` and `1.5` for both commands and that no slide ends up hidden.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::slide_hide_and_layout_reject_invalid_index`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib slide_hide_and_layout_reject_invalid_index`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
Other callers of `usize_param` are unchanged.

title: Media: a video with an unsupported codec says only its audio plays (#1237)
author: SusieeTheLinuxUser
body:
**Part of:** #1237 (the black video needs a VP8 decoder, a feature left out here; the missing audio did not reproduce, so the PR asks the reporter to confirm whether the audio plays with this build)

## What was wrong

A WebM whose video track is VP8 (the codec of the reporter's file-examples sample and most
stock WebM samples) renders as a black box, and the insert says nothing about it:

- DeckCraft has no VP8 decoder (`VideoDecoder::open` → "VP8 video isn't supported"), so there
  is no poster at insert and no frame ever decodes — the slide shows the near-black media
  placeholder. Only VP9/AV1/H.264/HEVC video is documented as supported; a VP8 decoder is a
  feature, not this fix.
- The Vorbis audio track *does* decode and play. Because of that, `insert.video` answered
  `playable: true, warning: null`: the "can't be played" warning only covers the case where
  *nothing* in the file is decodable. The user gets a permanently black, silent-looking box
  with no explanation — which is exactly how the report reads: "renders black with no audio".

The reported missing audio itself is **not reproducible**: through the real `insert.video` →
`media.play`/`MediaHost::play` → `Player` path, the Vorbis track of a VP8+Vorbis WebM decodes
and sounds. Verified on current main (b913c4f) *and* on v0.10.0 (b47195f, the reporter's
build; the playback path is byte-identical there), across mono/stereo, 22.05/44.1/48 kHz,
both ffmpeg Vorbis encoders, alternate cluster layouts, and .mkv — every variant played

## Root cause

`crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs` `media()`: the insert warning was computed only from
`playable` (= *something* decodable), so a video clip with a decodable audio track and an
undecodable video codec got `warning: null`.

title: PDF export: keep line breaks in the text layer's paragraph text
author: narain1
body:
## Problem

A paragraph with a line break (Shift+Enter) has its characters scrambled in the PDF text layer. Text after a break is read from one position too early, so search and copy give wrong text. In a table cell I saw `BETA` come out as `ETAG`.

## Cause

`text_layer` and `master_text_pieces` in `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs` build each paragraph's string with `p.runs.iter().map(|r| r.text.as_str()).collect::<String>()`, then cut the laid-out run's character range out of it. A `RunKind::Break` run has empty `text` but occupies one character in the layout, because `Run::content()` returns `"\u{b}"` for it. The string is one character short per break, so every later range is shifted.

## Fix

Build the string with `Paragraph::text()`, which is a sum of `Run::content()` and so counts a break as one character like the layout does. This covers both sites: the slide text layer, and the notes and handout master text.

## Tests

`crates/pdf/src/tests_line_breaks.rs` adds two regression tests:

- `line_breaks_preserve_actual_pdf_text_and_native_character_ranges` exports a slide for several paragraphs with breaks (leading, consecutive, trailing, and accented or Greek text with combining marks). It checks that the layout's character ranges index the paragraph text and that the extracted PDF text equals the source with the breaks removed.
- `line_breaks_preserve_master_pieces_and_notes_handout_pdf_text` checks `master_text_pieces` and the exported text on notes and handout pages, where the master header text has breaks.

Both fail on `main` and pass with this change. `cargo fmt --check` is clean and the 17 tests in `deckcraft-pdf` pass.

## Overlap with open PRs

#1192 and #1197 rewrite the same two lines for a different bug (slide-number fields, #1153): #1192 switches them to `r.content()` and #1197 to a precomputed `shown` string. Either also fixes this line-break bug, and I checked that applying only #1192's two `content()` hunks makes these tests pass. Neither adds a test for …

title: Text: AutoFormat starts bulleted and numbered lists as you type
author: dotCooCoo
body:
Typing `* ` or `1. ` at the start of a paragraph left the characters as typed. PowerPoint's AutoFormat as you type turns such a paragraph into a bulleted or numbered list ("Automatic bulleted and numbered lists"), and `docs/gaps.md` listed it as missing next to the ordinals rule from #856.

Microsoft's description of the feature: https://web.archive.org/web/20240714081832/https://insider.microsoft365.com/en-us/blog/automatic-bullet-formatting-in-powerpoint-for-the-web (the symbols and numbers, the space that starts the list, Backspace to revert). The two-dash lead for the square bullet comes from https://web.archive.org/web/20260608185337/https://office-watch.com/2023/use-the-fast-list-shortcuts-in-powerpoint/, and the hyphen lead and the tab from Microsoft's AutoFormat as you Type page for Word and Outlook: https://web.archive.org/web/20260526195210/https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/autoformat-as-you-type-195c72fc-5e3f-43d5-a0c3-bf3606e2e58e

What changes:
- A paragraph that holds only `*`, `-` or `–`, `--` or `—`, `>`, `<>`, `1.`, `1)`, `I.`, `i.`, `A.`, `a.` or `a)` before a typed space or tab becomes a list paragraph with a bullet from the Bullets gallery (•, –, ■, ➢ or ◆) or the matching numbering scheme. The typed lead and space are removed. `<>` gives ◆, the gallery's nearest bullet to the reference app's four-diamond bullet, and `-` gives the same – bullet as `–`.
- The list is applied with `format.bullets` or `format.numbering`, and the keystroke and the list are one undo step.
- Backspace right after the change puts the typed lead, the space and the paragraph's formatting back.
- Tools ▸ AutoCorrect has an "Automatic bulleted and numbered lists" checkbox, and `text.autocorrect` takes and reports `lists`. Like the ordinals rule, it runs only while AutoCorrect is on.
- `ROADMAP.md` and `docs/gaps.md` record it.

title: Decode numeric tab entities in HTML paste
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/richclip.rs:304 (numeric_char, used by decode_text)` (no existing issue): HTML paste leaves the tab entity 	 as literal text.

## Cause
`numeric_char` rejected every control character except '\n'. A tab is a control character, so `	` and `	` were treated as malformed entities and kept as literal text.

## Fix
`numeric_char` now also accepts '\t', so `a	b` decodes to `a\tb`. A regression test covers the decimal and hex forms.

## Not changed
Other whitespace controls such as '\r' and form feed are still rejected. I did not change them.

title: security(engine): check regular file and size bound on read, preserve permissions and symlinks on save
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
Addresses findings 50, 58, 73, and 79 in `storytold-deckcraft-agent-findings.json`:

- **Finding 58** (`crates/engine/src/io.rs`): Before reading, verify that the opened handle is a regular file and impose a 2 GiB byte limit, preventing unbounded buffering of special/endless devices (e.g. `/dev/zero` or FIFOs) from exhausting host memory.
- **Finding 73** (`crates/engine/src/io.rs`): Canonicalize the save path to resolve symlinks before creating the atomic sibling temporary file and renaming, ensuring saves update the target rather than breaking the symlink and replacing it with a regular file at the link's path.
- **Finding 79** (`crates/engine/src/io.rs`): Query and preserve existing destination permissions before atomic renaming, preventing restricted files from being replaced by world-readable files under the default umask.
- **Finding 50** (`crates/engine/src/recovery.rs`): Set mode `0600` on Unix when creating AutoRecover files, ensuring temporary and recovered dirty presentation contents are not readable by other unprivileged local users.
- Added unit tests in `crates/engine/src/io.rs`.

title: Tables: dragging across cells selects a range of cells
author: dotCooCoo
body:
A drag inside a table selected text in the cell where it started and never left that cell, so there was no way to select a range of cells with the pointer. `docs/ui-parity.md` listed it as missing ("no cell-range selection by dragging across cells"). The engine already had a cell range (`table.selectCells`), and Merge Cells, Shading, Borders, Cell Margins and Align read it, but no gesture set it and the canvas did not show it.

PowerPoint for Mac's steps for merging cells start with "drag the pointer across the cells that you want to merge", and the steps for deleting cell content say that the cell itself is not deleted: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/merge-split-or-delete-table-cells-in-powerpoint-d58e60ea-8994-4356-b1ef-5437ea59fd9b. title: Reject '+' sign in OPC target percent-decoding
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/pptx/src/opc.rs:263-277 (percent_decode, used by resolve)` (no existing issue): OPC target percent-decoding accepts a '+' sign, so '%+5' becomes a control character.

## Cause
percent_decode parsed the two characters after '%' with u8::from_str_radix(h, 16), which accepts a leading '+'. A target like 'a%+5b.png' was decoded to the control byte 0x05 instead of staying literal, so the part name no longer matched the part in the package.

## Fix
percent_decode now decodes only when both characters after '%' are ASCII hex digits. Otherwise the '%' is kept literally. A regression test covers '%+5' staying literal and '%20' still decoding to a space.

## Verified
- Regression test `opc::tests::resolve_percent_decode_requires_two_hex_digits`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-pptx resolve_percent`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
The '+' parsing problems in Rgba::from_hex and in HTML numeric entities are separate functions, and I didn't change them.

title: fix(codecs): harden media decoders against resource amplification and unbound state
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary

Hardens media and video/audio codec decoders against resource amplification, unbounded state accumulation, and DoS vectors:

- **Ogg recovery buffer reuse (Finding 29)**: Replaces repeated full-window buffer allocations with a retained, reused search scanner and enforces a cumulative recovery-work budget (`CaptureScanner`).
- **Opus empty packet handling (Finding 40)**: Skips empty stored Opus packets in Ogg and Matroska streams instead of invoking loss-concealment audio synthesis.
- **Opus decoded PCM memory budget (Finding 63)**: Enforces an aggregate decoded PCM budget (`MAX_PCM_SAMPLES`, 64M samples / 256 MiB) in planar conversion.
- **H.264 DPB reference eviction (Finding 56)**: Validates MMCO 6 against `max_long_term_frame_idx` and evicts entries to guarantee the retained references never exceed DPB capacity.
- **HEVC missing reference frame sharing (Finding 57)**: Reuses a shared gray replacement frame across missing references and bounds missing reference creation to DPB capacity.

- **AV1 nonuniform tile bounds (Finding 89)**: Enforces `MAX_TILE_COLS` and `MAX_TILE_ROWS` in nonuniform tile layouts, matching uniform layout guarantees.

body:
## What

PowerPoint draws a picture's own fill (`p:pic/p:spPr`, e.g. `a:solidFill`) behind the picture, so it shows through the picture's transparent pixels. DeckCraft drew a picture's outline but never its fill.

Old equation objects rely on this. An embedded object (`p:oleObj`, progId `Equation.3`) has a fallback `p:pic` whose `spPr` puts the equation's transparent WMF on an orange or yellow box. The reader took only that picture's image as the object's preview, so the boxes disappeared too.

## Evidence

- **Synthetic probe.** A deck written by DeckCraft with one half-transparent PNG three times: no fill, `solidFill FF9900`, and `solidFill FFFF00` with a 3 pt blue `a:ln`. In PowerPoint for Mac 16.114's PDF export, the orange and yellow boxes show behind the image, with the outline around the yellow one. DeckCraft now draws the same; before, it drew only the outline.

- `render/lib.rs`: the shape-fill loop (sub-paths, `useBgFill`, `grpFill`, fades) moves unchanged into `Renderer::fill_geometry`. title: MCP: keep serving when the app isn't open yet (#1248)
author: galagersharp-code
body:
Fixes #1248.

`deckcraft-cli mcp --connect` exited at once when the app wasn't running ("can't reach the app…"), so the client marked the server failed for its whole session and opening DeckCraft afterwards didn't help.

The server now falls back to a lazy remote, the way lightcraft-cli already behaves:

- `initialize` / `tools/list` / `resources` answer normally;
- a tool call returns "DeckCraft app at … is not reachable: …; will retry on each call";
- the first call that finds the app's port open connects and carries on. A lazy remote describes itself as waiting until it has connected, and its describe goes into the server instructions.

`Remote::lazy` shares the send/receive/reconnect logic with `connect` (one new `connected` flag gates the description and the retry hint; nothing else changes). Regression test: `a_lazy_remote_serves_once_the_app_opens` (fails with the retry hint while nothing listens; connects and answers once a listener is up). `docs/mcp.md` documents the behaviour.

`cargo test -p deckcraft-mcp` green (20), clippy clean, `deckcraft-cli` compiles.

title: Charts: a written chart carries the text sizes it is drawn at
author: pick2510
body:
## What

A chart written from the model (every chart made in DeckCraft, and an edited one) had no text sizes in its XML. PowerPoint then draws its axis labels and legend at its 10 pt default and its title at 18 pt, whatever the chart's size. DeckCraft draws them sized to the chart, so a DeckCraft-made chart looked quite different once opened in PowerPoint.

## Evidence

A synthetic deck written by DeckCraft, with a 560×360 and a 300×200 column chart, each with a title and a legend, exported as PDF from PowerPoint for Mac 16.114 (sizes measured from the PDF's word boxes):

| | DeckCraft draws | PowerPoint before | PowerPoint after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 560×360: axes, legend / title | 16 / 22 pt | 10 / 18 pt | 16 / 22 pt |
| 300×200: axes, legend / title | 9 / 13 pt | 10 / 18 pt | 9 / 13 pt |

The first run, with sizes of 16.36 and 22.91 pt written, showed that **PowerPoint draws chart text at whole points** (16.36 → 16, 22.91 → 23, 12.73 → 13, 9.09 → 9). So DeckCraft's automatic sizes are now whole points too, and the two agree exactly.

On a private corpus of 166 real-world decks (3,690 slides compared with PowerPoint's PDF exports), nothing changes, as expected: PowerPoint's own charts carry their sizes and are written back from their kept part.

## How

- `Chart::text_sizes(w, h)` (model) holds the rule the renderer used: the file's sizes, otherwise `min(w, h) / 22` clamped to 7–18 pt, with the title 1.4 times that, now rounded to whole points. The renderer and the writer both use it.
- `write/chart.rs`: `chart_xml_in(c, frame)` writes those sizes for the chart's frame (`chart_rel` passes the shape's size). title: Control server: a peer refused as busy still reads why, and two tests no longer race
author: dotCooCoo
body:
`a_pipelined_peer_still_reads_why_its_line_was_rejected` and `blocked_ui_times_out_and_full_queue_is_busy` fail intermittently on `main`. On Windows 11, 9 of 40 runs of the `deckcraft` binary's tests failed, and 17 of 80 failed with eight copies running at once. Two of the causes are in the server.

### What changed

- When every connection slot is taken, the accepting thread wrote the busy reply and dropped the socket, so a peer that had already written a line saw a reset instead of the reason. The busy path now closes like a rejected line (#1039): it sends the FIN and drains for at most 250 ms, or the write timeout when that is shorter.
- `close_politely` set its read timeout on the writing handle and read through a `try_clone` of the socket. On Windows, a read timeout set on one handle of a `try_clone` pair can fail to apply to reads through the other. On Windows 11 a rejected peer that stayed connected then kept its slot until the idle timeout (10 minutes by default). The timeout is now set on the handle that reads.
- The pipelined test connected 12 peers through 2 slots, and a slot comes back only after the thread serving the previous peer ends. Each peer now has a slot of its own.
- The queue test used a 50 ms sleep to order two requests from two connections. It now checks that one reply is `busy: too many queued requests` and the other `timeout`, each with its own id, in either order.

title: Add an Android app shell
author: tzhazuma
body:
This adds `apps/deckcraft-android`: a Gradle project that hosts the existing egui UI inside an `android-activity` window, plus the platform seams the desktop shell normally supplies.

The engine, the ribbon, the theme and the command table are untouched — the same `deckcraft_engine::Session` and `deckcraft_ui_egui::SlideApp` the desktop shell builds are wired up here, so the phone runs the desktop code paths. `apps/deckcraft` is not compiled, so `rfd`, `arboard` and the platform menus never enter the graph.

## What the shell does

- **Entry point** — the Rust crate builds as `libmain.so` and is loaded with `System.loadLibrary`; `android_main` is the usual `android-activity` entry.
- **File pickers** — the Storage Access Framework stands in for `rfd`. `pick_open` posts `ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT`, the Activity copies the picked document into `<filesDir>/import/` and the real path comes back over the app's own control channel, so the desktop `app.open` command does the opening. `pick_save` answers with a scratch path in `<filesDir>/export/` and publishes the finished file to the `ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT` destination once its size has been stable for 1.5 s. Six JNI calls in `src/saf.rs`; the JNI surface carries no file contents.
- **Storage** — `dirs` answers nothing on Android, so the data directory is registered explicitly; DeckCraft's `ui.json`/`prefs.json` pair is read at startup and written in `on_exit`.
- **Fonts** — the CJK face in `/system/fonts` is appended to every family once DeckCraft's theme has installed its own (earlier, and the theme's named families would be dropped).
- **Touch** — 40 pt hit targets and wider sliders, applied after the theme's style exists. The layout is not zoomed: it is designed for ≥900 pt wide and a phone gives ~411 pt, so the next step is a touch rework, not a scale factor.

title: Return BadParams for overflowing start in review.spellingChange
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/review.rs:424 (spelling_change)` (no existing issue): review.spellingChange panics with 'attempt to add with overflow' on a huge `start`.

## Cause
review.spellingChange reads `start` as any u64 and computes `start + word.chars().count()` without an overflow check. `start` = u64::MAX panics in debug builds, which the session reports as an Internal error. Release builds wrap silently.

## Fix
The addition now uses `checked_add`. An overflow returns a BadParams error (`bad `start``) instead of panicking. A regression test covers `start` = u64::MAX.

## Verified
- Regression test `cmd::review::spelling_change_range_tests::spelling_change_huge_start_is_bad_params`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib spelling_change_huge`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
I did not add a check of `start` against the paragraph length. A `start` that fits in usize but lies past the paragraph already returns the existing 'the word isn't there' error.

title: Match style as a whole attribute name in HTML paste
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/richclip.rs:230-242 (attr, used by tag_style)` (no existing issue): HTML paste ignores a tag's style attribute when an earlier attribute value contains the text "style".

## Cause
`attr` used the first substring match of "style" in the tag. When an earlier attribute name or value contained it, such as `class="style1"`, the following `=` check failed and the function returned None. The real `style=` attribute was never read.

## Fix
`attr` now looks through all occurrences of the key. It accepts the first one that is preceded by whitespace and followed by `=`, so it matches only a whole attribute name.

## Verified
- Regression test `cmd::richclip::tests::style_attribute_is_found_after_attributes_containing_style`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib style_attribute_is_found`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
I did not turn `attr` into a full attribute parser. An attribute value that itself contains text like ` style=` could still be matched.

title: Reject invalid index in animation remove, move, timing and options
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/animation.rs:232-246 (remove); same pattern in each_target :265 and move_anim :250` (no existing issue): animation.remove with an invalid (negative or non-integer) index removes the selected shape's animations.

## Cause
`animation.remove` and `each_target` (used by `animation.timing` and `animation.options`) read `index` with `usize_param`. That returns `None` for a negative, non-integer or string value, so a bad index was treated as absent and the commands fell back to the selected shapes. `animation.remove` deleted all of their animations, and `timing` and `options` changed them, all while reporting success. `animation.move` also reads `index` with `usize_param`, but it requires the index, so a bad value already failed with a "missing `index`" error, which was misleading.

## Fix
`animation.remove`, `animation.move` and `each_target` now read `index` with `opt_usize_param`, as `slide.delete` does. For remove, timing and options, an absent index still falls back to the selection. A present but invalid index returns a `BadParams` error and changes nothing. A regression test covers -1, 1.5 and "x" for remove, timing, options and move.

## Verified
- Regression test `cmd::animation::tests::invalid_index_is_an_error_not_the_selection`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib invalid_index_is_an_error_not_the_selection`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The `to` parameter of `animation.move` still uses `usize_param`. It is required, so a bad value already produces a missing-parameter error and never falls back to the selection.

title: Edit Points: Shift, Ctrl or Alt while dragging a handle makes the point smooth, straight or corner
author: dotCooCoo
body:
In Edit Points, dragging a point's control handle ignored the modifier keys: the point kept the type it already had. Microsoft's support article describes three modifiers for this drag: "To have the point treated as a smooth point, press Shift while dragging either of the handles attached to the point", Ctrl for a straight point and Alt for a corner point ([Draw or edit a freeform shape](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/draw-or-edit-a-freeform-shape-44d7bb9d-c05c-4e1c-a486-e35fc322299b)).

What changes:

- In `crates/engine/src/tools.rs`, a handle drag with Shift held makes the point smooth: the other handle mirrors the dragged one at the same length.

- With Alt (Option) held, the point becomes a corner: only the dragged handle moves.
- The drag passes that type to `shape.moveHandle`, and the point keeps it for the next drag without a modifier, as after Smooth Point, Straight Point or Corner Point in the right-click menu. Without a modifier the drag works as before.

title: Shapes: Arrow: Notched Right cuts its notch as deep as presetShapeDefinitions give it, parallel to the head

title: PPTX: keep media-bookmark animation sequences on save instead of turning them into clicks (part of #362)
author: zberry
body:
The first point of #362: an interactive sequence started by a media bookmark (`onMediaBookmark`) was imported as a click trigger on the media shape, so saving the deck turned the bookmark effects into click effects.

The model has no bookmark trigger, so the reader now keeps such a sequence verbatim on the slide (`Slide::kept_sequences`): the `p:seq` element and its `p:bldLst` entries, with shape ids mapped to model ids. The writer puts it back with the slide's file shape ids, fresh time-node ids after its own (a `p:tn` reference follows its node), and the build groups (`grpId`) the kept entries use left to them. A sequence that names a shape deleted since opening is left out rather than written with a dangling id.

What this does not do: DeckCraft's slide show does not play bookmark triggers and the Animation Pane does not list them; `docs/animation-parity.md` says so. The other points of #362 (a pause shortcut in the show, pen colours) are not touched.

The `showMediaCtrls` round trip that was in this PR is now #1474.

Tested with a synthetic file (a saved click trigger rewritten to `onMediaBookmark`): it is kept, written back with both conditions and its build entry, has unique time-node ids, survives a second save, and is dropped once its trigger shape is deleted. I have not tried a deck saved by PowerPoint with real bookmarks.

title: file.export {format: "frames"}: the slide show as a PNG frame sequence for a video encoder (toward #889)
author: zberry
body:
PowerPoint's Export to Video plays builds and transitions with their timings; DeckCraft had only the one-frame-per-slide GIF. This adds a frame-sequence export that a video encoder (ffmpeg, a browser) can turn into a video, plus one small export fix found by the same agent runs. It is a step toward #889 (video export): the frames carry the show's timing, so an encoder can lay recorded audio under them; it adds no encoder of its own and does not overlap the MP4/MOV series (#608, #616, #622, #628, #629), which could consume these frames.

- `file.export {format: "frames", path: folder, fps, secondsPerStep, secondsPerSlide, transitions, width}` writes `frame-000001.png`… at a constant fps: every build step of each slide plays through its timeline (the show's own `deckcraft_anim::state_for`), settles and holds `secondsPerStep` (automatic steps run on), the last step holds `secondsPerSlide`, and each slide's transition plays frame by frame from the previous slide with the show's composition (Morph shape by shape). A slide's pre-click state is held, and the export pauses before a click step that follows an automatic first step, as the show does. Hostile parameters are bounded and the frame and pixel totals are capped before anything is drawn; identical consecutive frames are encoded once; the answer maps frame numbers back to slides. The MCP `export` tool, CLI help, docs and the slide-show parity notes carry the new format.
- The per-shape show state (`state_for`) moves from the UI crate into `deckcraft-anim`, so the engine can play the show headlessly; the UI converts its result.
- `file.export` to an outline leaves footer, date and slide-number placeholders out, as PowerPoint's outline view shows title and body only.

No new dependencies. Tests cover step counts, holds and transitions, hidden slides, folder creation, parameter bounds and the MCP tool.

title: SmartArt: uniform text size, Font Color, no Flip; text and paragraph formatters take ids (part of #298)
author: zberry
body:
Fixes to SmartArt editing and to the text formatters, found by agent runs building diagrams through the MCP server (#298: the CLI, MCP and control channel answer agents).

SmartArt (matching PowerPoint):
- Node text is sized alike: one automatic scale (the tightest shape's) applies to every node, and `smartArt.fontSize {size}` (or `format.size` with the graphic selected) sets one size for all.
- Font Color with a SmartArt graphic selected colours all its nodes' text (kept across regeneration); before it answered ok and changed nothing. `shape.fill` on a picture is refused with a pointer to `picture.recolor` instead of answering ok and drawing nothing.
- Flip is refused on a SmartArt graphic (PowerPoint greys Flip out; Right to Left is the way to mirror) instead of turning it into a plain group that `smartArt.*` then refused.
- `smartArt.colors`, `layout` and `style` answer the regenerated graphic's `{id, ids}`, as `insert.smartArt` does.

title: Edit Points: Esc before releasing the mouse button cancels a point or handle drag
author: dotCooCoo
body:
In Edit Points, pressing Esc while dragging a point or one of its handles left Edit Points, but the drag went on: the point kept following the pointer, and the release added an "Edit Points" undo step. Microsoft's support article says: "To cancel the change to the point and line segments, press Esc before releasing the mouse button." ([Draw or edit a freeform shape](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/draw-or-edit-a-freeform-shape-44d7bb9d-c05c-4e1c-a486-e35fc322299b))

What changes:

- `Session::cancel_point_drag` in `crates/engine/src/tools.rs` ends a vertex or handle drag and puts back the document and selection from the press. It adds no undo step.
- In `crates/engine/src/keys.rs`, Esc calls it first, and the rest of the drag and the release change nothing. The support article does not say whether Edit Points stays on; in DeckCraft it stays on after a cancelled drag, and Esc without a drag still leaves Edit Points.

Test: `tests::edit_points_escape_cancels_a_point_or_handle_drag` drags a point of an ellipse, presses Esc, drags further and releases, then drags one of the point's handles, presses Esc and releases. After each, it checks that the shape's geometry matches the geometry before the press, that the undo stack has the same length, and that Edit Points is still on. It fails on `main` at the first check after Esc ("Esc puts the point back"). With the line that ends the drag removed, it fails at the check that no drag is in progress.

Checks: `cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib edit_points` (10 tests), `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p deckcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask assets` and `cargo xtask layers`.

title: Treat curly apostrophe as ASCII in spell check
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/spell.rs:693 (paragraph_words) and :353 (Dictionary::check)` (no existing issue): Spell check flags every word with a curly apostrophe (don’t, can’t) as misspelt.

## Cause
The word splitter keeps U+2019 inside words, and Dictionary::check looked the word up unchanged. Hunspell dictionaries list contractions with an ASCII apostrophe, so words like "don’t" were reported as misspelt.

## Fix
Dictionary::check now replaces U+2019 with an ASCII apostrophe before the lookup, so "don’t" passes when the dictionary has "don't". A regression test covers both forms.

## Verified
- Regression test `spell::tests::curly_apostrophe_matches_ascii_entry`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib curly_apostrophe_matches_ascii_entry`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
paragraph_words still keeps the curly apostrophe inside words. The dictionary's ICONV handling is unchanged.

author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Copying a slide from the thumbnails now also puts a picture of it on the clipboard, so it pastes into a chat, a browser or Preview's New from Clipboard (macOS for now).

Microsoft's page on sharing a single slide (https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/powerpoint/share-a-single-powerpoint-slide-with-someone-else) has you copy the thumbnail and paste it into an email as a picture, or into Preview with New from Clipboard. Here the slide copy (Ctrl+C, and Copy or Cut from the thumbnail's right-click menu, the ribbon or the Edit menu) writes a PNG of the slide (960×540 for a 16:9 deck, the same render as Export PNG at 1×) together with the text it already wrote, in a single pasteboard write. That text is what keeps Ctrl+V inside DeckCraft pasting the slide and not a picture (#182: with only an image on the clipboard egui-winit drops the paste). The untitled-slide marker is now never read as "no text, take the image". With several slides selected, the picture is the first one in deck order. I couldn't confirm which slide PowerPoint uses in that case, happy to switch. `edit.copy` / `edit.cut` take `{picture: true}` and return `png`. Cut draws the slide before deleting it.

Platforms: only the macOS host writes the picture (`NSPasteboard`, through objc2-app-kit/objc2-foundation 0.3, already in the tree through arboard; the calls need no `unsafe`). arboard writes one kind of data at a time, so it can't put text and image together. Windows, Linux (X11 and Wayland) and the web don't set the new `clipboard_set_image` service, and the slide copy stays plain text there, as before. I haven't tested those platforms, and Linux, where #1309 was reported, still needs its own writer. I'd do that as a follow-up (Wayland wants `copy_multi`, which needs a feature that isn't enabled in the tree today), so this doesn't close the issue.

@chocodev11: for Linux we plan to add it in a follow-up, with a clipboard writer of its own.

title: Show: Ctrl+wheel zooms the slide in and out around the pointer (#1286)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
During a slide show, Ctrl+wheel (Cmd+wheel on a Mac) now zooms the slide in and out around the pointer.

PowerPoint lists Ctrl + mouse scroll as a way to zoom while presenting (Microsoft's "Run a slide show" quick reference, and the PowerPoint Live presenting page: "hold down Ctrl key and scroll with mouse wheel", Esc resets). Its slide show magnifier goes from 200% on a click up to 400%. Here four notches double the zoom, so the wheel passes through the click-zoom's 2× and stops at 4×; the slide point under the pointer stays put, and zooming back out to the whole slide leaves the zoom (Esc still does too). The plain wheel keeps turning pages, and on a Mac the trackpad pinch is still not a show gesture: the zoom is read from Ctrl/Cmd wheel events only, not from egui's `zoom_delta`, which also carries the pinch. (On Windows a precision touchpad sends its pinch as Ctrl+wheel, so there it will zoom too; I haven't tried it.) The zoomed window keeps the slide's proportions (`zoom_uv` works in 0–1 slide space). Left out: panning a zoomed slide by dragging, and Ctrl+wheel over the presenter window (it zooms the audience slide from the audience window only). Four notches per doubling is my choice, happy to switch.

Closes #1286

title: Slide shows play animations and GIFs smoothly, even in the browser
author: nagasakimark
body:
## What this fixes

Animated slides and animated GIFs stuttered badly in slide shows. In the browser build they were close to unusable: a photo slide with a few animated shapes played at **3.5 frames per second**, and a GIF slide froze for about a third of a second every time the GIF changed frame. With this PR, animations and GIFs play at the display's frame rate on desktop and in the browser.

## Why it was slow

1. **The whole slide was redrawn for every animation frame.** DeckCraft draws slides on the CPU. During an animation, each frame re-rasterized every shape on the slide at full screen resolution, then uploaded the result to the GPU as a new 8.3 MB texture (at 1920×1080). An animated GIF did the same thing every time it advanced a frame.
2. **The web build didn't use WebAssembly SIMD.** `vello_cpu` only uses vector instructions on wasm when `simd128` is enabled at compile time. Without it, the browser ran the renderer's slower scalar fallback.

## What changed

**Slides are now composited, the way PowerPoint plays them** (`crates/ui-egui/src/show_layers.rs`). When a slide has animations or animated GIFs, it is split once into layers:

- the background, plus every shape below the first animated one, as one picture
- each shape from the first animated shape to the last on its own picture (a "sprite"), sized to what it draws. By-paragraph text builds get one sprite per animated paragraph. An animated GIF keeps one sprite per frame it has shown.
- every shape above the last animated one, as one picture

After that, each frame only **moves, scales, turns, fades and clips those pictures on the GPU**. Nothing is redrawn and nothing is uploaded.

Details:
- **Exact transforms.** The GPU transforms come from `render::shape_motion`, which uses the same code path the CPU renderer uses to apply animation state.
- **Things moving can't show.** A colour change, or a shape animated inside a group, is redrawn for that one shape only.
- **Sharp at rest.** A shape that comes…

title: Pasted shapes get the next automatic name instead of keeping the original's
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1290.

`edit.paste` gave pasted shapes fresh ids but left their names alone, so every copy of "Rectangle 3" was also called "Rectangle 3", while a new shape is numbered from the slide's shape count (`add_shape`). Now a pasted shape whose name is already used on the destination slide, and ends in a number ("Rectangle 3", also groups and freeforms), takes the first free "<name without number> n", counting from the number of distinct names on the slide and also checking the names given to shapes pasted earlier in the same paste. A shape whose name is free keeps it: Morph pairs shapes across slides by exact name, so renaming copies pasted onto the next slide would make them swap during the transition.

`add_shape` uses the same helper, so a new shape no longer reuses a name left over after a deletion (Rectangle 3, 4, 5, delete 4: the next one was a second "Rectangle 5").

Not changed: names without a trailing number (e.g. "Hero") stay as they are even if they collide, and Duplicate keeps its "... copy" naming, which looks deliberate. I haven't checked how PowerPoint names pasted shapes; I'm going by the issue. Happy to switch the scheme if you'd prefer something else.

author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Units: centimetres can be chosen in Preferences, and the Format pane, the ribbon size boxes, the Slide Size dialog and the ruler use them

PowerPoint has no units option of its own. It uses the system's measurement setting (Region › Measurement system on Windows, Language & Region on macOS), and "the ruler (and dialog boxes that show units of measure)" follow it ([Microsoft support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/powerpoint/change-the-measurement-units-from-inches-to-centimeters)). DeckCraft doesn't read that setting yet, so this PR adds Preferences › Measurement units (Inches / Centimeters) and stores it in `prefs.json` as the existing `geom::Unit`, which nothing used until now. Following the OS setting as the default would be closer to PowerPoint, and I'm happy to switch to that. The Format pane's Size and Position fields, Shape Format › Size on the ribbon, the Slide Size dialog and the ruler (whole centimetres with half-centimetre ticks) show and take the chosen unit. The deck still stores points. The Slide Size dialog now keeps each field's exact size in points next to the two decimals it shows, so OK with an untouched field, a preset or Portrait gives the exact size. Before, the rounded text was read back: 13.33" came out as 959.76 pt (16:9, A4, B4 and B5 drifted the same way in inches). The Size and Position dialog, Tabs and the Paragraph indents still show inches. I'll do those in a follow-up so this one stays small, which is why this PR doesn't close the issue.

title: Format: OK in the Font dialog keeps a preset or system text color
author: dotCooCoo
body:
The Font dialog got a preset text color as its bare name, which dropped the color's transforms, and a system color as its last RGB value, which dropped the system color. Pressing OK sent that value back, so it replaced the run's color: a preset `red` at 50% luminance came back as plain red, and a system color became a fixed RGB color.

What changes:

- `color_command_value` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs` writes `{"preset": name}` and `{"system": name, "last": "#RRGGBB"}`. The color's transforms go in order under `mods`, in the form the model stores them, so repeats such as `[inv, inv]` and the order of transforms are kept. A system color's `last` value or an RGB color that is not opaque is written as `#RRGGBBAA`.
- `color_value` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs` reads `mods` after the keyed transforms, so the keyed form (`{"scheme": "accent2", "lumMod": 75000}`) still works.
- The dialog's Color field (`color_label` in `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`) shows the preset's name or the system color's last value instead of an empty field.

Tests:

- `cmd::format::tests::font_dialog_ok_keeps_the_text_color` opens the Font dialog on runs with a preset color at 50% luminance, a system color at 60% alpha, a preset color with `inv`, a system color whose `last` value is at 50% alpha, and an RGB color at 50% alpha, sends the dialog's `color` back, and checks that each run's color is unchanged. It fails on `main`, where the preset comes back as RGB `ff0000` with no transforms. It also fails when `inv` is left out (the color comes back without it) or when the alpha is left out of `last` (the color comes back opaque). It also covers a preset with `[inv, inv]` and `accent2` with `[lumOff, lumMod]`, which the old object form returned as `[inv]` and `[lumMod, lumOff]`.
- `dialogs::font_dialog_tests::preset_and_system_colors_show_in_the_dialog_and_ok_keeps_them` checks that the Color field shows `red` and `#123456` and that OK keeps the color. With the old `color_label` it fails…

title: Colour names, media ids after a paste, and pressing a table outside its cells (#1344 follow-ups)
author: aiongg
body:
Follow-ups from the review of #1344.

## Fixes

- **Preset and system colour names** (from #1335): `{"preset": name}` and `{"system": name}` colour parameters accepted any name, and the writer saved it as `a:prstClr` / `a:sysClr val`, giving a file that fails schema validation. `deckcraft-color` has the `ST_PresetColorVal` names (including the later-edition aliases such as `darkBlue` and `lightGray`) and the `ST_SystemColorVal` names. Command parameters with an unknown name are rejected. The writer saves an unknown preset as `black` and an unknown system colour as `windowText` (keeping `lastClr`), so text bodies that reach the model by other paths still save valid files. The reader keeps what a file has.
- **Media ids after a paste or Accept Revision** (from #1289; the path predates it): media brought in from another deck keeps its id but did not raise the document's next id, so a picture inserted later could get the same id and draw the pasted picture. Both paths raise the next id past each item they add.
- **Pressing a table outside its cells** (from #1282): with a cell range selected, a press on the table outside its cells (the grab band around it) did nothing, so the table could not be moved until the range was cleared. That press now selects and moves the table like any shape, and ends the range. A click on that band of a selected table keeps the table selected; only a click in a cell puts the caret there.

## Notes in docs/gaps.md

- Copying a text range carries no media, so a picture bullet in copied text is lost; copying a cell range copies tab-separated text, not a table.
- Automatic lists start only while Replace text as you type is on, and Backspace after one puts the typed lead back.

title: Ignore signed \'hh hex escapes in RTF outline import
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/format/src/rtf.rs:226 (rtf_to_outline)` (no existing issue): RTF outline import accepts a '+' sign in \'hh hex escapes and inserts a control character.

## Cause
The RTF reader decoded the two characters after `\'` with `u8::from_str_radix(h, 16)`, which accepts a leading `+`. So `\'+5` became byte 0x05 and a control character was added to the slide text.

## Fix
Before parsing, the reader now checks that both characters after `\'` are ASCII hex digits. Any other pair is ignored like other malformed escapes.

## Verified
- Regression test `rtf::tests::hex_escape_rejects_sign`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-format --lib hex_escape_rejects_sign`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Resolve OPC relationship targets that use backslash separators
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/pptx/src/opc.rs:295-309 (resolve, used by rels_of)` (no existing issue): OPC relationship targets with backslash separators are not resolved.

title: Fix HTML paste panic on bare '&' before multi-byte text
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/richclip.rs:307-308 (decode_text)` (no existing issue): HTML paste panics on a bare '&' followed by multi-byte text.

## Cause
decode_text searches for an entity's closing ';' in `rest[..rest.len().min(32)]`. Byte 32 can fall inside a multi-byte character, so slicing there panics when a bare '&' is followed by non-ASCII text.

## Fix
The search window end is moved back to the nearest char boundary before slicing. A bare '&' is then kept as typed and the following text is pasted normally.

title: Keep auto-advance when transition.timing gets an invalid `after`
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/transition.rs:112-115 (timing)` (no existing issue): transition.timing with an invalid `after` (negative or non-integer) clears the slide's automatic advance time.

## Cause
In `transition.timing`, any non-null `after` went through `as_u64().map(...)`. A value that is not a non-negative integer (-5, 1.5, "abc") gave None, and that None was stored as `advance_after_ms`, so it silently cleared the slide's auto-advance time.

## Fix
`after` now only updates `advance_after_ms` when it parses as a non-negative integer. Invalid values leave the existing setting unchanged. An explicit `null` still clears it. The regression test covers -5, 1.5, "abc" and `null`.

## Verified

- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
Invalid `after` values are ignored, not rejected with an error. This matches how `duration` handles invalid input in the same function. The other numeric parameters are unchanged.

title: Slide show: render the Presenter View's next-slide preview off the UI thread
author: Naseq
body:
## What this fixes

With Presenter View on, every slide change re-rendered the next-slide preview **synchronously and single-threaded on the UI thread**. Turning the page waited for it.

Measured on the sample deck at 1920×1080 (release build, kittest harness, per-frame time after PageDown):

| | first frames after a slide change |
|---|---|
| Presenter View off | 5–36 ms |
| Presenter View on (before) | 35–80 ms |

Refs #964 (that issue already names this preview as a likely cause of the sluggishness).

## Change (`crates/ui-egui/src/show/presenter.rs`, fields in `show.rs`)

- `presenter_window` renders the preview on a `show-next-preview` worker thread, like the existing next-slide prefetch (#240); the frame that asks for it doesn't wait, and it is picked up with `try_recv` on a later frame (repaint requested while it is on its way).
- **One render at a time.** While a render is in flight, page turns start no other; when it finishes, its result is used if still wanted, otherwise the newest preview is requested.

- While a preview is on its way the box stays empty instead of reading "End of slide show".

title: PPTX: parse each tags part once and cap the tags an import copies (#1164)
author: Naseq
body:
Fixes #1164.

## Problem

`read::tags` re-parsed the tags part for every `p:tags` reference and copied every name/value into the model each time. One shape listing a large (well-compressed) tags part 100 times copied it 100 times; across many shapes the import could exhaust memory and abort.

## Change (`crates/pptx/src/read.rs`)

- `Imp::tags_by_part`: each tags part is parsed once per import (`Arc<[(String, String)]>`), by normalized part name.
- References to the same part from one holder count once.
- `Imp::tag_bytes` + `MAX_TAG_BYTES` (64 MiB): the tags copied into the model across the whole import are capped. Each pair costs its text plus `size_of::<(String, String)>()`, so empty pairs count too. Past the cap the rest are dropped, with one `log::warn!` per import (its own `tags_capped` flag).
- `MAX_TAG_BYTES` is re-exported from `crates/pptx/src/lib.rs` for tests.
- Fits with #1283: its budgets bound what the package inflates and parses; this bounds what is copied into the model from it.

Not in this PR: the audit's broader suggestion of a whole-import model byte budget across the other `pkg.xml(` call sites.

## Tests (`crates/pptx/tests/it/tags.rs`)

- `a_tags_part_listed_many_times_is_copied_once_and_capped`: a tags part a quarter of the budget, listed 100× by each of ≥5 shapes: every shape keeps it once, and only four copies fit.
- `empty_tags_count_against_the_budget`: shapes each carrying 10,000 empty pairs reach the cap (fails without the per-pair cost).
- `cargo test -p deckcraft-pptx` passes; clippy clean.

title: Render: skip shapes far larger than any screen instead of aborting (#1165)
author: Naseq
body:
Part of #1165 (the shape-geometry path).

## Problem

Shape geometry was only checked with `is_finite()` before reaching vello. An ellipse at the EMU size limit, group child scales compounding across levels, or custom-geometry guides can give an outline billions of pixels long; vello's flattener sizes a buffer from that on-screen length and the allocation aborts the process, which `catch_unwind` can't catch. Since every repaint, thumbnail and export renders it, such a deck can't be opened.

## Change

- `crates/render/src/geometry.rs`: `drawable(geo, m, w, h)` rejects a shape if any sub-path has a non-finite point (checked before any bounds, since a bounding box or a union with the frame can hide NaN), then measures the outline's **control box** (which always holds the curve, unlike the tight bounding box when finding an extremum overflows) unioned with the frame, under the shape's transform. Over `MAX_DEVICE_EXTENT` (1e7 px, ten thousand screens across) it is rejected.
- `crates/render/src/renderer.rs`: `geometry_shape` calls it before any fill, stroke or effect and skips the shape with a `log::warn!`. Every preset/custom-geometry shape, including group children, goes through this path.

Not in this PR (left open on #1165): import-time clamps on `Xfrm` sizes and group scales, and the metafile text-scale check in `metafile/src/place.rs`.

title: Open presentations larger than 2 GiB
author: mrojas-red
body:
## Problem

Presentations larger than 2 GiB can't be opened: `io::read_file` rejects them with
`file size … exceeds 2 GiB limit`. Decks with embedded video reach that size easily.

Raising only that cap isn't enough, because the readers behind it have their own, smaller limits:

- `pptx::opc`: any single part over 512 MiB is silently skipped (so a large video would be dropped
  from the deck without an error), and the package keeps at most 2 GiB in total.
- `format`: 2 GiB per entry and 4 GiB of media in total for `.deckcraft` files.
- `recovery`: autosave entries over 2 GiB are not read back.

And on save, `format::save` never sets `large_file`, so writing a `.deckcraft` with a media item over
4 GiB fails ("Large file option has not been set"). `pptx::opc` already does this correctly.

## Change

- `io::read_file`: 2 GiB → 16 GiB.
- `pptx::opc`: `MAX_PART` 512 MiB → 8 GiB, `MAX_TOTAL` 2 GiB → 16 GiB (`MAX_INFLATE_WORK` stays
  `2 * MAX_TOTAL`).
- `format`: `MAX_ENTRY` 2 GiB → 8 GiB, `MAX_TOTAL_MEDIA` 4 GiB → 16 GiB.
- `recovery`: `MAX_ENTRY_BYTES` 2 GiB → 16 GiB, so a deck that opens can also be recovered.
- `format::save`: set `large_file` on media and chart parts, with the same threshold `pptx::opc` uses.

These stay limits: they still guard against zip bombs and runaway allocations. They just sit
above what real decks with video need.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo test` for `deckcraft-pptx`,
  `deckcraft-format` and `deckcraft-engine`.
- By hand on macOS (on the 0.11.1 tag): I made a 2.48 GB PPTX (the sample deck saved by
  `deckcraft-cli`, plus a 2.3 GiB stored part). `deckcraft-cli info` and the GUI app opened it, and
  over the control channel `file.info` returned `bytes: 2483065679, slides: 8`. I didn't rerun this
  file on an unpatched build; the 2 GiB cap there is the explicit check in `io::read_file`.

There's no automated regression test, because it would need a multi-gigabyte fixture. Happy to add

title: Insert, draw and turn 3D models (STL, OBJ, FBX, glTF)
author: Elarionus
body:
Adds Insert ▸ 3D Models: STL, OBJ, FBX and glTF binary files can be inserted, are drawn on slides, in the show and in exports, can be turned, and round-trip through PPTX with their pose and a fallback picture.

## What changes

**New crate `crates/mesh`** (standalone, L0, wasm-safe, no new dependencies besides `miniz_oxide`, already in the lock file)
- Readers: STL (binary and ASCII, Z-up turned to Y-up), OBJ with `.mtl` diffuse colours, FBX 6.1–7.7 (binary with zlib arrays, and ASCII: meshes, normals, material slots, model transforms, Z-up files), glTF binary.
- `.glb` writer: every import is stored as `.glb`, the way PowerPoint keeps models. A `.glb` input is kept byte for byte.
- `raster`: a software z-buffer rasterizer (orthographic, double-sided, simple key/fill lighting, 2×2 supersampling) used both for slides and for the PPTX fallback picture.
- Input is treated as hostile: caps on triangles, vertices, array elements and depth; cycle-safe node walks; tests truncate and byte-flip every binary format.

**Model**: `ShapeKind::Model3d` gains `pose: Model3dPose` (the turn as `am3d:rot`, the camera, and the rest of `am3d:model3d` kept for writing back). `#[serde(default)]`, so existing `.deckcraft` files load unchanged.

**Render**: draws models in their pose, fitted inside the frame with their proportions kept. Pictures are cached per media item, size bucket and pose. An unreadable `.glb` falls back to its poster, else a grey box. PDF needed no change because it already renders slides through `render`.

**Engine**
- `insert.model3d`: from a file or base64. An OBJ's `.mtl` files are read only from beside `path`, through the automation read root.
- 3D Model tab commands: `model3d.view` (ten views), `model3d.views`, `model3d.rotate`, `model3d.turn` and `model3d.reset` (optionally resetting the size). Any pose change drops the stale poster.

author: SofiaAFigueredo
body:
Refs #1305

Setting DeckCraft as the default for `.pptx` fails in Finder (Get Info › Change All) with *"You can't change the item … to always open in the selected application … (error code 2)"*, while Open With on a single file works.

title: fix(morph): draw and upload only the changed region of each Morph frame (#1004)
author: SofiaAFigueredo
body:
Refs #1004 (Morph transition laggy). I could not reproduce the lag on my machine (see "What I could not verify"), so this removes the per-frame work that scales with the size of the slide, plus one real inefficiency found on the reporter's deck. It does not claim the issue is fully closed.

## What was slow

1. **Whole frame every frame.** Each Morph frame rasterised the whole slide, converted it to an egui image and uploaded it as a new texture, even when one rounded rectangle was the only thing moving.
2. **Identical groups were drawn twice.** In the attached `morph test.pptx` the `Ink` group is identical on both slides, but its children have different shape ids. `content()` compared those ids, so the group was treated as changed and drawn as two copies cross-fading, every frame.

## What changed

- `anim`: a group's content is compared without its children's ids, so an identical group moves as one shape.
- `anim`: `MorphFrame` now carries each shape's `reach` (where it can draw) and `same_backdrop`; the new `MorphFrame::changed_since(prev)` answers `Nothing`, `Region(rect)` or `Everything`. It is deliberately cautious: text, effects, 3-D, custom geometry, groups that change, outline morphs, a different set of shapes and backdrops that differ all return `Everything` (the old behaviour).
- `render`: `pixel_region` and `render_blend_part` draw one block of a frame.
- `ui-egui`: the show draws that block and uploads it with `set_partial`; a size change starts over with a whole frame. A Morph between slides that use blur-based effects anywhere (`needs_filters`: shadow, glow, soft edge) always draws whole frames, because a block drawn alone cannot blur pixels of a shape outside it.

On the attached deck, a frame now differs in a region of about 8.5% of the slide (it was always 100%), and the group is drawn once instead of twice.

- `anim`: reach for moving, rotated, stroked and callout shapes; every `Everything` case; the group regression.

title: fix(show): start a slide transition's clock after its first frame is rendered (#1385)
author: SofiaAFigueredo
body:
Part of #1385 (transitions not animated during slideshow playback).

## Cause
`Show::apply` stamped the transition with the time of the key press. The new slide is then rendered on the UI thread in the same frame, and for Pan, Reveal, Ferris Wheel and the other transitions that move content over backgrounds, `part_textures` renders four more pictures. On a large or busy screen that takes longer than the transition's duration, so the first frame that drew the transition was already at progress 1 and the next slide appeared at once. The delay and the missing animation are the same render.

## Fix
`Transition::progress` makes the first drawn frame the one that renders the new slide and the pictures (it shows the start of the transition), and starts the clock on the frame after it. The time spent rendering is no longer part of the transition. Hidden-show logic still uses the press time, so a minimized show still advances.

## Not changed
How long the render itself takes. The next slide is already rendered ahead of time (#240), and the first frame of a transition with parts still renders them synchronously. If navigation is still slow on the reporter's machine, that is a separate ticket, as the maintainers asked.

## Tests
- New: `a_slow_first_frame_does_not_use_up_the_transition`.
- `cargo test -p deckcraft-ui-egui show::` passes; clippy and fmt pass.
- Fail on `origin/main` as well, unrelated to this change: `deckcraft-pdf` `unembeddable_font_returns_error_instead_of_a_pdf_missing_text`, three `the_language_dialog_*` tests in `deckcraft-ui-egui`, and `cargo xtask wasm` (the wasm32 target is not installed here). The remaining `cargo xtask ci` steps (layers, assets) pass.

title: fix(windows): keep the shortcut icon after an update (#1114)
author: SofiaAFigueredo
body:
Fixes #1114.

## Cause

The MSI's Start menu shortcut took its icon from the WiX `<Icon>`. Windows Installer caches that file in `%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Installer\{ProductCode}\`. Every update is a major upgrade with a new ProductCode, and the old product's folder is deleted with it. The Start menu shortcut is reinstalled and points at the new folder, but a taskbar pin is a **copy** of the shortcut that the update never touches. The pin keeps pointing at the deleted icon, and Explorer shows its cached icon until the cache is flushed (a reboot, say), which is why the bug looks intermittent.

This is the same defect as storytold/craft-launcher#643, diagnosed there.

## Fix

- `packaging/windows/deckcraft.wxs`: remove `Icon`/`IconIndex` from the shortcut, so it uses the icon embedded in `deckcraft.exe` (`apps/deckcraft/build.rs`, release builds set `DECKCRAFT_REQUIRE_WINRES=1`). The exe's path stays the same across updates. The `<Icon>` stays for `ARPPRODUCTICON` (Apps & features), which isn't affected. The `.deckcraft` ProgId already used the exe's icon.
- `apps/deckcraft/src/main.rs`: new test `windows_shortcuts_use_the_icon_embedded_in_the_exe` fails if a shortcut names an MSI icon again (checked: it fails on the old `.wxs`).
- `ROADMAP.md`: progress log and revision history rows.

## Follow-up for affected users

Pins that already lost their icon won't fix themselves, because an update never touches a pin: unpin and pin again once after installing the fixed version.

## Not verified

`cargo xtask ci`: fmt, pdf-deps, clippy, assets and layers pass. Four tests fail here in code this PR doesn't touch (`deckcraft-pdf` `unembeddable_font_returns_error_instead_of_a_pdf_missing_text` and three `the_language_dialog_marks_*` in `ui-egui`); this machine has no `../craft-fonts` checkout. The doctest and wasm steps didn't run because the CI script stops at the first failure.

title: Animations: Dissolve In and Out show the shape through noise instead of fading
author: leobasilio
body: Dissolve In and Out were played as a plain fade. PowerPoint shows the shape through a fine noise that fills in until the shape is whole, so a dissolving shape looks speckled midway and a fading one looks gray. Seen in a real deck: several shapes on a slide animated with Dissolve In (`presetID 9`, ``) faded in on DeckCraft and dissolved in PowerPoint. Cause: the effect was mapped to opacity along with Fade, Random Bars, Blinds, Checkerboard and Wheel (`st.opacity = e` in `effects.rs`), and the animation state had nothing that can show part of a shape. The state now carries `dissolve`, the share of the shape that shows, and the renderer shows the shape through a mask where noise fixed in slide space is below that share. How PowerPoint's effect behaves, measured on PowerPoint for Mac's video export of a synthetic deck (black shapes on white, 4 s and 0.5 s effects) at 1080p and 4K: - It runs on its nominal time and over the whole duration, but the share is an S: nothing before a tenth of the way and everything by nine tenths. At p = .1 to .9 it is .003 .040 .140 .305 .508 .707 .866 .962 .997, which the Beta(4,4) curve `35p^4 - 84p^5 + 70p^6 - 20p^7` follows to within 0.015. - The noise is a fixed map: every pixel shown in one frame is shown in all later ones. - It is the same blobs at 1080p and 4K, so the pattern sits in slide space, not in device pixels. They are about 1 to 3 pt across, wider than tall. Value noise on a 2.0 x 1.4 pt grid with smooth interpolation reproduces the measured autocorrelation at lags 2 to 5 (within about 0.05; lag 1 is smoothed by the video codec). | Before | After | |---|---| | | | What is not measured: Dissolve Out (it plays the entrance backwards), shapes wit…
