title: Format: Fill offers Slide background fill
author: dotCooCoo
body:
Format Shape ▸ Fill had no Slide background fill option, and `shape.fill` had no parameter for it. The model already had the fill (`Fill::Background`), PPTX read and wrote it as `useBgFill`, and the renderer showed the slide background through such a shape (#274). A shape opened from a file with this fill showed Automatic chosen.

The Fill pane documentation lists "Slide background fill" after Pattern fill: "To use the presentation background as the fill for a shape, line, or character, click this option." It lists no other options for it ([Format Object (Fill pane)](https://web.archive.org/web/20240724010337/https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/format-object-fill-pane-1e3b0937-259b-4c93-a6d1-39da5e59a73b?ui=en-us&rs=en-us&ad=us)).

## What changes

- `shape.fill {background: true}` fills a shape or text box with the slide background, in one undo step. Only a shape or text box (`p:sp`) saves `useBgFill`, so pictures, connectors, tables and charts keep their fill. On a group, the group's shapes and text boxes take this fill and the group's own fill is cleared, unless a picture in the group uses it. When no selected object can take the fill, the command returns an error.
- Format Shape ▸ Fill lists Slide background fill after Pattern fill, except for a picture. A shape with this fill shows it chosen, with no Color button and no Transparency slider, and so does a group whose shapes and text boxes all have it. A group that keeps its fill for a picture shows no editor for that fill.
- `shape.fill {transparency}` leaves a slide background fill as it is.
- ROADMAP gets a Progress log row, and `docs/ui-parity.md` lists the option in the Format Shape row.

## Tests

- `cmd::shape::tests::background_fill_shows_the_slide_background_and_survives_a_save` sets a blue slide background, fills a rectangle with `background: true`, and checks that `slide.colorAt` inside it gives the background's blue, that undo returns the theme's fill, that `transparency` leaves the fill alone,…

title: Format: Line has a Transparency slider for solid lines
author: dotCooCoo
body:
Format Shape ▸ Line had Color, Width and Dash but no Transparency, and `shape.line` had no parameter for it. The renderer and the PPTX writer already handled a line color's alpha.

The Line Color pane documentation lists Transparency under Solid line: "move the Transparency slider or enter a number in the box next to the slider. You can vary the percentage of transparency from 0 (fully opaque, the default) to 100% (fully transparent)." ([Format Object (Line Color pane)](https://web.archive.org/web/20210127073218/https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/format-object-line-color-pane-dba8e3fd-3f90-4bca-843e-80526ae49214?ui=en-us&rs=en-us&ad=us))

## What changes

- `shape.line {transparency}` (0 to 1) sets a solid line's transparency in one undo step. It replaces any alpha the line had, including `alphaMod`, `alphaOff` and an alpha the line inherits. An automatic line becomes a solid line in its effective color, as `shape.fill {transparency}` does for an automatic fill. No line and gradient lines are left as they are.
- A `shape.line` call that changes nothing leaves an automatic line automatic. Before, it left an empty line behind, and the pane showed Solid line chosen.
- Format Shape ▸ Line shows a Transparency slider after Color for a solid or automatic line. It starts at the transparency the line draws with.
- The Format Shape sliders (Fill and Line Transparency, the effect sliders and Text Fill Transparency) drop the value they hold while being changed when an undo or a command run outside the pane changes the document. Before, the slider kept showing the old value, and leaving it wrote that value back over the change.
- Five existing tests counted or clicked the Transparency sliders in the Fill & Line tab. They now count the line's slider too, or click the Fill section's.
- ROADMAP gets a Progress log row, and `docs/ui-parity.md` lists line transparency in the Format Shape row.

title: Find zip entries stored with backslash separators in pptx packages
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/pptx/src/opc.rs:77-82 (Package::open_within), lookup in Package::get via norm at :258` (no existing issue): Zip entries named with backslash separators are never found when a .pptx is opened.

## Cause
Package::open_within keyed parts by `name.to_ascii_lowercase()`, but Package::get looks them up with `norm()`, which also turns `\` into `/`. Entries such as `ppt\slides\slide1.xml` were stored under the backslash name and could never be found.

## Fix
Parts are now keyed with `norm(&name)`, the same function the lookup uses. `norm` also lowercases ASCII, so case-insensitive lookup still works. The regression test `opc::tests::backslash_zip_entry_names_are_found` uses the mixed-case backslash entry `PPT\Slides\Slide1.xml`. It fails without the fix and passes with it.

## Verified
- Regression test `opc::tests::backslash_zip_entry_names_are_found`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-pptx --lib backslash_zip_entry_names_are_found`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
The original entry name is still stored and returned as before. How two entries that normalise to the same key collide is unchanged: the later entry still replaces the earlier one, as it did for case-only collisions. Verify with `cargo test -p deckcraft-pptx --lib backslash_zip_entry_names_are_found`.

title: Format: Line has a Gradient line option

- For a gradient line, the pane shows the gradient editor the Fill section uses (`fillui::gradient_editor`): preset gradients, type, direction, angle, and stops with color, position and transparency. title: Reject invalid slide index in file.export, file.render, slide.colorAt
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:581 (export); same pattern in render :539 and color_at :550` (no existing issue): file.export with an invalid (negative or non-integer) slide index exports the selected slide.

## Cause
file.export, file.render and slide.colorAt read `slide` with `usize_param`, which returns None for a negative or non-integer value. That looked the same as an absent `slide`, so the commands used the selected slide and succeeded.

## Fix
The three call sites now use `opt_usize_param`, so a present but invalid `slide` returns a `slide is not a valid index` error. An absent or null `slide` still falls back to the selection, and the `no slide N` check for too-large indices is unchanged.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::invalid_slide_index_never_falls_back_to_the_selection_in_export_commands`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib invalid_slide_index`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
`usize_param` itself and other callers of it are unchanged.

title: Text: a space after a symbol-font character keeps the run's font
author: pick2510
body:
## What

An arrow typed with a symbol font, as in "→ Only regulations…", is stored as U+F0E0 with `<a:sym typeface="Wingdings"/>`. PowerPoint puts that `a:sym` on the whole run, words included. PowerPoint draws only the symbol code in Wingdings; the space after it is in the run's own font.

DeckCraft kept that space in the arrow's face, because spaces, digits and punctuation stay in the face of the text before them. Wingdings' space is about four times as wide as a text font's, so the words after the arrow started about 20 pt too far right (24 pt text).

## Evidence

- **Synthetic probe.** A text box written by DeckCraft with four 24 pt lines: `a:sym` on a whole "→ Only …" run, `a:sym` on the arrow's run alone, plain text, and the arrow without a space. In PowerPoint for Mac 16.114's PDF export, the first two lines are identical. DeckCraft now draws the same; before, the first line had the wide gap.
- **Real decks.** On a private corpus of 166 real-world decks (3,690 visible slides; not attached) compared with PowerPoint's PDF exports, two slides with such arrows improve (3.6% → 2.5% and 4.7% → 4.2% of pixels differing). 78 slides change slightly, none by more than 0.23 points. The largest is a slide whose lines already wrapped where PowerPoint keeps them on one line. Its "⇒" spaces are now Arial spaces, as in PowerPoint, which moves that existing wrong wrap by a word.

## How

`crates/text/src/lib.rs`: a neutral cluster (space, digit, punctuation) stays in the previous face only if that face isn't a symbol font (`is_symbol_font`: Wingdings, Webdings, Symbol, Marlett). Otherwise it takes the run's font like any other character. Symbol codes themselves still draw in the `a:sym` font.

## Relation to #1049

#1049 (amosarc) makes all ASCII and high-ANSI neutrals take the run's Latin typeface by code range, which would also cover this case. It's broader (CJK runs, glyph advances), and this PR is one condition. If #1049 lands first, this reduces to its test, which pins t…

title: fix(slides): dragging several selected slides moves them all
author: fchinu
body:
## Summary

Dragging one of several selected slides in the thumbnail pane or the Slide Sorter moved only the slide under the pointer. Now the whole selection moves, as PowerPoint does:

- The selected slides land together at the drop point, in the order they were in.
- They stay selected.
- One undo step puts them all back.
- With sections, they join the section they land in.
- Dragging an unselected slide still moves only that slide, and it becomes the selection.
- Dropping a selection where it already is does nothing and adds no undo step.

## Changes

**Engine: `slide.move` takes `ids`** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/slide.rs`)
- New form: `{ids: [slide id], to}`. `to` is counted in the deck without the moved slides. The old `{from?, to}` form is unchanged.
- Ids are checked against the deck while they are parsed. The first unknown id is an error and the deck stays as it was. Repeats fold together, so the work never grows past the deck size, even with a huge or hostile list.
- The section update is now a shared helper, `reassign_sections`. It uses a position map, not a `position()` call per slide.
- The selection becomes the moved slides.

**UI: the drag carries every dragged slide** (`crates/ui-egui/src/thumbs.rs`, `sorter.rs`, `lib.rs`)
- `thumb_drag` is now a `SlideDrag { uid, ids, slot }`. Both views use the same helpers: `start_slide_drag`, `slide_drag_live`, `slides_move_dest` and `drop_slide_drag`.
- A drag started in one presentation never applies in another. This is the same `uid` guard the Sorter's inline rename uses.
- **Fixes a latent bug (already on `main`):** if no view saw a drag's release, the drag stayed live. That happens when a Sorter double-click opens Normal view mid-gesture, and it was reproduced through the control channel. The next unrelated release in the thumbnail pane then moved slides. A drag is now dropped once the primary button is neitherheld nor just released.
- Normal-view thumbnails now carry a `Slide N` accessibility label, like the S…

title: fix(clipboard): paste from other apps again on the desktop
author: fchinu
body:
## Summary

On `main`, text copied in another program doesn't paste into the desktop app with Ctrl+V or Edit ▸ Paste. Copy and paste within DeckCraft still works. This is a regression from the egui 0.37 migration (#1350). The v0.11.1 release predates #1350, so released builds are not affected.

## Cause

In the egui fork that #1350 moved to, eframe's access to the OS clipboard is the opt-in `clipboard` feature (it enables `egui-winit/clipboard` and `egui-winit/clipboard-image`). `apps/deckcraft` turns off eframe's default features and lists its own, and `clipboard` wasn't among them.

Without that feature, egui-winit uses a clipboard simulated inside the process. A Ctrl+V therefore only ever delivers what DeckCraft itself copied. `cargo tree -e features -i egui-winit` on `main` shows no `clipboard` feature enabled.

## Change

- `apps/deckcraft/Cargo.toml`: add `"clipboard"` to the eframe features.
- `Cargo.lock`: adds `smithay-clipboard` and its Wayland dependencies, which egui-winit's clipboard pulls in.

No code changes. The web app (`apps/deckcraft-web`) is untouched.

## Related

- #1407 edits the same eframe feature line (it adds `persistence`). Whichever of the two merges second gets a one-line conflict; keep both features.
- #1372 (slides pasted between DeckCraft windows) depends on the real system clipboard, so it needs this fix to work on `main`.
- #1414 (Windows image paste) is reported on v0.11.1, before this regression, so it's a separate issue (see #763 / #1057).

## Testing

- `cargo build --release --locked -p deckcraft`, `cargo clippy --locked -p deckcraft --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo test -p deckcraft` (44 tests)all pass.
- `cargo tree -e features -i egui-winit` now lists `egui-winit feature "clipboard"`.

title: CLI render: skip hidden slides like PowerPoint's export, and size images by --width
author: galagersharp-code
body:
Closes #1346.

## What changed

**`render --all` skips hidden slides**, like PowerPoint's own export: a deck converted headlessly no longer gets extra images for slides the author hid (`slide.hide`, or PowerPoint's Hide Slide). Each drawn slide keeps its PowerPoint number in the file name (`slide-01.png`, `slide-03.png`), so callers can map images back to slides without keeping a list. An explicit `--slide N` still renders a hidden slide — the caller asked for that one — and `--include-hidden` draws every slide again for callers that want the old behaviour.

**`render` accepts `--width PX`**, which `render-transition` already had: `--width 1920` gives a 1920-pixel-wide image whatever the slide's size is, so a caller that needs 1920 px images no longer has to read the slide size and compute a scale itself. `--scale` and `--width` are two ways to say one size, so giving both is an error.

## Tests

`all_skips_hidden_slides_and_width_sizes_the_image` builds a three-slide deck, hides slide 2, and checks that `--all` writes `slide-01.png` and `slide-03.png` but not `slide-02.png`; that `--include-hidden` and an explicit `--slide 1` both draw the hidden slide; that `--width 960` produces a PNG whose IHDR says 960; and that both sizing flags together, or a `--width` of 0, are refused. `slide_index_tests` covers the filtering directly, including a hidden slide keeping its number and an explicit `--slide` reaching it.

Help text (`deckcraft-cli render --help`) documents both flags. `cargo test -p deckcraft-cli`: 28 passed; clippy clean.

title: feat(clipboard): copy slides and shapes between DeckCraft windows on Windows
author: kinower
body:
## Problem

Copying a slide or shape in one DeckCraft process leaves only its text alternative on the Windows clipboard. On Windows each file opened from Explorer runs in its own process, so pasting into another window cannot recover the slides, shapes or pictures. Copying between document tabs of the same window already works through the in-app clipboard.

## Solution

- Register a `DeckCraft.Clipboard.v1` clipboard format and publish a self-contained, versioned selection alongside the existing Unicode text and HTML alternatives. The payload carries the shapes or slides, embedded media bytes, rich text and, for each slide, the source layout name and type. No temporary files or references to the source process are needed, so paste still works after the source window closes.
- Keyboard paste and ribbon/context-menu paste prefer the native selection when it is present. An unchanged offer keeps the local paste counter, so repeated paste still offsets. Textless objects keep the existing invisible plain-text marker so the window backend still raises paste events. Copy/cut at an empty caret publishes nothing.
- Imported objects go through the existing undoable paste path: media collision handling, shape/animation ID remapping, and the Reuse Slides destination-layout matching (same name, otherwise same type, otherwise the first layout). Pasted slides take the destination theme; source masters are not copied or imported, so repeated paste does not duplicate masters.
- The OS adapter is Windows-only and uses the safe `clipboard-win` API, already a transitive dependency through `arboard`. Other hosts keep their current behaviour. The native payload is capped at 64 MiB (32 MiB of embedded media); malformed or unsupported offers fall back to normal paste. No unsafe code and no new artwork.

## Validation

Windows x64, Rust 1.95.0:

- `cargo test -p deckcraft-engine -p deckcraft-ui-egui --lib clipboard`: 8 passed (engine 5, UI 3). Includes a regression that pastes the same forei…

title: Soak tests: fail on resident memory growth after warm-up
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Closes the memory half of the gap "Soak testing has no memory or timing budgets" in docs/gaps.md.

The engine soak and the UI soak now read the process's resident memory after a quarter of the run (so caches and allocator arenas are warm) and fail if it has grown by more than 256 MiB by the end. The failure message carries the seed.

The reading comes from the `memory-stats` crate (MIT or Apache-2.0), added as a dev-dependency of the engine and ui-egui crates. I used a crate because the repo forbids `unsafe`, which rules out calling the Windows and macOS APIs directly. The crate reads `/proc` on Linux, calls `GetProcessMemoryInfo` on Windows and the Mach task info on macOS, so no page-size guess is needed. Where it cannot read memory the check is skipped. Adding it made cargo re-resolve a few lockfile lines (windows-sys 0.52 and 0.59 to 0.61, getrandom 0.3 to 0.4); I did not choose those.

What CI actually runs: ci.yml runs `cargo xtask ci` on ubuntu-latest only, so only the Linux path is exercised on every push. freebsd.yml and windows-arm64.yml (shared workflows, triggered on release, on a schedule and when their own file changes) build and test on FreeBSD and Windows ARM64, which I could not inspect from this repo; FreeBSD is not covered by the crate's three platforms, and I do not know whether the Windows job runs the soaks. There is no macOS job.

What I ran on Windows 11 (outside CI, GNU toolchain, a copy of this branch's tree): `cargo test -p deckcraft-engine soak_random` and `cargo test -p deckcraft-ui-egui ui_soak_random`, both passed. The reading works there (it is the working set, 143 to 193 MiB). Growth after warm-up was at most 109 MiB for the engine soak (first seed, still warming up) and 28 MiB for the UI soak, so 256 MiB is about 2x the worst case seen. No Windows-specific change was needed.

title: Format: gradient fill has a Brightness slider for the selected stop
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Format Shape ▸ Fill ▸ Gradient fill had no Brightness control for a gradient stop. PowerPoint's gradient stops have Color, Position, Transparency and Brightness; DeckCraft had the first three. The slider is now on the selected stop, in Format Shape and in Format Background (they share the gradient editor).

Brightness is a color transform, not a new field, so no engine command changes: the pane writes the stop color through the existing `shape.fill {gradient}` / `design.background {gradient}` parameters, which already carry `lumMod` and `lumOff`.

## What PowerPoint does (observed)

New temporary presentations driven through COM, saved, the slide XML read, the files deleted, PowerPoint quit:

- +40% brightness on a theme color is `lumMod 60000` + `lumOff 40000`; -40% is `lumMod 60000` alone; 0 writes neither. The same pairs apply to a solid fill's color.
- Reading a stop back gives the same number, and Transparency stays a separate `alpha`.

`with_brightness` / `brightness_of` in `fillui.rs` write and read exactly those pairs, keep `alpha`, replace (not stack) an earlier pair, and clamp to ±100%. A preset gradient's dark stop (`lumMod 60000`) reads as -40%.

## Tests

- `crates/ui-egui/src/gradient_stop_tests.rs`: the values above, the round trip with alpha kept, and a pane test that clicks the Brightness slider on a two-stop gradient and checks only the selected stop changed.

title: Duplicate names the copy like PowerPoint: next automatic name, chosen names kept
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
## What

Duplicate (Ctrl+D) now names the copy the way PowerPoint does. Before, every copy of a named shape became "X copy" ("Rectangle 1 copy", "Hero copy").

- A shape with an automatic name ("Rectangle 1", "TextBox 3", "Group 15") gets the next automatic name for its kind ("Rectangle 5"), the same one a new shape would get. The shapes inside a duplicated group are renamed the same way.
- A name you chose ("Hero") stays as it is on the copy.

Paste already behaves like this (#1334); this brings Duplicate in line with it.

## What PowerPoint does (observed)

PowerPoint 16.0 for Windows (build 20527), driven through COM on new presentations only, then the saved XML read back:

| Before Duplicate | Copy |
| --- | --- |
| `Rectangle 1` (4 shapes on the slide) | `Rectangle 5`, then `Rectangle 6` |
| `TextBox 3` | `TextBox 9` |
| `Oval 2` | `Oval 10` |
| `Hero` (custom), and a copy of that copy | `Hero`, `Hero` |
| a custom name that looks automatic: `Rectangle 99`, `Oval 7` | kept as is |
| a rectangle renamed `Oval 3` | kept as is |
| group `Group 15` with `Rectangle 13`, `Rectangle 14` | `Group 16` with `Rectangle 17`, `Rectangle 18` |
| table, straight connector | `Table 20`, `Straight Connector 22` |

The tests use these values.

## Where DeckCraft still differs

- PowerPoint numbers a new shape as its shape id minus one, and treats a name as automatic only when it is the kind's name plus that number. DeckCraft numbers shapes across the deck, so its ids do not line up with names. Here any "{kind} {number}" counts as automatic (an oval a user renamed "Oval 7" is renamed on Duplicate; PowerPoint keeps it), and the new number is the first free one after the shape count, as for a new shape. After a shape was deleted, PowerPoint's number can be higher than ours (it gave "Oval 4" where we would give "Oval 3").

title: Shrink on overflow uses PowerPoint's font scale and line spacing steps
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
## What

Shrink text on overflow now picks the same steps PowerPoint does, and writes what PowerPoint writes when the text fits.

- The text scale (`fontScale`) falls in 7.5 % steps down to a floor of 25 %, and the line spacing reduction (`lnSpcReduction`) is 10 % or 20 %, in the pairs PowerPoint saves. Before, DeckCraft searched a continuous scale (for example 92.2 % / 6.3 %, 76.2 % / 19.0 %), so a deck saved by DeckCraft showed different text sizes in PowerPoint until the text was edited.
- Text that fits is saved as a bare `<a:normAutofit/>`. Before, it was saved as `fontScale="100000"`.
- `text.set` refits like typing does (it kept the scale of the previous text).

title: Fonts: a variable font's named instances answer to their Windows family names
author: oran-gutierrez-fugon
body:
Fixes text in non-RIBBI weights of an installed family silently drawing in the fallback font.

## The bug

Open a .pptx whose runs name `Montserrat ExtraBold` (or SemiBold / Medium — the Windows-style family names PowerPoint writes for non-RIBBI weights). With the static Montserrat files installed, DeckCraft draws those runs in Inter Regular, and does not report the font as missing. LibreOffice and PowerPoint render the same file correctly.

## Root cause

1. DeckCraft bundles Montserrat as a **variable** font; `make_face` only sets Windows (legacy) names for static faces, so its named instances become faces like ("Montserrat", "ExtraBold") with `legacy = None`.
2. `add_fonts` skips any installed face whose (typographic family, style) is already present, so the user's static `Montserrat-ExtraBold.ttf` — the face that *does* carry the Windows name "Montserrat ExtraBold" — never loads.
3. `find("Montserrat ExtraBold")` then matches neither a family nor a legacy name and falls back to Inter Regular, while `has_family` is still true via the catalog, so no missing-font warning fires.

Inter's SemiBold/Medium are unaffected only because the bundled Inter has no such named instances.

## The fix

Each named instance of a variable font other than Regular, Italic, Bold and Bold Italic now also answers to its Windows family name — `"<family> <weight>"` with a Regular or Italic style — exactly as Windows lists them and documents reference them. Regular and Bold stay reachable only through the family itself.

Includes a regression test (`variable_font_instances_answer_to_their_windows_names`); the full fonts suite passes.

title: Keep whole character after a backslash in RTF outline import
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/format/src/rtf.rs:301-326 (symbol / text, reached via escape)` (no existing issue): RTF outline import drops the rest of a paragraph after a backslash followed by a multi-byte character.

## Cause
In `rtf_to_outline`, `symbol()` advanced the cursor by one byte. For a backslash followed by a multi-byte character, that left the cursor inside the UTF-8 character. The next `text()` run then started at a non-character boundary, `rtf.get(..)` returned None, and the text up to the next special character was silently dropped.

## Fix
`symbol()` now advances past the whole character using the existing boundary-aware `advance()` helper. For a non-ASCII control symbol it also emits that character, so `A\éB` imports as `AéB`.

## Verified
- Regression test `rtf::tests::multibyte_control_symbol_keeps_character_and_following_text`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-format multibyte_control_symbol_keeps_character_and_following_text`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `backstage::tests::start_screen_opens_the_palette_and_preferences`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
Unknown ASCII control symbols are still ignored. I made no other changes to RTF parsing.

title: feat(format-painter): paint text in another box by dragging across it (#1216)
author: fchinu
body:
Closes #1216.
## Summary

With formatting picked up in Format Painter, the first press on another text box (one not being edited) painted the **whole box** and used up a one-shot painter. You could never select text there and paint only that text. Painting a range (#1076) only worked inside the box already being edited.

Now, in any box:
- A drag across its text paints just the dragged text.
- A double-click paints the word; a triple-click paints the paragraph.
- The same works in a table cell.
- A plain click puts the caret there and keeps the painter armed, which is what already happens inside the box being edited (`format_painter_waits_for_a_range_on_a_plain_click`).
- A press on a box's **frame band** paints the box whole, whether or not it is being edited, as does a press on a shape without text.

### Change from #1216's acceptance criteria

#1216 asks that "a confirmed plain click still paints the whole shape". This PR moves whole-box painting to the frame instead.

The reason: with a plain click painting the box, a double-click can only paint a word if the first click's paint is held back until the double-click window has passed. The engine has no timer for that. Using the frame gives one rule for edited and unedited boxes, with no timing involved.

This hasn't been checked against PowerPoint yet. If PowerPoint behaves differently for a plain click on another box's text, only the press rule in `painter_selects_text_at` needs to change.

- **`crates/engine/src/tools/hit.rs`**: new `painter_selects_text_at`. A painter press selects text when the shape has text, isn't a line or group, and the press is inside its frame band, or in a cell of a table.

title: Speed up PDF export by reusing equal slide backdrops
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## Summary

PDF export (`file.export` / `save_bytes(.., "pdf")`, the slowest step in `deckcraft-cli bench`) is 21-39 % faster, depending on how many slides share a background. Exported PDFs are byte-identical to `main`.

## What changed

Each slide is rasterised as a backdrop and a content layer (#845). Profiling with gdb stack sampling showed most of the main thread outside rendering spent on per-pixel work around those rasters:

- compositing the backdrop onto white (~24 % of main-thread samples, not vectorised),
- the writer hashing every backdrop raster to deduplicate it (~12 %),
- the straight-alpha conversion scanning every content pixel (~11 %).

Changes, in `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs`:

- `opaque` (was the pixel loop in `backdrop`): saturating adds, the same formula as before; 16-pixel blocks that are already opaque are skipped.
- `straight`: blocks with no partly transparent pixel are skipped; the per-pixel formula is unchanged.
- `Backdrops`: keeps the most recently used opaque backdrops. When a slide renders a backdrop identical to one already seen (compared byte for byte), the writer is handed the same `Image` again. The writer already stored equal backdrops once; now it also skips hashing and deflating the copies.

title: Fonts: draw MicroType Express embedded fonts
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Embedded fonts that PowerPoint writes (Embedded OpenType with MicroType Express compression, flag 0x4, optionally XOR-obscured with 0x10000000) are now decompressed and used to draw, so text in a deck that embeds a font no longer reflows into a stand-in. Closes the "Embedded MicroType Express font subsets aren't drawn" gap (F10).

No other open PR covers this (checked open PRs for MicroType, MTX and embedded fonts; #1206 isolates embedded fonts per presentation and is unrelated to decompression).

## What
- `crates/fonts/src/mtx.rs`: decoder written from the W3C member submission "MicroType Express (MTX) Format". Adaptive Huffman LZCOMP with the run-length layer, the three CTF streams (tables, glyph push data, instructions), glyph, composite glyph and `cvt ` translation, `loca` rebuilt, and hop-coded push data expanded back to `NPUSHB`/`NPUSHW`.
- `embedded_sfnt` now returns a `Cow` and handles the EOT flags; the engine caller takes ownership.
- `hdmx` and `VDMX` (device metrics for hinted rendering) are left out of the decompressed font. Nothing here reads them.
- Docs: gap removed, parity table and roadmap updated.

## Testing
- Unit tests (made by us, nothing from PowerPoint committed): a test-side MTX writer turns the bundled Ubuntu Light into MTX streams (plain, run-length coded, XOR-obscured), and the decoded font must have identical outlines and glyph programs for every glyph. Also hop codes, 255SHORT/255USHORT forms, `cvt`, other tables surviving, and truncated or corrupted input returning none.
- Real PowerPoint output, run locally only: decks saved by desktop PowerPoint 16 with Verdana (regular, bold, italic) and Georgia embedded decode, and every glyph outline in the subset matches the installed font's outline (198 for Verdana, 173 for Georgia; Georgia's subset has 20 composite glyphs).

title: Spell check: don't check words longer than 100 characters (fixes #1175)
author: ayozetr
body:
Fixes #1175

## Problem
`Dictionary::check` → `check_exact` → `compounded` (`crates/engine/src/spell.rs`) tries every split point of a word looking for compound parts, building a `String` for each head. With a compounding dictionary (German, Dutch, …) a check costs O(n²) in the word's length. `suggest()` is capped at `MAX_SUGGEST_CHARS` (64), but `check()` had no cap.

The audit marked this "needs verification", so I measured it in release with a `COMPOUNDFLAG` dictionary: 2,000 characters took 0.01 s, 4,000 took 0.03 s and 8,000 took 0.11 s. That's quadratic, and a 100,000-character "word" takes about **17.5 s** per check. Spell check runs again on edits, so a deck with such a word freezes.

## Fix
Words longer than `MAX_CHECK_CHARS` (100, as the audit suggests and as Hunspell's word length limit) pass unchecked, so they get no squiggle. The check counts at most 101 characters (`chars().nth(MAX_CHECK_CHARS)`), so it costs nothing for long input. Words up to the limit are checked as before.

## Tests
- `spell::tests::a_word_longer_than_the_check_limit_is_not_checked`, with a small compounding dictionary: a normal compound is still checked, a misspelt word of exactly 100 characters is still reported, and 100,000-character and 101-character words pass unchecked.
- Without the cap the test takes 17.5 s in release on the 100,000-character word and fails, since that word isn't valid.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, pdf-deps and clippy pass. Every test binary passes except two `ui-egui` tests (`the_language_dialog_marks_the_whole_presentation` and `…_with_nothing_selected`), which also fail on `main` here: the "Español (España)" entry isn't found in this environment. doctest, assets, layers and wasm pass when run separately.

title: Fix HTML paste style leaking past closing tags of a, td, mark
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/richclip.rs:121-139 (html_to_body), with tag_kind at :175` (no existing issue): HTML paste: bold, italic or underline from a style attribute on a tag other than span/font/p leaks to all following text.

## Cause
html_to_body keyed the style stack entry by tag_kind(name), which is empty for tags such as <a>, <td> and <mark>. A closing tag only popped the stack when its kind was non-empty, so the bold, italic or underline from the style attribute was never undone and applied to all following text.

## Fix
The stack entry for an element without a known kind is now keyed by its tag name, and a closing tag pops the nearest matching entry by that key. The style now ends at the element's close. The regression test checks that the styled run has the expected property set and that the following run has none.

## Verified
- Regression test `cmd::richclip::tests::style_on_other_tags_ends_at_their_close`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib style_on_other_tags_ends_at_their_close`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `backstage::tests::start_screen_opens_the_palette_and_preferences`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
tag_kind and the existing handling of span, font, p, b, i and u are unchanged. The 64-entry search window and 128-entry stack cap are also unchanged.

title: i18n: interface languages from craft-i18n, English and German (#15)
author: filforce95
body:
DeckCraft's interface can now be shown in English or German. By default it follows the system language. **Preferences › Interface language** offers System language, English and Deutsch, and the `app.language` command does the same for the control channel and MCP. Related to #15.

This is roadmap step 3d from storytold/craft-i18n#48: DeckCraft reads the shared craft-i18n catalogs, wired the same way as WordCraft's pilot (storytold/wordcraft#4072). That is why there is no `i18n/*.tsv` here. The German catalog is `locales/de/deckcraft.tsv` in craft-i18n (companion PR: storytold/craft-i18n#71). Other languages can then come as catalog-only PRs there.

## How it works
- **Lookup:** strings stay English in the code and are looked up when drawn (`tl!`, `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n.rs`). A string without a translation shows in English.
- **Build:** `build.rs` embeds `locales/<lang>/common.tsv` and `deckcraft.tsv` from `CRAFT_I18N_DIR`, at the commit in `craft-i18n.rev`. Without it the build is English only, so CI and every existing build are unchanged. With `CRAFT_I18N_REQUIRED=1` a missing checkout is an error, for releases.
- **Setting:** `language` in `ui.json` is `auto` (follow the system; `DECKCRAFT_LANGUAGE` overrides) or a code. A code this build doesn't offer falls back to `auto`. Cancel in Preferences puts the previous language back.
- **Stays English:** command ids, ribbon tab ids (`view.tab`, `ui.set`), engine labels returned to scripts, the control channel, the CLI and MCP.

## What is translated
- Ribbon tabs and every ribbon button, through the shared widgets (`big_button_ex`, `small_button_named`, `icon_toggle`, `color_split`, `check_item`, `spinner`, `section`, `drop_button`), including accessible names and tooltips.
- The command palette, searchable by the German name, the English name or the id.
- The status bar, notes pane and spelling popup.
- File tab navigation, headings, links and the start page.

title: Make layout/master placeholder formatting reach slides
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1487

## Cause
In Slide Master view, `format_run` and `format_para` only changed the placeholder's existing runs and paragraphs (`ed::format_all`). They never touched the placeholder's `list_style` (`<a:lstStyle>`), and that is the only thing `resolve::level_style` reads from layout and master placeholders. Because slide placeholders (and often the layout placeholder itself) have no runs of their own, formatting changes like font or alignment never showed up on slides.

## Fix
When the selection target is a layout or master and the shape is a placeholder, `format_run` and `format_para` now apply the same change to all nine list-style levels of that placeholder, as well as to its runs and paragraphs. For paragraph changes, a level change (indent/outdent) is ignored because a list-style level can't move.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::master_layout_placeholder_format_inherits`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib master_layout_placeholder_format_inherits`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
Formatting a text range while editing a layout placeholder's prompt text still only changes that text. `master.title_style` / `body_style` are left unchanged, because a master placeholder's own list style already takes precedence over them when slides resolve their formatting.

title: Skip non-integer colour transform values instead of zeroing them
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd.rs:~425 (color_value)` (no existing issue): Colour object with a non-integer transform value gets that transform set to 0, which turns the colour black.

## Cause
`color_value` converts each transform value with `as_i64()` and `i32::try_from`. A string, a float or an out-of-range number gives `None`, and `ColorTransform::from_xml` turns `None` into 0. The result is `LumMod(0)` (black) or `Alpha(0)` (fully transparent), with no error.

## Fix
In `color_value`, a transform that carries a value is now skipped when its value isn't a usable i32. The rest of the colour is kept. Transforms without a value (comp, inv, gray) are unaffected. A regression test covers a string, 75000.0, 0.75 and a number above the i32 range, and checks that a valid integer still works.

## Verified
- Regression test `cmd::tests::a_non_integer_colour_transform_is_skipped_not_zeroed`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib a_non_integer_colour`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `backstage::tests::start_screen_opens_the_palette_and_preferences`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
`ColorTransform::from_xml` still defaults a missing value to 0, because other callers pass it that way. The whole colour is not rejected, so one bad key doesn't fail a load.

title: Grant network access so update checks can reach GitHub
author: dylanmtaylor
body: The DesignCraft/DeckCraft Flatpak reports "Could not check for updates: couldn't reach GitHub (Temporary failure in name resolution)". The cause is that the sandbox has no network permission, so DNS lookups and connections to GitHub fail. title: Honor CARGO_BUILD_TARGET in FreeBSD packaging for aarch64 release builds
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Root cause

`packaging/freebsd/package.sh` assumed a native build:

- The arch came from `uname -m`. The shared release workflow cross-compiles aarch64 inside an x86_64 FreeBSD VM, so `uname -m` reports the host arch and the archive would be mislabelled.
- The binaries were read from `target/release/`, but with `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET` set cargo writes to `target/<triple>/release/`.
- The final `deckcraft-cli --version` smoke run would execute an aarch64 binary on an x86_64 host and fail.

## Change

When `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET` is set:

- cargo gets `--target "$CARGO_BUILD_TARGET"`
- binaries are read from `target/$CARGO_BUILD_TARGET/release/`
- arch is `aarch64` for `aarch64-unknown-freebsd` and `x86_64` otherwise
- the `--version` run is skipped (the binary cannot run on the build host)

When unset, behaviour is unchanged (`uname -m` mapping, `target/release/`, version run). The release workflow is not touched.

## Testing

- `bash -n` and a dry run on Linux with `--skip-build` and placeholder binaries:
  - `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET=aarch64-unknown-freebsd` produces `deckcraft-<ver>-freebsd-aarch64.tar.gz` from `target/aarch64-unknown-freebsd/release/`.
  - unset produces `deckcraft-<ver>-freebsd-x86_64.tar.gz` from `target/release/` (the placeholder `--version` run fails, as expected for a non-executable placeholder).
- FreeBSD CI on this branch via `workflow_dispatch` (run link in the PR comments / test report).

title: render: keep the slide's worker threads when a shape uses a filter effect
author: cleversonpompeu
body:
## The problem

`Renderer::canvas` dropped the whole slide to a single thread as soon as `needs_filters` found one shadow, glow, reflection or soft edge **anywhere** on it, because vello_cpu's multi-threaded dispatcher panics with `unimplemented!("Filter effects are not yet supported in multi-threaded rendering")`. That is still the case in vello_cpu 0.3.0, so this is not something a dependency bump fixes.

One shadowed shape therefore cost the slide every worker thread, however many the machine has.

Measured on a 12-slide deck at 2560x1440 (a 16:9 slide filling a 5120x1440 display), Ryzen 9 9900X:

| slides | 1 thread | 16 threads, before | 16 threads, after |
|---|---|---|---|
| without filters | 45-56 ms | 4-5 ms | 4-5 ms |
| with a shadow | 85-92 ms | **85-92 ms** (no gain at all) | **25 ms** |

## The change

- **Only the shape that needs a filter takes a detour.** It is drawn on its own single-threaded canvas, sized to its box with the effect's spill (`extent::shape_box`), then pasted 1:1 where it stands. Stacking order is preserved for free: the paste happens at that shape's place in the drawing order, into the same canvas.
- **`needs_st_canvas`** keeps the old single-threaded canvas for the one case the detour cannot serve: a fill overlay that blends (`mult`, `screen`, `darken`, `lighten`) mixes with whatever lies *behind* the shape, which a separately drawn patch does not have.
- **`text_has_effects` now looks inside table cells.** Cell runs carry shadows and glows like any other run, and a slide whose only filter lived in a table was already at risk of the panic on a multi-threaded canvas before this change.

## Numbers

719 ms -> 127 ms for the 12 slides (**5.6x**); worst slide 92 ms -> 25 ms. Presenting the same deck in the app: average CPU 15% -> 7%, peak 39% -> 14%.

This is felt during a show because the slide texture's cache key includes the animation state, so a running animation re-rasters the whole slide every frame.

## Fidelity

title: Count histogram values on a bin edge in that bin
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/model/src/chart.rs:1273 (Chart::histogram_bins, bin index computation)` (no existing issue): Histogram puts a value that sits exactly on a bin's upper edge into the next bin, because of float division.

## Cause
`Chart::histogram_bins` stores each bin's edges as `lo + width * (i + 1)`, but works out each value's bin with a separate division, `((x - lo) / width).ceil() - 1`. The two can round differently. For example, 2.1 / 0.3 = 7.000000000000001, so 2.1 was counted in (2.1, 2.4] instead of the (1.8, 2.1] bin whose stored upper edge is exactly 2.1.

## Fix
The division is still used as a first guess for the index. That guess is then moved down or up until the value fits the bin's stored bounds (lo, hi]. The first bin still holds the minimum and the last bin still takes anything above its edge, so the bin labels and the counts now always agree.

## Verified
- Regression test `chart::chartex_tests::histogram_value_on_a_bin_edge_counts_in_that_bin`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-model --lib histogram_value_on_a_bin_edge_counts_in_that_bin`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `backstage::tests::start_screen_opens_the_palette_and_preferences`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
How bin edges and the bin count are computed is unchanged, including the float noise in edges such as 0.09999999999999999. With a fixed bin count, [0, 0.1, 0.3] in 3 bins puts 0.1 in the second bin. That is correct for the stored edges, so it is left as is.
